A check that asserts an absence records it only beside a control that shows the search works at the scope the claim rests on: the same grep, the same route read or the same census, run against a planted instance, finding it. A search that is misspelled, scoped to the wrong tree or refused by a permission answers zero exactly as a clean tree does, and the zero is then a reading of the search rather than of the code. The planted instance and the real search go in the same output, so a reader who was not there can tell which they are looking at.

A negative control counts as biting only when the run's output **names the assertion it broke**. A bare non-zero exit, an empty output or a `FAIL` line with no failing assertion under it is a run to repeat alone, never a control that bit: a run the pod's memory limit reaped produces exactly that, so a failure-expecting control is satisfied by a run that never happened. Every control mutates a scratch tree and never this issue's workspace, which all six roles share and which `jj` snapshots on any command, so a deliberately broken file left in place reaches the branch at the next commit. A control archives the package under test and every package its test files import, then mutates the copy. Where a control's own words require an edit in place, the control is wrong and comes to the architect to be rewritten, with what it proves unchanged.

# How dispatch://TREE-2 is proved

**Who runs what, and where.** This is the owner's rule of 2026-11-16 (dispatch://TREE-5/comment/c0b271c7-fd09-485f-8787-862d45795160). No role runs a whole package or a whole suite of tests in the pod, and the testing step's role repeats no `before_merge` check that CI proves.

- **The implementer iterates on one test at a time.** A check written as `go test ./... -run '^Test…$'` is run as `go test <the one package that holds that test> -run '^Test…$'`, with the same flags and the same reads of its PASS and SKIP lines. `./...` in a run string only finds the package.
- **Whole packages and whole suites run in CI.** One `workflow_dispatch` of `ci.yaml` on the issue's branch runs every Go suite and the full browser lane at that head. No role runs them in the pod, to prove a fix or for any other reason.
- **The implementer records each `before_merge` check with no `ci_check` once, at the head it hands off.** A `before_merge` check that no CI job runs and that takes more than ten minutes, such as a cost check under `-tags basebuild`, runs at that head. The testing step's role runs it again there. It does not where its words, document or plan give it one run at a head. Nor does it where they give its run only to another role, a person or another step.
- **The testing step's role runs again each `before_merge` check that CI does not prove, at that head.** A check whose words, document or plan give it one run at a head, or its run only to another runner, is the exception. It runs the negative control of each check this round changed, which proves that the check can fail. Then it starts Dispatch and drives the workflows this issue changes, through the CLI and the browser as a person and an agent do, with the release before this one running beside this build where the issue changes what two builds share. It records what it saw. A defect it finds there that no check covers is no fail result: the tester reports it to the architect, and the work adds the check that missed it.
- **The tester reads before it runs.** For each check the round changed, it reads the test or driver the check names against the check's words. It says whether the test asserts each thing the check states, and whether the test can fail. That reading found every test finding of dispatch://TREE-3, and no drive of a check found one (dispatch://TREE-5/artifact/retro-model-timeline-md).
- **Each slice is reviewed when it is ready.** The implementer gives each finished slice to a reviewer that has not seen the work, as a subagent, and fixes what it finds before the handoff. One review of dispatch://TREE-3 found four critical defects that four test rounds did not.
- **Work that touches different files runs at the same time.** The implementer splits a round's findings by the files they change and runs the groups as parallel subagents, not in one line.

The checks run in a Legion pod, at this issue's own head, in its own pull request. The pod needs these steps once, in order, from the issue's workspace.

```
cd -- "$LEGION_WORKSPACE" && bun install
(cd packages/contracts && bun run build)
export PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH="$TMPDIR/ms-playwright" DISPATCH_E2E_PG_BIN=/usr/lib/postgresql/18/bin
(cd packages/dispatch && bunx playwright install chromium)
export DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL="$LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN" BASELINE_SHA="${BASELINE_SHA:?set BASELINE_SHA to the value the pull request body names}"


(cd packages/envoy && go build -ldflags "-X main.buildCommit=$(git rev-parse HEAD)" -o "$TMPDIR/bin/envoy-dispatch" ./cmd/dispatch) && export PATH="$TMPDIR/bin:$PATH"
psql "$LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN" -c 'create database infra_1253' -c 'create database infra_1253_upgrade'
export INFRA_1253_DATABASE_URL="${LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN%/*}/infra_1253"
export INFRA_1253_UPGRADE_DATABASE_URL="${LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN%/*}/infra_1253_upgrade"
DATABASE_URL="$INFRA_1253_DATABASE_URL" DISPATCH_E2E_PORT=8777 bun run dispatch:local > "$TMPDIR/dispatch-local.log" 2>&1 &
until grep -q 'Press Ctrl-C to stop' "$TMPDIR/dispatch-local.log"; do kill -0 $! || break; sleep 2; done
```

`$LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN` is the pod's own test Postgres, never the sessions database that `OMP_SESSION_SQL_DSN_FILE` holds. The Go checks read it as `DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL`, which `storetest.Open` reads and which no other variable replaces: without the export every Postgres test skips in silence, and the check's own proof that its test executed then fails. `storetest.Open` gives each test a new database of its own on that server.    Everything that installs or caches goes under `$TMPDIR`, since the container's own disk is small. `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH` puts there the chromium that the browser check `c-view-editor` launches: Playwright reads it when it installs the browser and again when the run's global setup asks where chromium is (`refuseMissingBrowsers` in `packages/dispatch/e2e/global-setup.ts`, through `chromium.executablePath()`), and that setup refuses a run whose browser it does not find. `--project=chromium` needs chromium alone (`neededEngines` in the same file), so the one download serves the check.

No step exports `DATABASE_URL`. At one worker the browser harness takes a `DATABASE_URL` it finds rather than starting a Postgres of its own, and it truncates and seeds that database, so an exported one would empty a database that other runs in the pod use. With no `DATABASE_URL`, the harness of the browser check `c-view-editor` starts a Postgres of its own, under the run's own temporary directory, from the directory `DISPATCH_E2E_PG_BIN` names (`stackPostgres` in `packages/dispatch/e2e/harness-postgres.ts`, which `startPool` in `e2e/harness-pool.ts` calls), as `packages/dispatch/README.md` gives for an issue pod. That directory, `/usr/lib/postgresql/18/bin`, holds `initdb` and `pg_ctl`, and the `vector` extension stands at `/usr/share/postgresql/18/extension/vector.control`. Without that variable the harness starts no Postgres, and its server refuses to start for want of a `DATABASE_URL` (`e2e/run-server.sh`). No other check starts that harness, and `bun run dispatch:local` reads its own `DATABASE_URL` and not that variable (`e2e/local-instance.ts`). This issue has two databases of its own on the pod's test server instead, `infra_1253` and `infra_1253_upgrade`. `INFRA_1253_DATABASE_URL` and `INFRA_1253_UPGRADE_DATABASE_URL` hold their addresses, and no tool reads those names. Each reaches `DATABASE_URL` only as the prefix of a command. What starts a server over either one truncates and reseeds it, so neither is ever the database `$LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN` names.

`infra_1253` is the database of `bun run dispatch:local`, which the last two lines above start on `127.0.0.1:8777`. With `DISPATCH_E2E_PORT` unset the operating system chooses the port, and a run that addresses `127.0.0.1:8777` then finds no server. That command builds and starts this head's server, and it truncates and reseeds its database each time it starts (`packages/dispatch/e2e/local-instance.ts`). It serves the agent bearer `e2e-token` (`packages/dispatch/e2e/run-server.sh`) and seeds the project `CORE` and the person `alice` (`packages/dispatch/e2e/workspace.ts`). It prints `Press Ctrl-C to stop` once it is up, and the last line waits for that. `infra_1253_upgrade` is the database of the drivers that write through the earlier release first, which start their own servers. The build above stamps `main.buildCommit` with this head's commit, as the image build stamps it (`packages/envoy/docker/Dockerfile`), because the conversion's fleet gate compares the commit each live process serves, and an unstamped build serves none. `bun run dispatch:local` builds its own server unstamped (`packages/dispatch/e2e/run-server.sh`), so no driver over `infra_1253` runs the conversion.

Each Go test runs against the pod's test Postgres, which `storetest.Open` reads from `DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL` (`packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/store/storetest/storetest.go`). A bare `go test ./... -run <Test>` cannot stand as the gate. It exits zero when the pattern matches nothing, and `storetest.Open` calls `t.Skip` on every Postgres test when that variable is unset. So each Go check runs `-v -count=1`, writes the run's own log under `$TMPDIR`, and then reads that log. It requires the `--- PASS:` line of the test this check states, and it requires no `--- SKIP` line anywhere. A test that is absent, that carries other words, or that skips therefore fails the check rather than passing it. Each Go check below says that in its own body. A driver can also exit zero with a section it needs skipped, or after it stops early, so each driver run requires the driver's closing `PASS: <driver file> complete` line and fails on any `SKIP` line.

Each driver check runs an acceptance driver this issue adds under `packages/dispatch/e2e/acceptance/`, in the shape the five drivers there already take beside `lib.sh`. Its `run` begins `cd packages/dispatch`, because `e2e/acceptance/<file>.sh` is a path from there, and it sets `DISPATCH_TOKEN=e2e-token` and `PROJECT=CORE`. Eight drivers read the `bun run dispatch:local` server above: `c-reparent-and-state`'s `issue-tree-reparent.sh`, `c-coverage-states`, `c-issue-relations-read`, `c-duplicate-neighbourhood`, `c-conversation-holds-the-discussion`, `c-tree-read-views`, `c-child-placement` and `c-child-view`. Their `run` also sets `DISPATCH_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8777` and `DATABASE_URL=$INFRA_1253_DATABASE_URL`, as `packages/dispatch/README.md` records `DISPATCH_URL`, `DISPATCH_TOKEN` and `PROJECT` for `block-graph.sh`. The other fourteen start their own servers over `infra_1253_upgrade`. Thirteen of them read rows an earlier release wrote, as the next paragraph requires of every check that converts anything. The fourteenth, `c-reparent-and-state`'s `issue-tree-text.sh`, runs the release before beside this head's server, so that this head creates an issue that is not born converted. Each of them starts its own servers, so its `run` sets `DATABASE_URL=$INFRA_1253_UPGRADE_DATABASE_URL` and no `DISPATCH_URL`. A driver that writes as a person sets `DEV_SIGNIN_LOGIN=alice` in its `run`. A person's write is a criterion, a comment or a message that must count as a conversation node, an approval, or a Keep of a decision, because a comment or a message an agent wrote is no conversation node, a criterion is a node a person or, on an issue Legion runs, an architect R28 names writes, and the Keep route takes a person's credential alone (`routes_table.go`, `model.ScopePerson`). Never run `bun` on these scripts, because Bun's shell cannot run them. Each driver sources `e2e/acceptance/lib.sh`, prints one `PASS` or `FAIL` line per assertion, and exits non-zero on the first failure. It ends with `PASS: <driver file> complete <N> sections`, printed only after its last section, and its `run` greps `^PASS: <driver file> complete `, so a driver that stops early cannot pass.

Every check of this issue that converts anything reads rows an earlier release wrote. A check that reads rows an earlier release wrote is a driver over `infra_1253_upgrade`. A Go check seeds a database that `storetest.Open` migrated to this head. It writes through this head's writers, or by SQL where it needs a row in the shape the release before this one stores, and it says which. A Go test that built an earlier commit would need the `basebuild` tag, which no CI job runs, so the half of a check that needs an earlier build is a shell driver of surface `cli`. Replaying content through this branch's own writer would exercise none of the state the old writer left. That is the fault a second reading found in an earlier draft of this document. So those checks build the earlier release first. This child opens after dispatch://TREE-4 merges, as the spec's R6 states and the parent's order fixes, so the commit `BASELINE_SHA` names already carries the deletion of every `decisions.md` and of the `decisions` role, and the earlier release writes three documents for each issue. Each upgrade driver sources `e2e/acceptance/lib-baseline.sh`, which this branch takes as it is from `legion/TREE-1` at `1a5ac4fbefc6`, in a commit of its own. At that commit the library stamps each server it builds with its commit, so the base server registers its own commit in `server_processes`. At that commit the library reads `BASELINE_SHA`, boots a prebuilt server named by `BASELINE_BINARY` in place of a build, and passes the `NAME=value` pairs of `BASELINE_EXTRA_ENV`, one per line, to every server it boots. Its `baseline_start` reads the input `BASELINE_SHA`, takes that commit's tree with `git archive` into a directory of its own under `$TMPDIR`, builds `./cmd/dispatch` from it, and boots that build. It adds no `git worktree` and checks nothing out. `BASELINE_SHA` is the release this child lands after, and it has no default, so the steps above refuse an unset one, naming the variable. While a branch this child builds on is unmerged, `BASELINE_SHA` is a commit that holds every such branch and none of this child's work. The implementer measures it again after each merge of a sibling's head into this branch. For each such branch it runs `git merge-base --all <this head> origin/<branch>`. The value is a commit of which each commit those runs print is an ancestor (`git merge-base --is-ancestor <commit> <value>`). The pull request body names the value, the head it was measured at, and those commands with their output. A run reads the value from the pull request body at the head under test, and never from this document. Where no such commit exists, the body says so, and no upgrade driver runs at that head. The baseline build carries its own commit, stamped as `lib-baseline.sh` stamps it. The driver stops it before any conversion runs, and a process that stops deletes its own `server_processes` row, so the fleet gate never reads it. Its `run` names `infra_1253_upgrade` as `DATABASE_URL`. Upgrade drivers run one at a time, because each empties `infra_1253_upgrade`. Each server a driver starts serves on a port that `scripts/e2e/lib/held-port.py` chooses and holds, as `lib-baseline.sh`'s `baseline_boot` starts it, so no two servers meet on one port. The driver empties that database first, then calls `baseline_start`, which boots that binary against it. `cmd/dispatch`'s `main` calls `database.Migrate`, so `Store.Migrate` installs the schema of that commit. It never uses `infra_1253`, because `bun run dispatch:local` serves that database and has migrated it to this head. `baseline_boot` starts each of its servers with `DISPATCH_AGENT_TOKEN` set to the `DISPATCH_TOKEN` the run gives, which the server requires (`packages/envoy/cmd/dispatch/AGENTS.md`), and with `DISPATCH_DEV_SIGNIN=1` on loopback, which a person's write through `DEV_SIGNIN_LOGIN` needs (`packages/envoy/cmd/dispatch/settings.go`). The driver signs the person `alice` in once through `GET /auth/_dev/signin`. It then creates `PROJECT` there through `POST /api/v1/projects`, with `default_assignee` set to `alice`, because a create by the agent bearer, which acts for no person, must name a person who has signed in (`api/projects.go`). It drives that server's own API to write the fixtures, records what it wrote, and stops it. It then boots this branch's server, the stamped `envoy-dispatch` the preamble puts on `PATH`, over the same database with `baseline_boot`, as the file's own `--selftest` boots it. It boots it with `DISPATCH_TEST_HOOKS=1` and `DISPATCH_TEST_HOLD_ISSUE_ROOM_STEP=1` in `BASELINE_EXTRA_ENV`. That setting holds the conversion step of R6 at boot and on its tick, so this head converts an issue only when the driver runs the command. Production sets neither. The implementer adds the server's reading of `DISPATCH_TEST_HOLD_ISSUE_ROOM_STEP` with R6's conversion step: no server code reads it at this branch's head, and only `e2e/acceptance/lib-tree.sh` sets it. Two boots of this head run without that setting: the automatic case of `c-conversion-scope`, and the deferral pass of `c-room-cutover`. That server applies this branch's migrations over those rows. Before it reads anything, the driver waits for the backfill: it polls every 2 s until `select count(*) from document_block_versions where version is null or store_owed_at is not null`, which counts the null version a process of the release before sets and the mark the backfill of R16 sets, and the item owed counts (`comment_block_state`, `message_block_state` and `ask_block_state` rows whose `owed_at` is not null), and the count of issues that hold no head mark (`select count(*) from issues i where not exists (select 1 from issue_head_marks m where m.issue_key = i.key)`, R8), all read 0 and the boot backfill has logged its end, prints each count with the database's `clock_timestamp()`, and fails after 300 s naming the count that stayed above zero. It waits on that condition and never on a fixed sleep. Every row the conversion then reads was written by the earlier release's writers. A driver runs the conversion as `envoy-dispatch convert-issues --project CORE`, the command R6 names. Before it converts, it waits until the newest `server_build_announcements` row names this head's commit, which this head's server writes once every live process serves that commit. It polls every 2 s and fails after 300 s. Each such check says below which rows it captured before the upgrade and compares against that capture.

The fixture the two tree checks seed is one issue carrying all three documents. Those are a spec of two requirement blocks, a Verification document of two check blocks that serve them, and a plan of one task that serves one of those requirements. The issue has three documents and four views, Spec, Verification, Plan and Decisions, because Decisions is a view over decision nodes and not a document. Beside them the fixture holds a conversation written through the real API, which is a comment of two blocks, a message and an open ask. It also holds a criterion a person wrote under the comment's block, and a requirement under that criterion. It holds a comment whose prose cites a block of the Verification document, and a recorded result on one check. It holds one approval of the spec, given before any node moves. It holds one check that serves three requirements under two criteria, which is the shape this document's own checks take. Each conversation block id comes from that item's own blocks read, never from a guess.

`c-old-versions-render`, `c-migration-size` and `c-shared-id-census` each print every count they take, with the time they take it. No check of this tree reads the deployment's rows, because no pod of it can.

## The checks

:::check{#c-tree-census serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-one-tree dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-queries dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-artifacts-in-tree dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-result-node dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-issue-relations dispatch://TREE-1/spec#b-r-document-tree" surface="api" run="cd packages/dispatch &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; DATABASE_URL=$INFRA_1253_UPGRADE_DATABASE_URL DISPATCH_TOKEN=e2e-token PROJECT=CORE bash e2e/acceptance/issue-tree-graph.sh 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/issue-tree-graph.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^PASS: issue-tree-graph.sh complete ' $TMPDIR/issue-tree-graph.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q '^SKIP' $TMPDIR/issue-tree-graph.log" when="before_merge" negative_control="In refs.IndexBlocks, append the part_of tuple of a moved block and skip the document_blocks.parent_block_id update. The census counts one projection row whose parent differs from its tuple, and the driver exits non-zero with that node id, the parent the row holds and the parent the tuple gives."}
This is the issue's census, and it reads zero differences in both directions for every projection this child writes. The driver writes documents through the API covering the shapes the renderer and the block walk disagree on most easily. Those are headings followed by paragraphs, a nested list, and a list whose last item is empty. They are also a typed block that holds a code block, a table, and a quote that holds a list. It then compares each projection with the store, for every issue in `PROJECT`.

The corpus is not only what this branch wrote. Half of it comes from the earlier release, through the base-commit server this document's preamble states. The driver boots that binary and writes the same shapes through its API. It records the block ids, the parents, the ask identities and the citation targets it created, and stops it. It then boots this branch's server, which migrates those rows forward. The driver then waits until `select count(*) from document_block_versions where version is null or store_owed_at is not null`, which counts both marks of R1, and the item owed counts (`comment_block_state`, `message_block_state` and `ask_block_state` rows whose `owed_at` is not null), and the count of issues that hold no head mark (`select count(*) from issues i where not exists (select 1 from issue_head_marks m where m.issue_key = i.key)`, R8), all read 0. It polls every 2 s, prints each count with the database's `clock_timestamp()`, and fails after 300 s naming the count that stayed above zero. Only then does it take the census. The census runs over both halves, and the driver reports the two halves separately. It reads the census's line `census: versions …` print `tree_mismatch=0` and `tree_mismatch_repaired=0`, since no writer of either release writes a version whose tree does not render as its stored markdown and the driver drops no update (R16). It reads the second because the server's reconciliation repairs a mark on its next quiet tick, after which only `tree_mismatch_repaired` shows it. It fails printing that line otherwise. The driver asserts both halves hold more than zero rows. So a census that reads zero over this branch's rows alone fails here.

The nodes must match. The blocks the server reads back for each document and the block nodes the store holds are equal, id for id. No node is without its row, and no row is without its node. The parents must match. Each node's parent is the node the rendering draws it inside, computed the way `pmdoc.ValidDocument.BlockDescendantIDs` walks it. An authored node is the exception: its parent is its `parent` attribute's target, else its first `serves` target of its own issue, else, for a requirement, the conversation node of its own issue that its `From:` line names first, else the issue. A top-level block of a role document hangs under the issue and never under an artifact; an uploaded document's body hangs under that document's node. The ranks must match. Each node's place among its siblings is the order of its source rows, and two reads of the tree give one order. Siblings compare by rank byte for byte (`collate "C"`). The driver refuses to run, printing a FAIL line, where `select 'a' < 'B'` is false, since such a database cannot tell byte order from its own collation.

It then takes the same two-sided count for five more projections. It takes it for `check_results` against the result nodes and their tuples. It reads each `check_results` row the earlier release wrote, byte for byte as captured before the upgrade, with its check still listing it. It takes it for `issues.parent_key` against the `child_of` tuples and for `issue_links` against the `needs` tuples whose two ends are issues. It takes it for `artifacts` and `artifact_versions` against the artifact, query and document version nodes, and for `node_search`'s node rows against the text values and its document rows against live documents with markdown (R17). It takes it for `components`, `component_depends` and `issue_component_members` against the component nodes and their `part_of`, `depends_on` and `affects` tuples. It prints the count on each side and the symmetric difference for each. It asserts it read more than zero issues, so an empty database cannot pass as equality. It makes no claim about row counts before and after, because a result and an artifact are now nodes and their rows follow the store.
:::

:::check{#c-parent-written serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-one-tree dispatch://TREE-1/spec#b-r-block-parent" surface="cli" run="cd packages/envoy &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; go test ./... -run '^(TestTheIssueTreeHoldsTheParentAndRankOfEveryBlockOfTheVersion|TestTheBlockIndexPassRunTwiceWritesNoDuplicate|TestAFreshPassWritesEachParentInItsInsert|TestTheWasteRemovalsLeaveTheSameRows)$' -count=1 -v 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/parent-written.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestTheIssueTreeHoldsTheParentAndRankOfEveryBlockOfTheVersion ' $TMPDIR/parent-written.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestTheBlockIndexPassRunTwiceWritesNoDuplicate ' $TMPDIR/parent-written.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestAFreshPassWritesEachParentInItsInsert ' $TMPDIR/parent-written.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestTheWasteRemovalsLeaveTheSameRows ' $TMPDIR/parent-written.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q -- '--- SKIP' $TMPDIR/parent-written.log" when="before_merge" negative_control="Write the rank only for the ids IndexBlocks collects as changed, and not in reconcileBlockParents. The moved paragraph keeps its first rank, and the test fails with that block id, the rank it kept and the rank the version gives it. A further control: date the pass's tuples at the version's own time (`versionAt`) again. The tuples of the version the reconciliation indexed late then carry the version row's time, earlier than the pass, and the test fails naming the block and both times. A third control: let the append of a tuple leave the conflict arm off for a tuple of a node that stood before the pass, with no filter on what the pass's node insert returns (graphstore/write.go). The second run of TestTheBlockIndexPassRunTwiceWritesNoDuplicate then fails with the unique violation of graph_tuples_once or graph_tuples_value_once, and the test prints it. A fourth control: put back the update of queueBlockParents (refs/block_nodes.go) for every placed row. TestAFreshPassWritesEachParentInItsInsert fails naming the count of rows it updated."}
The run proves this test executed. `go test` exits zero when its pattern matches nothing, so the command reads the run's own log for the `--- PASS:` line of this test. It also fails on any `--- SKIP` line, which is what `storetest.Open` writes when `DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL` is unset.

A document is indexed at one version, then at a second that moves a paragraph under a different heading and changes no character of it. `refs.IndexBlocks` writes no `document_blocks` row for such a block, because its text sum equals the stored one (`storedBlocks`), and only `reconcileBlockParents` reaches it. The broken state this case fails on is a rank written only where a row is written. The moved paragraph then keeps its old rank. The test reads the `part_of` tuple of the moved block after the second index. That `part_of` tuple and the retraction of the moved block's old one share one time, which is the second pass's own, read once that pass holds the owner lock and the fence. It is no earlier than the second version row's `created_at`, and the two tuples carry that version's writer and event. A request pass and a reconciliation pass each date their tuples that way, and among the tuples one pass writes under one owner lock, a tuple's time is ordered as its sequence is. The test also has the reconciliation index a version some time after its row was written, and reads that pass's tuples at a time later than the version row's `created_at` by at least that wait. It finds the new holder, with a retraction of the old one at the same time. It reads `document_blocks.parent_block_id` for that block and finds the same holder, and reads the rank values of the moved block and of its new siblings.

The move must cost the block nothing else. The test reads the block's `changed_version` and its `document_block_texts` rows and finds the first version's, because the move changed no text. It reads the Keep recorded on that block before the move and finds it standing, and reads the decision mark on it unchanged. It reads the citation of that block resolving to the same words. A build that bumps `changed_version` for a parent write fails here, with the Keep it cleared.

It then proves the backfill. It reads the block back through the issue's tree read, at its place under the criterion, with no second socket opened. It opens the socket for the spec document's own uuid, after that issue converted, and reads the admission to the issue's room. The payload it then writes lands in the issue's tree. It reads the `document_rooms` row for that uuid and finds the issue's tree node as its room. It opens the socket for a document whose issue has not converted and finds that document admitted to itself.

It proves two overlapping views of one issue. It opens two sockets on the issue's room and holds both. One goes through the spec query's old uuid, and one through the Verification query's. It brings both sockets to one state vector. On the first socket it writes one block of the part the second is drawing, and waits until the issue's version count rises by one. Then, on the second socket, it writes one block of the part the first is drawing, from the state vector it held before that first write. Both writes stand afterwards, both views read both, and the issue's version count rose by the writes and no more. The broken state this case fails on is the old one room per artifact. There the second write overwrites the first and one block is gone. The driver asserts both blocks, and prints the one that disappeared when they are not both there.

It proves the three stored tables are untouched by shape. It reads the columns of `doc_updates`, `doc_snapshots` and `doc_checkpoints` out of the catalog of the upgraded database and compares them with the catalog of a database the same migrations build from zero, finding them equal. The comparison is against the migrations as a whole and never against `packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/store/migrations/0001_init.up.sql` alone: `packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/store/migrations/0041_document_update_classes.up.sql` adds `doc_updates.content_changed`, so the catalog holds five columns where 0001 creates four, on main and on every branch of it, and a check written against the first migration reads an untouched table as a defect. It reads the foreign key of each to `artifacts (id)` and finds it in place.

It then proves what the room admits. A schema version change goes through dispatch://TREE-3's schema switch, under that child's R7. Three rooms become one, in one transaction, and no issue is left half converted. The rooms it converts are rooms an earlier release wrote. The driver builds that release the way this document's preamble states and boots it. It edits each of the issue's three documents through that server's sockets. So `doc_updates`, `doc_snapshots` and `doc_checkpoints` hold rows that writer made. It records each room's head state, its row counts and each document's rendered markdown. It stops that server and boots this branch's, which migrates those rows forward, and waits for the backfill as this document's preamble states. The broken state this ordering catches is a conversion that works on rooms its own writer seeded. Such a conversion can lose an update shape the earlier release wrote.

It runs the conversion, `envoy-dispatch convert-issues --project CORE`, and reads the result for that issue. The issue's room holds each of the three documents' content in its own fragment, written in the order R21 states, and the tree's walk shows the spec's blocks first. Each document's text equals the markdown captured before the upgrade, character for character. Its first update was written by the conversion, which the driver reads as the room's version 1.

It proves what the conversion leaves behind. Every `doc_updates`, `doc_snapshots` and `doc_checkpoints` row of the three old rooms is still stored. The driver counts them before the upgrade and after the conversion and finds the two counts equal. The three `document_rooms` rows point at the issue's tree node. The driver then proves the transaction is whole. It creates, in `infra_1253_upgrade`, a trigger on `document_rooms` that raises for the spec artifact id of a second issue the earlier release wrote. It runs the conversion and reads the error naming that trigger. It drops the trigger and finds no `document_rooms` row and no `doc_updates` row keyed by that second issue's tree node.

It proves the reconnecting client. It opens a socket on the spec room and holds it. It runs the conversion. The socket is closed, which `closeRoomOnReplacedHistory` decides. A stale client that reconnects with the old room's kept Yjs document is refused and its socket closed with `4205` (`docs/old_room_document.go`), so no stale update writes the old document into the issue room's fragment; a fresh client that reads the artifact again is admitted to the issue's room and reads the converted tree. No write of the held socket reaches a document after the close.

It proves the fleet gate. It boots the baseline build beside this branch's server, stamped with `BASELINE_SHA`, runs the conversion, and reads the refusal naming that build and that instance. It then stops the baseline server. It runs the conversion. The conversion refuses and prints that build and that instance. It removes the row and stops this branch's server, so no process is live. It inserts a `server_build_announcements` row naming another commit, runs the conversion with no server up, and reads the same refusal. It then inserts a row naming the conversion's own stamped commit, and the conversion runs. It boots this branch's server again. The driver reads that the conversion printed each issue it converted, and that a second run over a converted issue changes nothing. It then proves the birth of an issue while only announcing builds are live, two of them of different commits. The second build is this head built again with `main.buildCommit` set to another commit, and the driver boots it beside the first. It creates an issue, writes its spec, and reads a `document_rooms` row to that issue's room from the first write. It stops the second build. A later run passes over that issue without converting it again. A run with `--dry-run` over the same seeded project prints the same issues, each with its time, and a total. After it, every row of `document_rooms`, `doc_updates` and `graph_tuples` reads as it did before, and the real run that follows converts exactly the issues the dry run named. Last, in a second pass over an emptied `infra_1253_upgrade`, the driver keeps the baseline server of `BASELINE_SHA` live and boots this branch's server beside it, as a roll does. It creates an issue through this branch's server and writes its spec. It reads no `document_rooms` row for that issue, and its spec socket is admitted to the spec's own room, as today. It stops the baseline server, runs the conversion, and reads that issue converted. Last, a deferral, in a third pass over an emptied `infra_1253_upgrade`. The driver takes the lease of the block index's reconciliation tick, `docs.BlockIndexLease`, on a `psql` session of its own that it keeps open, with `select pg_try_advisory_lock(1280266064, hashtext('block-index'))`, as `duty.Exclusive` takes it before each pass (`leaseNamespace`, `0x4C4F4F50`, in `internal/dispatch/duty/exclusive.go`), and as `holdBlockIndexLease` in `cmd/dispatch/memory_harness_test.go` holds it. While it holds that lease, no reconciliation tick runs. A write of 2,000 blocks or fewer still indexes its own blocks in its own request (`deferBlockIndexBlocks`, `docs/reference_excerpts.go`). Through the earlier release the driver writes two issues in flight. The first holds a Verification document of more than 2,000 blocks, which that write leaves to the reconciliation, so that document's `document_block_versions.version` stays null, and the driver reads it null. The second holds documents of a few blocks each. It stops that server and boots this branch's server without `DISPATCH_TEST_HOLD_ISSUE_ROOM_STEP`, and in this pass it does not wait for the backfill as the preamble does, because the owed documents are the case under test. The upgrade marks owed the documents the earlier release stored (R1), and only the reconciliation tick drains them, so while the lease is held both issues owe their block index. While it still holds the lease, it runs `envoy-dispatch convert-issues --project CORE --dry-run` and then `envoy-dispatch convert-issues --project CORE`. Each run prints both issues deferred, each with its reason and a document of that issue that still owes its block index. It accepts any such document of each issue, because the upgrade leaves every document of both issues owed. It reads in the server's log a deferred line of the step for each issue, and it reads both issues `converted: false`. It then gives the lease back and runs no command. It reads `converted: true` for both issues on `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/tree`, every 2 s, and fails after 300 s naming each issue that stayed unconverted. So the step itself converts a deferred issue on a later tick. It reads the conversion's census of each issue at zero.
:::

:::check{#c-reparent-and-state serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-reparent-and-state dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-serves-coverage" surface="api" run="cd packages/dispatch &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; DATABASE_URL=$INFRA_1253_DATABASE_URL DISPATCH_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8777 DISPATCH_TOKEN=e2e-token PROJECT=CORE DEV_SIGNIN_LOGIN=alice bash e2e/acceptance/issue-tree-reparent.sh 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/issue-tree-reparent.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^PASS: issue-tree-reparent.sh complete ' $TMPDIR/issue-tree-reparent.log &amp;&amp; ! First, append the new part_of tuple and leave the old one standing. The driver reads the subtree under both parents and exits non-zero, with the node id and the two parents it hangs under. Second, let the `PATCH` retract the moving node's outbound tuples and append them again with its part_of. The driver reads the second lens's triggered_by tuple retracted and appended again, and exits non-zero naming the lens and that tuple. Third, drop the refusal of a parent that is, or stands under, the node of a document that a removal could take. The move of the first lens's finding directly onto the node of U answers 200, and the driver exits non-zero printing `the move of &lt;finding&gt; under &lt;U's node&gt; answered 200, want 409 PARENT_DOCUMENT_REMOVABLE`. Fourth, read the kind of the moved node alone and not the kinds of its subtree. The move of the fifth lens onto the node of U answers 200, and the driver exits non-zero printing `the move of &lt;fifth lens&gt; under &lt;U's node&gt; answered 200, want 409 PARENT_DOCUMENT_REMOVABLE`. Fifth, read a document only through its row, so that a document node at an address where no row stands counts as no document a removal could take. The move of the requirement under the node of V answers 200, and the driver exits non-zero printing `the move of &lt;requirement&gt; under &lt;V's node&gt; answered 200, want 409 PARENT_DOCUMENT_REMOVABLE`. Sixth, let the route count its issues as `{key}` alone, for its locks and for the second read's test. Move B then waits for no lock and does not retry: it answers 200 and commits while A holds the owner lock, and once A commits, Q stands under L, a lens on U. TestAMoveUnderALensOfAParentIssueWaitsForThatIssuesLock fails in its subtest `criterion` printing `the move of &lt;Q&gt; under &lt;L&gt; did not wait for the owner lock of &lt;K1&gt;, which the move of &lt;L&gt; onto &lt;U&gt; held: it answered 200, and &lt;Q&gt; stands under &lt;L&gt;`. Seventh, resolve the parent through the loader of documents (loadArtifactNodes), which reads the artifacts row, so that the node of V resolves to no node. The move of the requirement under the node of V answers 404 NOT_FOUND, and the driver exits non-zero printing `the move of &lt;requirement&gt; under &lt;V's node&gt; answered 404, want 409 PARENT_DOCUMENT_REMOVABLE`. Eighth, let the route move a constraint under any parent. The move of the constraint under the moved requirement answers 200, and the driver exits non-zero printing `the move of &lt;constraint&gt; under &lt;requirement&gt; answered 200, want 400 INVALID_POINTER`. Ninth, read the rule of a constraint after the rule of a document that a removal could take. The move of the constraint under the node of U answers 409 PARENT_DOCUMENT_REMOVABLE, and the driver exits non-zero printing `the move of &lt;constraint&gt; under &lt;U's node&gt; answered 409, want 400 INVALID_POINTER`. Tenth, let the route move an ask. The move of the ask under the second criterion answers 200, and `envoy-dispatch census --store` then prints `census: store kind=ask_parent difference at &lt;at&gt;: &lt;cause&gt;` for the ask's `part_of`, which no longer names the document that holds its block. The driver exits non-zero printing `the move of &lt;ask&gt; under &lt;criterion&gt; answered 200, want 400 NODE_NOT_MOVABLE` and `the census reads an ask_parent difference after the move of &lt;ask&gt;: &lt;line&gt;`. Eleventh, let the `PATCH` move a comment. The move of the comment under `issue/&lt;child key&gt;` answers 200. The driver exits non-zero printing `the move of &lt;comment&gt; under &lt;issue/child key&gt; answered 200, want 400 NODE_NOT_MOVABLE`. Twelfth, let the route take a parent the walk does not reach. The move of the first decision under the agent's status note then answers 200, and TestThePatchRefusesAParentTheWalkDoesNotReach fails, printing `the move of &lt;decision&gt; under &lt;status note&gt; answered 200, want 409 PARENT_NOT_REACHED`. Thirteenth, let the index pass compute a stored block's `part_of` from its text. The driver reads P3 back under its old parent after the next index pass, prints the block and both parents, and exits non-zero. Fourteenth, let the ranker recompute stored ranks from the text. After the flat move and a separate index pass, the driver reads a changed stored rank and prints the block and both ranks. Fifteenth, take a `PATCH` with no `If-Match`. The driver prints `PATCH with no If-Match answered 200, not 428` and exits non-zero. Sixteenth, let the pass rank a parent's children without reading the ranks the store holds of its other children. The driver prints the inserted paragraph and the stored paragraph holding one rank, and exits non-zero. Seventeenth, skip the re-placement of a removed block's stored children. The driver prints P3, missing from the tree read after P2's deletion, and exits non-zero. Eighteenth, keep a stored block's place against its `parent` attribute. The driver prints the check still under its stored parent after the edit that names another, and exits non-zero. Nineteenth, omit `placement_seq` from the first indent's response. The driver prints `PATCH of &lt;node&gt; answered without placement_seq for the next If-Match` and exits non-zero. Twentieth, remove `expected_count` from the generated DELETE operation. The contract test prints `DELETE /api/v1/issues/{key}/nodes/{id} lacks expected_count` and fails. Twenty-first, keep the old `parent=` attribute in the requirement's Markdown. The driver prints `the new spec version of &lt;key&gt; still names the old parent &lt;node&gt;` and fails. Twenty-second, leave the text unchanged when a check that names no `parent` moves under another requirement. The driver prints `the new version of &lt;key&gt; holds no parent= for &lt;check&gt;, want &lt;requirement&gt;` and exits non-zero. Twenty-third, keep the old `parent=` attribute when a requirement moves under a lens. After the next index pass the driver reads the requirement back under its old criterion, prints the requirement and both parents, and exits non-zero. Twenty-fourth, skip the write of the parent value the store holds of the moved block's version. After the next index pass the driver reads the block with a placement other than `stored`, prints the block, its placement and its `part_of`, and exits non-zero. Twenty-fifth, write the list move through the edit route's ops instead of the direct write of the tree. The driver reads the item still at its old depth in the new version, prints `list item &lt;id&gt; at depth &lt;n&gt;, want &lt;n+1&gt;`, and exits non-zero. Twenty-sixth, on the converted issue, let the drain write its version of the spec query and leave the request on the query node at the version before, with no move of that request (`docs.MoveApprovalAsk` in `docs/approval_ask.go`). The driver prints `the request on &lt;query node&gt; names version &lt;n&gt; after the drain, want &lt;m&gt;` and exits non-zero. Twenty-seventh, in the callout case, write the moved paragraph flat, outside X's content, as under a decision. The driver prints `the new version of &lt;key&gt; holds &lt;paragraph&gt; outside &lt;callout&gt;, want inside it` and exits non-zero. Twenty-eighth, in the decision case, nest the moved paragraph in D's content, as under a callout. The driver prints `the new version of &lt;key&gt; holds &lt;paragraph&gt; inside &lt;decision&gt;, want outside it`, or, where the `PATCH` refuses the nested text, `the move of &lt;paragraph&gt; under &lt;decision&gt; answered 409 ANSWERED_ASK_KEPT, want 200`, and exits non-zero. Twenty-ninth, in `issue-tree-text.sh`, create the issue of the text cases after the release before stops, while this head's server alone is live. The issue is born converted, and the driver prints `the issue &lt;key&gt; of the text cases holds a document_rooms row, want none` and exits non-zero. Thirtieth, in the list paragraph case, write the moved paragraph flat, outside L's content. The driver prints `the new version of &lt;key&gt; holds &lt;paragraph&gt; outside &lt;list item&gt;, want inside it after its first paragraph` and exits non-zero. Thirty-first, in the table case, nest the moved paragraph in the requirement's content. The driver prints `row requirement: the move of &lt;paragraph&gt; wrote version &lt;n&gt; of &lt;document&gt;, want none`, or `row requirement: &lt;requirement&gt; reads token &lt;token&gt;, want &lt;token&gt;`, and exits non-zero. Thirty-second, drop the refusal `409 CONTAINER_WOULD_EMPTY` from the `PATCH`. In the emptied case, the move out of Y or out of Y2 then answers another status, a refusal of the emptied tree by validation (the `block+` content of a `callout`) or a `200` that changes the document. The driver prints `the move of &lt;paragraph&gt; out of &lt;callout&gt; answered &lt;status&gt; &lt;code&gt;, want 409 CONTAINER_WOULD_EMPTY`, or `the move of &lt;paragraph&gt; out of &lt;callout&gt; changed &lt;what&gt;, want no change`, and exits non-zero."}
A subtree moves with one appended tuple, and a dead branch stops counting as open. The driver writes, as `DEV_SIGNIN_LOGIN`, two criteria. Under the first it writes a requirement with two checks under it. It moves the requirement under the second criterion through `PATCH /api/v1/issues/{key}/nodes/{id}` with the body `{parent}` and an `If-Match` naming the node's `placement_seq`, with `{id}` the requirement's store address, percent-encoded as one path segment, then reads the tuples. It finds one appended `part_of` to the new parent, one retraction of the old, and no tuple written for either check. It reads the tree and finds both checks under the moved requirement, in the order they had before. It reads each check's `serves` tuples and finds them as they were, so the move changed the place and left the coverage standing. The driver uses the browser cookie from its dev sign-in for Alice. A person-scoped token is also a person for these routes (R32).

It reads the refusals. A parent inside the moving subtree is refused, and the error states the cycle. A parent in an issue of another tree is refused, which `refs.IssueAncestors` decides. A move whose stated placement revision is older than the node's current one is refused under dispatch://TREE-1/spec#b-r-write-protocol. The driver reads the newer parent still standing. The move keeps the node's words. The cases below check how the new placement affects the Markdown. It then writes, through dispatch://TREE-6's write routes, a lens of kind `pre-mortem` on the first criterion with its `has_kind` tuple, a second lens of kind `pre-mortem` on the second criterion with its `has_kind` tuple and a `triggered_by` tuple to the first lens, and a risk under the first lens with a `prevented_by` tuple to one of the checks. It moves the second lens under the moved requirement through the `PATCH`. It reads one appended `part_of` tuple and one retraction, and the second lens's `has_kind` and `triggered_by` tuples unchanged. It moves the risk under the second lens, which is of kind `pre-mortem`, through the `PATCH`. It reads one appended `part_of` tuple and one retraction, and the risk's `prevented_by` tuples unchanged. It then writes a third lens, of kind `trade-off`, and moves the risk under it through the `PATCH`. The store refuses that move with `400 INVALID_POINTER`, because dispatch://TREE-6's store rule lets a risk sit only under a lens of kind `pre-mortem`, and this route holds no copy of that rule. The risk reads back under the second lens, with no tuple appended and none retracted.

It then proves that a constraint moves only under an issue node (R7). It creates a child issue of the issue through `POST /api/v1/issues`, with the issue as its parent, and writes a constraint under the issue through `POST /api/v1/issues/{key}/constraints`. It moves the constraint under the moved requirement through the `PATCH`. It reads `400 INVALID_POINTER`, naming the constraint, the requirement and its kind, with no tuple appended and none retracted, and the constraint still listed by `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/constraints` of the issue. It moves the constraint under the child issue's node, `issue/<child key>`, and reads `200`, one appended `part_of` tuple and one retraction. It then reads the constraint listed by `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/constraints` of the child issue, and not by that of the issue. Else the driver exits non-zero, printing `the move of <constraint> under <parent> answered <status>, want <status>`, or `the constraint <constraint> is listed under <issue>, want <child key>`.

It then proves that the route moves no ask (R7). It writes an ask block into the issue's spec through `POST /api/v1/artifacts/{id}/edits`, so the ask's row names the spec as the document that holds its block, and the ask's node's `part_of` names the spec's node. It moves the ask, by its address `ask/<uuid>`, under the second criterion through the `PATCH`. It reads `400 NODE_NOT_MOVABLE` naming the ask, with no tuple appended and none retracted, and the ask's current `part_of` still naming the spec's node. It then runs `envoy-dispatch census --store` with the driver's `DATABASE_URL`, and reads no line that starts `census: store kind=ask_parent difference`. It also reads the census's line `census: versions …` print `tree_mismatch=0` and `tree_mismatch_repaired=0`, since no writer of the product writes a version whose tree does not render as its stored markdown and the driver drops no update (R16). It runs the census whatever the move answered. Else the driver exits non-zero, printing `the move of <ask> under <criterion> answered <status>, want 400 NODE_NOT_MOVABLE`, `the census reads an ask_parent difference after the move of <ask>: <line>`, or `the census reads tree_mismatch=<n> tree_mismatch_repaired=<m>, want 0 and 0: <line>`.

The driver tries to move a block under the child issue's node. That `PATCH` answers `400 INVALID_POINTER` naming the block, its requested parent and the child issue. It also checks the `PATCH` refusal for a comment (R7). It writes a comment of the issue through `POST /api/v1/issues/{key}/comments`. It moves the comment, by its address `comment/<uuid>`, under the child issue's node, `issue/<child key>`, through the `PATCH` with `{key}` the issue. It reads `400 NODE_NOT_MOVABLE`, naming the comment and its kind, with no tuple appended and none retracted, because the `PATCH` moves no comment (R7). It then reads `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/tree` of the issue and of the child issue, whatever the move answered, and finds the comment listed under the issue, where it stood. It moves the third lens, of kind `trade-off`, under `issue/<child key>` through the `PATCH` with `{key}` the issue, and reads `200`, one appended `part_of` tuple and one retraction, and the lens listed by `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/tree` of the child issue. Else the driver exits non-zero, printing `the move of <node> under <parent> answered <status>, want <status> <code>`, or `the comment <comment> is listed by the tree of neither <key> nor <child key>`, or `the lens <lens> is not listed by the tree of <child key>`.

It then proves that the route refuses a parent the walk does not reach, and that a version of the decisions query holds the same bytes for every move the route takes (R7, R15). `TestThePatchRefusesAParentTheWalkDoesNotReach` in `internal/dispatch/api`, a Go test the implementer adds, creates through `POST /api/v1/issues` a converted issue whose spec holds a paragraph, an ask and two `decision` blocks. It writes a comment on the issue as an agent's session (`sessionActor` in `api/interactions_test.go`), a status note that R2's test does not pass, and it removes the paragraph from the spec through `POST /api/v1/artifacts/{id}/edits`, so the paragraph's node is `gone` once the block index states that version. The agent also comments on the second decision's text. No person replies. The read returns this comment as context, not as a conversation node. It reads the newest version of the decisions query and its stored bytes. It then moves the first decision's block through `PATCH /api/v1/issues/{key}/nodes/{id}` with the body `{parent}` and an `If-Match` naming the node's `placement_seq` under each of four parents in turn: the agent's comment on the second decision's text, the status note, the status note's first block, whose parent the walk does not reach, and the paragraph's `gone` node. Each move answers `409 PARENT_NOT_REACHED`, naming the parent and the reason, the decision's current `part_of` still names the parent it had, and the decisions query's newest version and its stored bytes are the ones read before. It then moves the first decision under the second decision, a parent the walk reaches. That move is taken, and the version of the decisions query that `DrainOwedQueries` writes for it stores the same bytes as the version before it, byte for byte. Else the test fails, printing `the move of <decision> under <parent> answered <status> <code>, want 409 PARENT_NOT_REACHED`, `the refusal of the move of <decision> under <parent> does not name the parent and its reason: <body>`, `the refused move of <decision> under <parent> changed its part_of to <node>`, `the decisions query of <key> stands at version <n> after a refused move, want <m>`, or `the version of <decisions ref> written for the move of <decision> under <decision> differs from the version before it from byte <n>`.

It then proves that no move puts a node where a removal of a document would leave it `live` behind no row (R7). Through `POST /api/v1/issues/{key}/artifacts` it creates two documents of the issue: U by a title alone with no content, so U holds one empty version, and W with text in its first version. It moves the constraint, which now stands under the child issue's node, under the node of U through the `PATCH` with `{key}` the child issue. It reads `400 INVALID_POINTER`, and not `409 PARENT_DOCUMENT_REMOVABLE`, with no tuple appended and none retracted. It writes, through dispatch://TREE-6's write routes, a fourth lens, of kind `trade-off`, on the first criterion, with one finding under it, and one finding under the first lens. It moves the fourth lens onto the node of U through the `PATCH`. It reads `200`, one appended `part_of` tuple and one retraction, and the lens's `artifact_id` value equal to the id of U's row. It moves the first lens's finding directly onto the node of U, and reads `409 PARENT_DOCUMENT_REMOVABLE` naming the finding and its kind, the node of U and U, with no tuple appended and none retracted. It moves that finding under the fourth lens, and reads `200`. It writes a requirement with nothing under it under the first criterion, and moves it under the fourth lens. It reads `409 PARENT_DOCUMENT_REMOVABLE`, with no tuple appended and none retracted. It moves that requirement under the node of W, which holds writing, and reads `200`. It then writes a comment whose text cites U, which leaves U holding no writing. It moves the requirement under the fourth lens again, and reads the same refusal. Else the driver exits non-zero, printing `the move of <node> under <parent> answered <status>, want <status>`.

It then proves the rule at a depth greater than one. It moves the first lens's finding under the finding that the fourth lens holds, and reads `200`. It moves the requirement from the node of W under the first lens's finding, which now stands two levels under the fourth lens, and reads `409 PARENT_DOCUMENT_REMOVABLE`, with no tuple appended and none retracted. Else the driver exits non-zero, printing the same line.

It then proves that the rule reads the moved node's whole `part_of` subtree. It writes a fifth lens, of kind `trade-off`, on the first criterion, moves the requirement under it, and reads `200`. It moves the fifth lens onto the node of U, and reads `409 PARENT_DOCUMENT_REMOVABLE`. That refusal names the fifth lens and its kind, the node of U and U, says that the moved node's subtree holds a node of a kind that may not stand there, and does not name the requirement. It moves the fifth lens under the fourth lens, and reads the same refusal. Neither refusal appends or retracts a tuple. Else the driver exits non-zero, printing the same line, or `the refusal of the move of <lens> under <parent> reads <message>, want the subtree's node of a kind that may not stand there, unnamed`.

It then proves that a document node whose row has gone counts as a document that a removal could take. It creates a third document of the issue, V, by a title alone. It takes the lease of the block index's reconciliation tick, `docs.BlockIndexLease`, on a `psql` session of its own that it keeps open, as `c-conversion` holds it. So no tick runs, and no sweep of a tick (`graphcensus.StateOrphanedGone`) states the node of V `gone`. It then deletes V's row by SQL in one transaction, as the removal of `main` does (`removeArtifact` in `api/artifact_removal.go` at `origin/main`): the rows of V that `artifactRemovalClears` lists, the rows that `refs.ForgetDocument` deletes, and then V's `artifacts` row. Like that removal, it writes no node and no tuple. The driver reads the node of V `live` and no `artifacts` row at its address. It moves the requirement from the fifth lens under the node of V, and reads `409 PARENT_DOCUMENT_REMOVABLE` naming the requirement and its kind, the node of V and V, and not `404 NOT_FOUND`, with no tuple appended and none retracted. It then releases the lease by closing that session. Else the driver exits non-zero, printing the same line.

`TestAMoveUnderALensOfAParentIssueWaitsForThatIssuesLock`, in `internal/dispatch/api`, proves the lock in its subtest `criterion`. The implementer adds it, and the run reads its `--- PASS:` line and fails on any `--- SKIP` line. The subtest makes a lens L of kind `trade-off`, a document U made by a title alone, and a requirement Q of an issue other than the one L stands under. It holds the owner lock of the issue that L stands under through `lockstep.HoldOwner`, in a transaction A of its own (`lockstep.Hold`'s `Tx`). In A it writes the move of L onto the node of U through the store's write: one `part_of` tuple to the node of U and one retraction of the old one. It then starts move B in the background, Q under L, through `PATCH /api/v1/issues/{key}/nodes/{id}` with the body `{parent}` and an `If-Match` naming the node's `placement_seq`, with `{key}` the issue of Q. It waits, for at most `lockstep.Wait` (30 s), for a backend other than A's whose advisory lock `pg_locks` shows not granted. It reads, through `lockstep.RequireStoppedAt` on that backend, that it waits at the statement that takes an owner's lock (`lockstep.OwnerLockStatement`). It then commits A. B answers `409 PARENT_DOCUMENT_REMOVABLE` naming Q and its kind, L and U, and Q's current `part_of` still names its old parent. Where B answers while A still holds the lock, the test commits A and fails, printing `the move of <Q> under <L> did not wait for the owner lock of <issue>, which the move of <L> onto <U> held: it answered <status>, and <Q> stands under <parent>`. Where B answers another status after A commits, it fails, printing `the move of <Q> under <L> answered <status> after the move of <L> onto <U> committed, want 409 PARENT_DOCUMENT_REMOVABLE`.

In `criterion`, an issue K1 holds a criterion, L stands on that criterion, U is a document of K1, and Q is a requirement of a child issue K2 of K1. A holds the owner lock of K1.

It then seeds a third requirement with no check and one plan node under it, and a sibling requirement with no check. It reads both listed as gaps by `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/coverage`, and the plan node with a position in `?view=plan` of the tree read. It sets the third requirement's node `state` to `overtaken` through dispatch://TREE-6's route `POST /api/v1/issues/{key}/nodes/{id}/state`, with `{id}` read as in the `PATCH`. Coverage then lists no gap for it while its sibling's gap stands, and `?view=plan` gives its plan node no position. It reads `select to_id, at from graph_tuples where from_id = <the requirement's node id> and kind = 'state' order by seq` and finds the earlier value with the time it changed, because the value appends. A node `state` value outside the five that dispatch://TREE-6 closes the set to is refused `400 INVALID_ATTRIBUTE_VALUE`, naming the attribute and the value it refused. That refusal is dispatch://TREE-6's, at the store's attribute write path.

The driver then works the outline's moves on a converted issue through `PATCH` alone, starting with the `If-Match` from the tree read's `placement_seq`. Each successful move answers `200` with `parent`, `after` and `placement_seq`. The driver checks the parent and the preceding sibling, or null when there is none. It chains the indent, outdent and second indent of P3 using each reply's `placement_seq` as a quoted entity tag in the next `If-Match`. It fetches no tree tag between these three moves. It indents a prose block P3 of the room's own fragment under the prose block P2 above it, whose only child is a comment, with `after: null`, and reads P3 first among P2's ranked children. It outdents P3 again, then indents it back. In the room's own fragment it writes a requirement with its paragraph and a callout that holds a paragraph and a list. The read with no view answers each typed block as one node and no node of the blocks its text holds, and the dry run of the delete of each counts 1. After a prose block of the fragment moves under the requirement through `PATCH`, the read answers it under the requirement, and that dry run counts 2. These cases are named `own-text` in the driver. It moves a check up and down among the checks under one requirement, and indents and outdents a criterion, a requirement and a plan task. After each move it reads the node's `part_of`, its place among its siblings, and `placement: stored`. For the paragraph under a paragraph, it also checks that Markdown keeps the paragraph flat. The move writes no text value, `text_parent` or `text_rank` for it. Its text digest, `changed_version` and Keep stay unchanged. A new query version may still record the changed tree placement. It then writes an edit of the room that changes another block's words alone, and reads every place it moved unchanged after that version's index pass. It writes an edit that inserts a paragraph in the text between the two paragraphs whose ranks a stored paragraph stands between, and reads, after the pass, the new paragraph's rank equal to no rank under that parent, and the stored paragraph's rank unchanged. It writes an edit whose text names, in the moved check's `parent` attribute, another requirement, and reads the check under that requirement with the placement `authored`. It deletes P2 in the room's text, and reads P3 back in the tree read, under the block whose text holds it, or under the issue, with the placement `text`. An `after: null` puts the node first in its own rank band. The separate memo case below checks the exception for a spec block. A `PATCH` with no `If-Match` is `428 PRECONDITION_REQUIRED`; one with a stale tag is `412 PRECONDITION_FAILED`; a body with neither `parent` nor `after` is `400 MOVE_INPUT`; an `after` that is no child of the parent, an `after` naming the comment under P2, which holds no rank, and an `after` naming a requirement for a check, which stands in another band, are each `400 INVALID_POINTER` naming `after`; each stores nothing. `GET /api/v1` lists `PATCH` and `DELETE` under `/api/v1/issues/{key}/nodes/{id}`. The driver greps `packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/api/routes_table.go` at the head for the rows under that path and finds exactly `PATCH`, `DELETE`, `findings`, `pointers`, `state` and `settle`; it first runs the same grep over a scratch copy of that file into which it writes a `/move` row, and finds that row, so a grep that matched nothing cannot read as clean. The outline keeps the tree placement even when Markdown renders it flat. This follows the owner's answer in dispatch://TREE-2/comment/a2219523-e7b6-4b0f-884e-98650fd30635 and its interpretation in dispatch://TREE-2/comment/c15f4116-74e2-48c1-a08e-c6e6722074ef. The caller scope rule follows dispatch://TREE-2/comment/6fe69ea5-1afc-437a-9247-c0af3952228a and dispatch://TREE-2/comment/dd478237-1093-48ff-80a4-432128b9a051.

The same lock test adds a case for a comment on the parent's chain. Alice writes a comment in a child issue on the text of a lens in that issue. She then moves the lens under the parent issue through `PATCH`. The comment keeps its issue and its `part_of` to the lens. The test holds the owner lock of the comment's issue, then starts a move of a block from that issue's child under the comment. The move waits for that owner lock, as `lockstep.RequireStoppedAt` shows. It succeeds once the test releases the lock. No request moves the comment itself.

The implementer adds `TestNodePlacementRoutesMatchTheGeneratedContract` in `internal/dispatch/api`. It reads `packages/contracts/schemas/dispatch-openapi.json` and `packages/contracts/src/dispatch-api.generated.ts`. It checks the two operations at `/api/v1/issues/{key}/nodes/{id}`: `PATCH` declares the `parent` and `after` body and returns `parent`, `after` and `placement_seq`. Both declare the `If-Match` header for writes. Only `DELETE` declares `dry_run` and `expected_count`, and its `200` response for the delete and the dry run declares `count`. The `409 DELETE_COUNT_MOVED` response declares `count` for the current number. Both operations declare `403 DOCUMENT_WRITER_NOT_ARCHITECT` and `409 ANSWERED_ASK_KEPT`. The DELETE description also names `409 PARENT_CONTENDED`. The `PATCH` description and the `DELETE` description each also name `409 CONTAINER_WOULD_EMPTY`. The test reports the operation and field or code it cannot find.

The driver seeds a memo and at least one ranked sibling in every band. Under the issue, it moves a spec requirement S with `after: null` and finds S immediately after the memo. It moves a room-fragment paragraph T, a Verification check V and a plan task P with `after: null` under the same issue. Each goes first in its own band and after all siblings of every earlier band. The driver reads the band byte and the order after each move, in the order `RankBandSpec`, `RankBandTree`, `RankBandVerification`, `RankBandPlan`, `RankBandOther` from `refs/block_nodes.go`. For the last band, it moves a block U of an uploaded document under the same parent and reads it from the store, because the skeleton does not open that document's blocks. U stays after every earlier band and precedes the other blocks in its band. In every read of the issue the memo stays first.

Use separate cases for the text rules of R7's `PATCH`, on an issue that has not converted, which the second driver, `issue-tree-text.sh`, runs (below). Each case but the decision case, the table case and the emptied case writes one version of the document that holds the moved block: the spec, or the Verification document in the gained case. In the rewritten case, a requirement whose `parent=` names criterion K1 moves under criterion K2, and the new text names K2. In the gained case, a check that names no `parent`, and stands under its requirement through `serves`, moves under another requirement. The new text gains `parent=` naming that requirement, in a new version of the Verification document, which holds the check, and the spec gains no version. In the dropped case, a requirement whose `parent=` names K1, and which serves K1, moves under a lens of kind `trade-off` on K2. A lens is no target the attribute can name, so the new text holds no `parent` attribute and is flat there. The tree read answers the requirement under the lens. In the list case, a list item moves under the item above it in the same list. The new text nests it one level deeper. The `PATCH` writes the tree of the document directly under the room locks, because the edit route has no op that nests a list item (`MoveBlock` in `pmdoc/blocks.go`). In the order case, a block moves among its siblings, and the new text holds it in its new place. In the callout case, the decision case, the list paragraph case and the table case below, the text nests a moved block only under a container that has no words of its own (R7, new). Open an approval request on the document the move writes before each move. Read the attribute, nesting or order in the head render and in the new stored version. Check the `text_parent` and `text_rank` of the new version, its `artifact.version` event, and the open request now naming the new version. The earlier version still renders its original bytes.

The second driver, `e2e/acceptance/issue-tree-text.sh`, which the implementer adds, runs these text cases over `infra_1253_upgrade`. It starts its own servers, as this document's preamble states for each driver over that database, and its `run` sets `DATABASE_URL=$INFRA_1253_UPGRADE_DATABASE_URL` and no `DISPATCH_URL`. It needs an issue that has not converted, and an issue that this head creates while it alone serves its database is born converted (R5, R6). So the driver empties `infra_1253_upgrade` and calls `baseline_start`, which builds `./cmd/dispatch` at `BASELINE_SHA` and boots it. It signs alice in and creates `PROJECT` on that process, as the preamble states. It then boots this head's server, the stamped `envoy-dispatch` that the preamble puts on `PATH`, beside that process with `baseline_boot`, which gives both processes one dev sign-in key. It waits for the backfill as the preamble states. Each process serves on a port that `scripts/e2e/lib/held-port.py` chooses. The release before writes no block that the cases move, because this child adds the `criterion` type and the `parent` and `serves` attributes of a `requirement` (`pmdoc/schema/blocks.json`).

While both processes are live, the driver creates the issue as alice through this head's `POST /api/v1/issues`, with its spec. `fleetServesIssueRoom` in `api/issue_create.go` answers false, because the process of the release before lists no `issue_room`, so the issue is not born converted. The driver writes no block while the release before is live, and stops that process (`baseline_stop_server`). Right after the release before stops, through this head's `POST /api/v1/issues/{key}/artifacts` it adds the issue's Verification document and its plan with their blocks (since an empty create under a role slug is refused `400 ARTIFACT_ROLE_NAME`). An upload joins an issue's room only where the issue holds one (`documentJoinsIssueRoom` in `api/issue_create.go`, and the upload in `api/artifacts.go`), so each of the three documents still keeps a room of its own. Through this head's server alone it writes every block that the cases move, the decision D of the decision case included, and it makes every move. No step converts the issue after that stop. This head runs with `DISPATCH_TEST_HOOKS=1` and `DISPATCH_TEST_HOLD_ISSUE_ROOM_STEP=1` in `BASELINE_EXTRA_ENV`, as the preamble sets them, and that setting holds R6's step at boot and on its tick. The implementer adds the server's reading of that setting with R6's conversion step: no server code reads it at this branch's head, and only `e2e/acceptance/lib-tree.sh` sets it. Before the first block and after the last move, the driver reads no `document_rooms` row for the issue. Else it prints `the issue <key> of the text cases holds a document_rooms row, want none` and exits non-zero.

In the callout case, alice moves a prose paragraph of the spec under a `callout` X of the spec, with no `after`. X does not open the spec, so it is no memo (R14). A callout has no words of its own, so the new text nests the paragraph in X's content as X's last block. The paragraph's node holds a stored `part_of` naming X (the newest `part_of` tuple of the paragraph's node in `graph_tuples`), and the tree read answers no node for the paragraph (R2, R8). Else the driver prints `the new version of <key> holds <paragraph> outside <callout>, want inside it` and exits non-zero.

In the decision case, the agent (`DISPATCH_TOKEN`) moves a second prose paragraph of the spec under D, a `decision` that alice wrote, with no `after`. Before the move, alice keeps D through `POST /api/v1/artifacts/{id}/blocks/{block_id}/keep`, with the `text_sha256` that `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/decisions` answers for D. The move is taken, because the paragraph is no decision and R32 lets an agent move it. A decision's content is its own words, so the text stays flat: the newest version holds the paragraph outside D's content, D's content holds the blocks it held before. The paragraph's node holds a stored `part_of` naming D (the newest `part_of` tuple of the paragraph's node in `graph_tuples`), and the tree read answers no node for the paragraph (R2, R8). D's `text_sha256` in the decisions read is unchanged, `kept` names alice and `waiting_review` is false. Else the driver prints `the move of <paragraph> under <decision> answered <status> <code>, want 200`, `the new version of <key> holds <paragraph> inside <decision>, want outside it`, or `the decision <D> reads text_sha256 <sum> after the move, want <sum>, waiting_review <bool>`, and exits non-zero.

In the list paragraph case, alice moves a third prose paragraph of the spec under a list item L of the spec that holds one paragraph, with no `after`. A list item has no words of its own, so the new text nests the paragraph in L's content after L's first paragraph, because the content of a `list_item` is a paragraph followed by blocks (`pmdoc/node.go`). The paragraph's node holds a stored `part_of` naming L (the newest `part_of` tuple of the paragraph's node in `graph_tuples`), and the tree read answers no node for the paragraph (R2, R8). This case moves a paragraph and not a list item, so it does not take the path of the list case. Else the driver prints `the new version of <key> holds <paragraph> outside <list item>, want inside it after its first paragraph` and exits non-zero.

The table case holds the text flat under each block whose content is its own words (R7, new). It has one row for each of seven blocks: a `requirement`, a `criterion`, an `ask` block and a `reading` of the spec, a `check` of the Verification document, a `plan_task` of the plan, and a `callout` C that stands inside a `decision` D2 of the spec. In each row, alice moves under the block a prose paragraph of the document that holds the block, with no `after`, so the text could hold the paragraph inside the block. The move is taken. It writes no version of that document, and the document's head render is byte for byte the one read before, so the text stays flat. The paragraph's node holds a stored `part_of` naming the block (the newest `part_of` tuple of the paragraph's node in `graph_tuples`), and the tree read answers no node for the paragraph (R2, R8). The block's `token` in `GET /api/v1/artifacts/{id}/blocks` is the one read before the move. In the row of C, D2's `text_sha256` in `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/decisions` is the one read before too. Else the driver prints `row <type>:` and then `the move of <paragraph> wrote version <n> of <document>, want none`, `<paragraph> holds a stored part_of naming <node>, want <block>`, `the tree read answers <paragraph>, want no node`, `<block> reads token <token>, want <token>` or `<decision> reads text_sha256 <sum>, want <sum>`, and exits non-zero.

The emptied case holds the refusal of a move that would leave a container with no block of its own (R7, new). A `callout` Y at the top level of the spec holds one paragraph. A list item of the spec holds its first paragraph and a `callout` Y2, and Y2 holds one paragraph. A second list item, M, holds its first paragraph and a second paragraph. Alice moves Y's paragraph under the issue through the `PATCH`, with `after` naming a top-level block of the spec that stands before Y, so the paragraph's place in the text is outside Y. She then moves Y2's paragraph under the issue the same way. Each of those two moves answers `409 CONTAINER_WOULD_EMPTY`, naming the callout and its kind. She then moves M's first paragraph under the issue the same way, and that move answers `409 CONTAINER_WOULD_EMPTY`, naming M and its kind, because M would hold no first paragraph of its own.  None of the three moves writes anything: the spec's version count, the store's tuple count and the count of the `doc_updates` rows of the spec's room are the ones the driver read before the moves, and each paragraph's `part_of` names its container still.
