Else the driver prints `the move of <paragraph> out of <container> answered <status> <code>, want 409 CONTAINER_WOULD_EMPTY`, or `the move of <paragraph> out of <container> changed <what>, want no change`, and exits non-zero.

Each moved block keeps the placement `stored` (R7, new). After the version's own index pass, the driver writes an edit of the room that changes another block's words alone, so a later pass runs. After that pass each block that a text case moves reads `placement: stored` and the `part_of` its move wrote. The requirement of the dropped case stays under the lens and does not go back under K1, which its `serves` names.

The request that moves is the one on the version the move writes (R7, R14). On the issue that has not converted, each case above that writes a version reads the request on the document it writes naming that version. On a converted issue of `infra_1253`, `issue-tree-reparent.sh` opens an approval request on the spec query node and moves a requirement under another criterion through the `PATCH`. The drain then writes a version of the spec query, and the request on the query node names that version. The driver prints the request, the version it names and the version it wants.
:::

:::check{#c-node-delete serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-reparent-and-state dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-serves-coverage" surface="api" run="cd packages/envoy &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL=$LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN go test ./internal/dispatch/api/ -run '^TestADeleteTakesTheNodeAndItsSubtreeOutInOneWrite$' -count=1 -v 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/node-delete.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestADeleteTakesTheNodeAndItsSubtreeOutInOneWrite ' $TMPDIR/node-delete.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q -- '--- SKIP' $TMPDIR/node-delete.log" when="before_merge" negative_control="Sixteen controls, run one at a time. First, mark the nodes gone and make no edit of the room. The test reads R1 live again after the next index pass, prints it, and fails. Second, leave the tuples out of the nodes marked gone standing. The test prints C1's `serves` tuple to R2 still standing after C1 goes `gone`. Third, drop the `409 NODE_HOLDS_RESULT` refusal from the route. The test prints `DELETE of &lt;C3&gt; answered 200, not 409` and C3's result's check gone, and fails. Fourth, write the room's edit and the states in two transactions, and fail the second. The test reads the room without R1 and R1's node live, prints both, and fails. Fifth, edit only the room of `{key}`. The test reads Q live again after the child's room's next index pass, prints it, and fails. Sixth, drop the `409 ANSWERED_ASK_KEPT` refusal for a person's decision node. The test prints `agent DELETE of &lt;R6&gt; answered 200, not 409` and names the removed decision. Seventh, skip the orphaning of the comments on what the DELETE takes. The test prints the agent's comment on R1's text with its anchored_in to R1 standing and `orphaned` false, and alice's comment on the lens with its node anchor not orphaned, and fails. Eighth, mark gone the comments of the subtree too. The test prints the agent's comment on R1's text gone, and fails. Ninth, skip the lift-out. The test prints C4 gone with X1's text. Repeat with the take of R4, which takes X4. It prints the lost ask block or the `400 INVALID_ASK_BLOCK` response instead of `200`. Tenth, count every node the DELETE takes. The test prints the dry run's count 9, not 6, and fails. Eleventh, take the DELETE with a stale `expected_count`. The test prints `DELETE of &lt;R2&gt; with a stale expected_count answered 200, not 409` and fails. Twelfth, bypass the refusal checks in the dry run. The test prints `dry run of &lt;C3&gt; answered 200, want 409 NODE_HOLDS_RESULT` and fails. Thirteenth, do not retry after the first under-lock read finds an unlocked owner. The contention case prints `DELETE stopped after attempt 1, want 2` and fails. Fourteenth, write the lift-out and the removal through the edit route's `delete` and `move` ops, one op at a time, as the edit route applies them, in place of one direct write of each document's tree. The move of C4 out of X1 leaves X1 empty, and `MoveBlock` in `pmdoc/blocks.go` refuses that document under the `block+` content of a `callout` (`pmdoc/schema/blocks.json`). The test prints `DELETE of &lt;R1&gt; answered &lt;status&gt; &lt;code&gt;, want 200` with the refusal it read, and fails. Fifteenth, let the node routes find the node that `{id}` names without its kind's visibility rule (`refs/reasoning_nodes.go`). The first agent session's dry run and `DELETE` of the second session's author-only lens then answer `403 STATE_NOT_PERMITTED`, and its `PATCH` of that lens is taken. The test prints `agent DELETE of &lt;hidden lens&gt; answered 403, want 404 NOT_FOUND`, or the same line for the dry run or the `PATCH`, and fails. Sixteenth, drop the `409 CONTAINER_WOULD_EMPTY` rule from the `DELETE` and from its dry run. The dry run of R9 then answers `200` with `{&#x22;count&#x22;: 2}`, and the `DELETE` of R9 answers `200` or a refusal of the emptied tree by validation (the `block+` content of a `callout`). The test prints `dry run of &lt;R9&gt; answered 200, want 409 CONTAINER_WOULD_EMPTY`, or `DELETE of &lt;R9&gt; answered &lt;status&gt; &lt;code&gt;, want 409 CONTAINER_WOULD_EMPTY`, and fails."}
`TestADeleteTakesTheNodeAndItsSubtreeOutInOneWrite` in `internal/dispatch/api` is new. On a test server, a person (alice), in the browser, creates an issue born converted and approves its spec. Its spec holds a criterion K with a requirement R1 under it, and a requirement R2 under the issue. C1 is a check with no result. It hangs under R1 and serves R1 and R2. A check C2 serves R1 and R2, and alice moves it under R2. A requirement holds paragraphs alone (`pmdoc/schema/blocks.json`), so a block that holds C4 is a `callout`, whose content admits blocks. A callout X1 holds one check, C4, which serves R2 alone. The spec opens with K, so X1 is not the memo (R14). Alice moves X1 under R1 through `PATCH`. Alice writes a prose block P in the room's own fragment, where it stands under the issue, and moves it under R1 through `PATCH`. A lens L with a finding F stands on R1; alice comments on L's text by node anchor. A child issue stands under K, and alice moves a prose block Q of the child issue's room under R1 through `PATCH`. A check C3 holds a result. An agent session writes a requirement R4 and a callout X4 that holds two ask blocks, and moves X4 under R4 through `PATCH`. One ask is open. Alice answered the other. A separate subtree R6 holds a `decision` whose `decided_by` names Alice. The agent comments on R1's text and on R2's text. The agent session writes a requirement R5, and a second agent session an author-only lens on R5.

`DELETE /api/v1/issues/{key}/nodes/{id}?dry_run=true` of R1 by alice answers `200` with `{"count": 6}`: R1, C1, P, L, F and X1, the nodes of the issue's tree read; it leaves out R1's and C1's own paragraphs, which no read returns, and Q, a node of another issue, which the walk of `{key}` passes over. A `DELETE` of R1 with no `If-Match` answers `428 PRECONDITION_REQUIRED`. A `DELETE` with a stale tag and the current count answers `412 PRECONDITION_FAILED`. A `DELETE` with no `expected_count` answers `400 DELETE_INPUT`. Then the `DELETE` with the `If-Match` of R1's `placement_seq` and `expected_count=6` answers `200` with `{"count": 6}`. Then R1, C1, P, Q, L, F and X1 read `gone`, and so do R1's and C1's own paragraphs; the newest versions of the spec, the Verification document and the child issue's room hold none of R1, C1, P, Q and X1; C4 stands live, its text where X1's text stood and its `part_of` to R2 unchanged. The lift-out of C4 empties X1, and the `DELETE` takes X1 and removes it in the same write, so the newest Verification version holds no callout with no content. Every tuple out of the nodes marked `gone` is retracted, including both of C1's `serves` tuples. Every tuple into them from a node that stays still stands: C2's `serves` to R1 among them. R2 stays live. Its coverage lists C2 and C4 but no C1. The agent's comment on R1's text reads `live`, its quote kept, its anchor `orphaned` true, and its `anchored_in` and `part_of` retracted, and `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/comments?node_anchor=true` answers its `node_anchor` naming R1's block node in the state `gone`. Alice's comment on L's text reads `live`, its `comments.node_anchor` naming L with its quote and `orphaned` true, its `anchored_in` and `part_of` retracted; the tree read answers it under the issue, its `anchor` naming L in the state `gone`, and the comments read with `node_anchor=true` answers the same. Alice then edits R2's words so they no longer hold the quote of the agent's comment on R2's text: that comment reads `orphaned` true and its `node_anchor` names R2 in the state `live`, so `orphaned` alone tells no delete. `envoy-dispatch census --store` reads `comment_anchor_block` at zero differences. `?view=spec&v=<the approved version>` still answers R1; the spec's approval reads changed since. A dry run of R2 answers `200` with `count`; alice then writes a prose block and moves it under R2 through `PATCH`, and the `DELETE` of R2 with the old `expected_count` answers `409 DELETE_COUNT_MOVED` with the new number in `count`, equal to a fresh dry run, while R2's `If-Match` still holds. `DELETE` of K answers 200, and the child issue reads its `child_of` and its `part_of` to K unchanged and stands under the issue in the tree read. `DELETE` of C3 answers `409 NODE_HOLDS_RESULT` naming C3 and the result. The agent session's dry run of R4 returns the count 2, R4 and X4, which excludes both ask blocks. It uses that count and the current tag to delete R4. The write answers `200` with the same count. It lifts both blocks out of X4's text to the place X4's text stood in the same document. The lift-out empties X4, and the same write removes X4, so the new version holds no callout with no content. Both ask ids, their states and the answered ask's answer survive. The dry run and the write of R6 instead answer `409 ANSWERED_ASK_KEPT`, quoting the person's decision and naming it. Neither refusal writes anything. `DELETE` of an ask, a comment, a message, a result and the issue node each answer `400 NODE_NOT_DELETABLE`. Alice's dry run of R5 answers `200` with `count` 1, counting R5 but not the hidden lens. The first agent session's dry run and its `DELETE` of R5 with a current tag and count 1 both answer `403 STATE_NOT_PERMITTED`. Neither response names the hidden lens or carries `count`. Each refusal and each dry run leaves every room's version count and the store's tuple count unchanged. The test reads both before and after.

The `DELETE` writes the lift-out and the removal as one direct write of each document's tree (R7, new). It writes under the room locks, as the `PATCH` writes its text, and it validates each document once, at the end. So the `DELETE` of R1 adds exactly one version to each document whose text it changes, the spec, the Verification document and the child issue's room among them, and the `DELETE` of R4 adds exactly one to the document that holds X4. The test reads each document's version count before and after, apart from the versions that the query drain writes. No version of those documents holds a `callout` with no content, because each container that a lift-out empties is a block the `DELETE` takes.

The `DELETE` does not go through the edit route's `delete` and `move` ops. `MoveBlock` in `pmdoc/blocks.go` validates the document after each move, and the `block+` content of a `callout` and of a `decision` (`pmdoc/schema/blocks.json`) refuses a container left empty for a moment, X1 and X4 among them. The fourteenth control writes the `DELETE` through those ops and reads that refusal.

Each node route reads a node through its kind's visibility rule (`refs/reasoning_nodes.go`), so another author's author-only node answers R7's `404 NOT_FOUND` (R32). The first agent session names the second session's author-only lens on R5 as `{id}`, with that lens's current `placement_seq` in `If-Match`, which the test reads from the store. Its dry run, its `DELETE` with `expected_count=1` and its `PATCH` with `parent` R2 each answer `404 NOT_FOUND`. Each answer holds the words that `nodeNotFound` in `api/node_address.go` answers for an address that names no node, `no node "<address>" under <key>`, and none of them writes anything. The second session, the lens's author, sends the same dry run and reads `403 STATE_NOT_PERMITTED`, R7's refusal of a lens that a caller who is no person takes `gone`, and not `404 NOT_FOUND`. So the route finds the lens for its author alone.

The `DELETE` refuses a removal that would leave a container it keeps with no block of its own (R7, new). Alice writes in the spec a `callout` Z, which holds one prose paragraph P9, and a requirement R9 with nothing under it, both under the issue. She moves P9 under R9 through the `PATCH`. A requirement's content is its own words, so P9's text stays in Z, and the tree holds P9 under R9 with the placement `stored`. Alice's dry run of R9, and her `DELETE` of R9 with the current `If-Match` and `expected_count=2`, each answer `409 CONTAINER_WOULD_EMPTY`, naming Z and its kind, with no `count`. The `DELETE` would take P9 and remove its text from Z, and Z stands outside what the `DELETE` takes. Neither answer writes anything: the spec's version count and the store's tuple count are the ones the test read before, and P9 and R9 read `live`. Else the test prints `dry run of <R9> answered <status> <code>, want 409 CONTAINER_WOULD_EMPTY`, or the same line for the `DELETE`, and fails.

The tree keeps the stored placement of P and Q, as the owner's answer in dispatch://TREE-2/comment/a2219523-e7b6-4b0f-884e-98650fd30635 and its interpretation in dispatch://TREE-2/comment/c15f4116-74e2-48c1-a08e-c6e6722074ef state. Person scope follows dispatch://TREE-2/comment/6fe69ea5-1afc-437a-9247-c0af3952228a and dispatch://TREE-2/comment/dd478237-1093-48ff-80a4-432128b9a051.

The test also uses `lockstep` to drive the two-attempt owner-lock rule. It uses a fresh subtree and two prose blocks from different child issue rooms. A test hook pauses the request after each unlocked discovery read and before it takes owner locks. While it pauses, Alice uses a separate `PATCH` to put one of the child-room blocks under the deletion target. Each under-lock read finds a different owner it did not lock. The first attempt releases its locks. The second starts with a new discovery read. After the second attempt the `DELETE` answers `409 PARENT_CONTENDED`, not `409 DELETE_COUNT_MOVED`. Neither attempt changes a room, a version, a tuple, a state or an event. Compare each with the state after the two moves, the only writes in this case.

For every refusal in R7's ordered list, the test sends a dry run and a write with valid write preconditions. It reads the same status, code and visible details in both answers, with no `count`. Include a document target, the R28 writer refusal on a Legion issue, and a subtree containing a person's protected decision refused under R32. A case that could trigger two refusals verifies the order. Dry runs take no write lock. The lock contention and missing or stale write preconditions are tested only on actual writes.

For each document whose text the `DELETE` changes, read the `artifact.version` event for the version the edit writes. Open an approval request before the delete and check that the request now names the new version. The node tuples are still written at `graphstore.NoEvent`. Check the document versions separately from the versions that the query drain writes.
:::

:::check{#c-removal-indexed serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-reparent-and-state" surface="api" run="cd packages/envoy &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; go test ./internal/dispatch/api/ -run '^TestEachForeignKeyCheckOfARemovalProbesAnIndex$' -count=1 -v 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/removal-indexed.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestEachForeignKeyCheckOfARemovalProbesAnIndex ' $TMPDIR/removal-indexed.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q -- '--- SKIP' $TMPDIR/removal-indexed.log" when="before_merge" negative_control="Two controls, run one at a time, each in a scratch copy. First, take the index on `user_document_reads.artifact_id` out of this child's migration. The test fails printing `the foreign key user_document_reads_artifact_id_fkey of user_document_reads.artifact_id plans no scan of an index led by artifact_id`. Second, take the `set local lock_timeout` out of the removal's transaction. The removal waits until the test ends the transaction that holds the lock, and the test fails printing `the removal waited &lt;seconds&gt; s on a held lock, past its lock_timeout of &lt;timeout&gt;`."}
The run proves this test executed. It greps the run's own log for this test's `--- PASS:` line and fails on any `--- SKIP` line, which `storetest.Open` writes when `DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL` is unset.

`TestEachForeignKeyCheckOfARemovalProbesAnIndex` in `internal/dispatch/api` is new, and this child adds it, with five migrations, each building a plain index on one of five columns concurrently, because pgmigrate admits one concurrent index build in a migration (`concurrentIndex`). At `810aa47b` no plain index leads them: `asks.block_artifact_id`, whose `asks_block_id_unique` holds only the rows where `block_id is not null`; `related_checks.source_artifact_id`; `user_document_reads.artifact_id`, whose primary key leads `login`; `write_suggestions.source_artifact_id`, whose `write_suggestions_pending_artifact` holds only the rows where `outcome = 'ignored'`; and `issue_room_blocks.document_id`, in a table this child adds. So the delete of the document's row in `removeArtifact` (`api/artifact_removal.go`) reads every row of each of those tables, while the removal holds the issue's owner lock and sets no `lock_timeout` (dispatch://TREE-2/artifact/measure-carry-removal-md).

On a database that `storetest.Open` migrated to this head, the test reads from `pg_constraint` every foreign key that references `artifacts (id)`, 31 at `810aa47b`, the five above among them. Else it prints `no foreign key on <table>.<column>`. For each key it takes the plan of the statement that the key's trigger runs when a row of `artifacts` is deleted: `select 1 from only <table> x where $1 = <column> for key share of x` for a key with no action, and `delete from only <table> where $1 = <column>` for a key that cascades, each with a uuid parameter (`explain (generic_plan)`). It takes each plan with `enable_seqscan` off. The test's tables are small, and on a small table the planner chooses a sequential scan though an index is there. Each plan holds an `Index Scan`, an `Index Only Scan` or a `Bitmap Index Scan` on an index whose first key column (`pg_index.indkey[0]`) is the key's column, and no `Seq Scan`. An index that serves the probe through a later column, as `user_document_reads_pkey (login, artifact_id)` does, does not count. Else the test prints `the foreign key <name> of <table>.<column> plans no scan of an index led by <column>`.

Then the test makes an untouched document through `POST /api/v1/issues/{key}/artifacts`. A second transaction takes `lock table user_document_reads in access exclusive mode` and holds it, and the test sends `DELETE /api/v1/artifacts/{id}` for the document. The removal answers with a status other than 204 within its `lock_timeout` and 5 s more, and the document's row still stands. The test ends the second transaction once that time has passed, whatever the removal answered. It then sends the `DELETE` again and reads 204. Else it prints `the removal waited <seconds> s on a held lock, past its lock_timeout of <timeout>`.
:::

:::check{#c-queries serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-queries dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-result-node dispatch://TREE-1/spec#b-r-verification-edges" surface="api" run="cd packages/dispatch &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; DATABASE_URL=$INFRA_1253_UPGRADE_DATABASE_URL DISPATCH_TOKEN=e2e-token PROJECT=CORE DEV_SIGNIN_LOGIN=alice bash e2e/acceptance/issue-tree-queries.sh 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/issue-tree-queries.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^PASS: issue-tree-queries.sh complete ' $TMPDIR/issue-tree-queries.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q '^SKIP' $TMPDIR/issue-tree-queries.log" when="before_merge" negative_control="Four controls, run one at a time. First, restore the document lookup in the coverage read, so it finds the requirements through the issue's spec artifact, on an issue whose spec nodes have moved. The read answers no requirement and the driver exits non-zero, printing the empty answer. Second, make the Plan query leave out the `serves` attribute of each plan task. The Plan query then answers a plan task without the `serves` the earlier plan read answered, and the driver prints both and exits non-zero. Third, make the tree read answer the prose blocks of the spec. The driver prints the first prose block it read and exits non-zero. Fourth, make `?view=decisions` answer `waiting_review` true for the decision that is kept. The driver prints that entry with both values and exits non-zero."}
Spec, Verification, Plan and Decisions are the four queries. The issue's relations answer from the same graph and are not a query of their own. The issue this check converts was written by the earlier release, through the base-commit server this document's preamble states, and the driver takes the reads before the move from that issue. It then boots this branch's server, and waits for the backfill as this document's preamble states, and converts the issue with `envoy-dispatch convert-issues --project CORE`. On that converted issue the driver reads `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/coverage` and `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/results`. It compares the fields the earlier release answered, entry for entry and word for word, with what the same reads answered before the move, except for the two fields the conversion moves by design — `checks[].version` (to the converted verification query version) and `results[].check_artifact_id` (to the issue's tree artifact id) — each asserted at its exact new value. It finds the same requirements in the same order with the same references. It finds the same checks with their `when`, `surface`, `run` and `negative_control`, the same results, and the same gap lines. The line `<block id> has no plan task` still appears only once the issue has a plan. The driver then compares the four queries and the tree read with the reads they replace, on the same converted issue. The issue holds, written through the earlier release, at least one open ask in its spec and a decision in each review state: one marked replaced, one kept through the Keep route and one waiting review. The driver fails where the earlier decisions read answered no entry in `open_questions`, or no entry in `decisions`, or no decision in one of those three states. Before the move it took, from the earlier release, `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/artifacts/{slug}/text?blocks=true` for the spec, `verification-md` and `plan-md`, and `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/decisions`. Each of the three documents holds prose blocks beside its typed blocks, as a real spec does. Each query is compared over the parts R8 gives it, block by block, keyed by block id, with each block's markdown as the earlier read answered it. The Spec query is compared over the memo callout, where the spec holds one, and the requirement blocks, because no earlier release wrote a criterion. The Verification query is compared over the check blocks, with their `serves`, `surface`, `run`, `when` and `negative_control`. The Plan query is compared over the plan tasks, with their `serves` and `needs`. The tree read with no view answers each of those blocks once, which are the blocks R2 and R16 put in the issue's tree, and it answers no prose block of the three documents, because R2 and R16 keep a role document's prose out of every query. The Decisions query is compared with the earlier decisions read through that read's two members, `open_questions` and `decisions`, entry for entry over the entries the earlier read answered, each keyed by the id that read gives it. For an open question, keyed by its ask id, `?view=decisions` answers the same question and options. For a decision, keyed by its `block_id`, it answers the same heading, text, kind, `replaced`, `kept` and `waiting_review`. `?view=decisions` may also answer entries the earlier read left out, such as an answered ask or an ask outside the spec, so the comparison is not an equality of the two lists. The driver prints every difference with the query and the block or entry it is in.
:::

:::check{#c-head-projection serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-queries dispatch://TREE-1/spec#b-r-no-regression" surface="api" run="cd packages/envoy &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; go test ./internal/dispatch/graphstore/ -run '^TestEveryWriterOfAHeadFactWritesTheHeadRow$' -count=1 -v 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/head-writers.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestEveryWriterOfAHeadFactWritesTheHeadRow ' $TMPDIR/head-writers.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q -- '--- SKIP' $TMPDIR/head-writers.log &amp;&amp; go test ./internal/dispatch/api/ -run '^TestTheHeadProjectionAnswersAsTheWalk$' -count=1 -v 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/head-walk.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestTheHeadProjectionAnswersAsTheWalk ' $TMPDIR/head-walk.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q -- '--- SKIP' $TMPDIR/head-walk.log &amp;&amp; go test ./internal/dispatch/graphcensus/ -run '^TestTheHeadProjectionBackfillReadsZero$' -count=1 -v 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/head-backfill.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestTheHeadProjectionBackfillReadsZero ' $TMPDIR/head-backfill.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q -- '--- SKIP' $TMPDIR/head-backfill.log &amp;&amp; go test ./internal/dispatch/graphcensus/ -run '^(TestTheFillHoldsTheHeadFillLockAgainstAWriteOfTheReleaseBefore|TestTheTickRefillsAnIssueWhoseMarkWasTakenAway)$' -count=1 -v 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/head-fill.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestTheFillHoldsTheHeadFillLockAgainstAWriteOfTheReleaseBefore ' $TMPDIR/head-fill.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestTheTickRefillsAnIssueWhoseMarkWasTakenAway ' $TMPDIR/head-fill.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q -- '--- SKIP' $TMPDIR/head-fill.log &amp;&amp; go test ./internal/dispatch/graphstore/ -run '^TestEveryWriterOfACommentWritesItsHeadRows$' -count=1 -v 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/head-comment-writers.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestEveryWriterOfACommentWritesItsHeadRows ' $TMPDIR/head-comment-writers.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q -- '--- SKIP' $TMPDIR/head-comment-writers.log" when="before_merge" negative_control="Ten controls, run one at a time, each on a copy as this document's preamble states. First, take the head write (`graphstore.QueueHeads` or `graphstore.WriteHeads`) out of the state route, `writeNodeState` in `api/reasoning_write.go`, so the route appends the node's `state` and writes no row of `issue_head_nodes`. TestEveryWriterOfAHeadFactWritesTheHeadRow fails printing `api/reasoning_write.go#writeNodeState writes a value or a relation out of a tree node and no head row`. TestTheHeadProjectionAnswersAsTheWalk fails in its state route case, printing `the head read of &lt;key&gt; answers &lt;node&gt; as &lt;got&gt;, the walk as &lt;want&gt;` and `after the state route write the census kind issue_head_node reads 1 difference(s) at &lt;node&gt;`. Second, have the backfill pass `backfillIssueHeadNodes` pass over one stored issue. TestTheHeadProjectionBackfillReadsZero fails printing `the backfill left &lt;key&gt; unmarked`, because the skipped issue holds no mark, and the census reads no unmarked issue. Third, drop the triggers on `graph_tuples` and `graph_nodes` that take an issue's mark away. In each case of the release before's writes, the mark stands, and the head read answers the stale row. TestTheHeadProjectionAnswersAsTheWalk fails printing `the head read of &lt;key&gt; answers &lt;node&gt; as &lt;got&gt;, the walk as &lt;want&gt;`. Fourth, have the trigger delete the mark without taking the issue's head-fill lock. In the case of a fill and a write of the release before, the write does not wait, its delete does not see the fill's uncommitted mark, and the mark stands after both commit. TestTheHeadProjectionAnswersAsTheWalk fails printing `the mark of &lt;key&gt; stands after a write of the release before`. Fifth, have the trigger take the issue's owner lock in place of its head-fill lock. In the case of the owner lock's holder and the write that holds the row `for share`, Postgres aborts one side with `deadlock detected`, and TestTheHeadProjectionAnswersAsTheWalk fails printing that error. Sixth, take the head write out of the cause site that the exemption of `Queue` in `refs/blocks.go` names. TestEveryWriterOfAHeadFactWritesTheHeadRow fails printing `refs/blocks.go Queue leaves its head row to &lt;cause site&gt;, which writes none`. Seventh, have the trigger take the head-fill lock in exclusive mode. In the case of two writes of the release before on one unmarked issue, the second waits for the first and fails with `lock timeout`, and TestTheHeadProjectionAnswersAsTheWalk fails printing `two writes of the release before on &lt;key&gt; waited on each other's head-fill lock`. Eighth, have `graphcensus.FillIssueHeads` and `backfillIssueHeadNodes` fill without `store.LockHeadFill`. A plain-SQL write of the release before then commits beside the real fill, and TestTheFillHoldsTheHeadFillLockAgainstAWriteOfTheReleaseBefore fails printing the issue whose mark stands over a row the write changed. Ninth, have the block index tick skip `graphcensus.FillIssueHeads`. TestTheTickRefillsAnIssueWhoseMarkWasTakenAway fails printing the issues still unmarked after the ticks. Tenth, remove the `graphstore.KeptHeadRows` claim from the item index's comment statements. TestEveryWriterOfACommentWritesItsHeadRows prints `refs/item_blocks.go#queueBlocks writes a comment, its blocks or their texts in a statement that does not claim their head rows kept`."}
The run checks a named `--- PASS:` line for each of the six tests and rejects every `--- SKIP` line. Both writer checks run in `internal/dispatch/graphstore`.

It proves that each writer R8 names writes the head row. `TestEveryWriterOfAHeadFactWritesTheHeadRow` in `internal/dispatch/graphstore` reads the module's source as `TestEveryStoreWriteCallSiteIsListed` in `graphstore/store_writers_test.go` reads it. It finds each call site that writes a node row, or that appends a value or a relation tuple out of a node. It fails on each such site that calls neither `graphstore.QueueHeads` nor `graphstore.WriteHeads` beside it, and prints `<site> writes a value or a relation out of a tree node and no head row`. The test keeps a named exemption list, and prints each entry with its reason in the log. An entry is a writer of nodes that no tree holds (persons, sessions, roles, pages, runs, frames, components, the lens catalogue), a wrapper of `graphstore` whose callers are the sites checked, or a site that writes only a node row whose facts are appended later in the same transaction at a cause site the entry names. For each entry of the last sort the test fails when the named cause site calls neither `graphstore.QueueHeads` nor `graphstore.WriteHeads`, and prints `<site> leaves its head row to <cause site>, which writes none`. The same scan over a copy of one file with such a site planted finds it, and both readings go into the log.

It proves that the head read answers what the walk answers (R8). `TestTheHeadProjectionAnswersAsTheWalk` in `internal/dispatch/api` has one case for each writer class R8 names, each through its real write. Four cases more are the corpus of 2,000 blocks at depth 6 of the root's `c-read-cost`, a plan of 2,000 `plan_task` blocks, a node stated `gone`, and a node that another person may not see. `readCostTreeText` in `api/read_cost_corpus_test.go` writes the first, as a document other than a role document, so the read with no view answers none of its blocks. The plan's blocks are typed role blocks, so the read with no view answers each of them. One more is a person's reply in a thread an agent wrote, which makes the agent's comment a conversation node (R2). After each write the test reads `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/tree`, with no view and with each of the four views, as the issue's author and as another person. Each answer equals, byte for byte, the same read answered from the walk at the head cut. Else the test prints `the head read of <key> answers <node> as <got>, the walk as <want>`.

It proves the marks of `issue_head_marks` (R8). An issue that the test creates holds its mark from the write that makes its first tree node, and the head read of a marked issue reads `issue_head_nodes`. Else the test prints `<key> holds no mark after its first tree node` or `the head read of marked <key> walked the tuples`. After each current writer runs, the issue retains its mark because the writer claims `dispatch.head_rows=kept` and writes the head rows in the same transaction. The comment writer test checks this claim on the statements that write the comment, its blocks and their texts. Else the test prints `the <class> write took the mark of <key> away`. Three cases are writes of the release before, each by plain SQL on a marked issue, with no head row and no setting, as a build with no head write makes them. The first inserts into `graph_tuples` a tuple out of a node of the issue's tree. The second inserts into `graph_nodes` a new node, with its `part_of` tuple into that tree. The third updates in place a `graph_nodes` row of that tree. After each, the issue's mark is gone when the transaction commits, and the head read walks the tuples and answers the new state. Else the test prints `the head read of <key> answers <node> as <got>, the walk as <want>`. One more case holds a fill and a write of the release before apart. On one connection a transaction takes the issue's head-fill lock, as a fill does, and writes the issue's mark. On another connection a plain-SQL write of the release before on the same issue starts, and it waits. The first transaction commits its mark. Then the write completes, and the issue's mark is gone. Else the test prints `the mark of <key> stands after a write of the release before`. One more case holds that no cycle forms. On one connection a transaction takes a marked issue's owner lock, and then the issue's row `for no key update`. On another connection a write of the release before holds that row `for share`, and appends by plain SQL a `part_of` tuple into that issue's tree. Both transactions complete, and neither fails with `deadlock detected`. Else the test prints the error Postgres answered. Two more tests drive the real fill rather than a transaction that takes the lock by hand. `TestTheFillHoldsTheHeadFillLockAgainstAWriteOfTheReleaseBefore` runs `graphcensus.FillIssueHeads`, and then `backfillIssueHeadNodes`, beside a plain-SQL write of the release before on the same issue: the write waits for the fill, and the mark the fill wrote is gone after both commit. `TestTheTickRefillsAnIssueWhoseMarkWasTakenAway` takes the marks of more issues than one tick's batch away, runs the block index tick, finds a full batch refilled and marked, runs it again, and finds every issue marked. Both tests are new, in `internal/dispatch/graphcensus` (dispatch://TREE-2/artifact/plan-md#b-t13j). One more case holds that two writes of the release before do not wait on each other's head-fill lock. On an unmarked issue, on two connections, each under `set local lock_timeout = '2s'`, a plain-SQL write of the release before appends a tuple into that issue's tree, and neither commits until both have run: both statements complete, and neither fails with `lock timeout`. Else the test prints `two writes of the release before on <key> waited on each other's head-fill lock`. On a marked issue the same two writes run, and the second waits until the first commits, on the mark's row, and then completes; the mark is gone after both. Else the test prints what Postgres answered.

After each write the test also takes the census kind `issue_head_node`, which compares each whole row of each marked issue with the tuples. It reads zero differences in both directions. Else the test prints `after the <class> write the census kind issue_head_node reads <n> difference(s) at <node>`.

It proves the backfill. `TestTheHeadProjectionBackfillReadsZero` in `internal/dispatch/graphcensus` writes by SQL, in the shape the release before stores, issues that hold blocks, a conversation and a result. It writes no row of `issue_head_nodes`, because the release before has no such table. The backfill pass `backfillIssueHeadNodes`, through `graphcensus.Backfill`, then writes one row for each node of each issue's tree. It marks each issue in the transaction that holds the issue's owner lock, after it writes every row of that issue. After the pass every issue the test wrote holds its mark. Else the test prints `the backfill left <key> unmarked`. The census kind `issue_head_node` reads zero differences after it. Else the test prints `after the backfill the census kind issue_head_node reads <n> difference(s) at issue <key>`. The test then takes one issue's mark away and appends a tuple of its tree. The next run of the pass writes that issue's rows again and marks it again. Else the test prints `the backfill left <key> unmarked` or the census line above.

`TestEveryWriterOfACommentWritesItsHeadRows` scans writers of `comments`, `comment_blocks` and `comment_block_texts`. It checks that each writer that changes a projected value writes its head rows in the same transaction and makes the `KeptHeadRows` claim before the row triggers run. It checks the named same-transaction callers that write the head rows for a writer. It prints the verdicts of planted writers, one missing its head write and one missing its claim. `TestEveryWriterOfAHeadFactWritesTheHeadRow` above checks the separate set of node and tuple writers.
:::

:::check{#c-tree-read-bound serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-queries dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-kind-filter dispatch://TREE-1/spec#b-r-no-regression" surface="api" run="case &#x22;${TREE_READ_BOUND_STAGE:?set TREE_READ_BOUND_STAGE to job or median}&#x22; in job) cd packages/envoy &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL='postgres://postgres:ci@127.0.0.1:5432/postgres?sslmode=disable' go test -tags basebuild ./internal/dispatch/api/ -run '^(TestTheTreeReadAnswersTheSkeletonWithinItsBounds|TestTheTwoCutsAnswerAsTheUncutWalk)$' -timeout 170m -count=1 -v 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/tree-read-bound.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestTheTreeReadAnswersTheSkeletonWithinItsBounds ' $TMPDIR/tree-read-bound.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestTheTwoCutsAnswerAsTheUncutWalk ' $TMPDIR/tree-read-bound.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q -- '--- SKIP' $TMPDIR/tree-read-bound.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q 'database time was not measured' $TMPDIR/tree-read-bound.log ;; median) p='(\.IssueTreePageSize[[:space:]]*=[^=]|IssueTreePageSize[[:space:]]*:[^=])'; planted=$(mktemp -d) &amp;&amp; printf 'package main\n\nfunc limit(deps *api.Deps) { deps.IssueTreePageSize = 2 }\n' &gt; &#x22;$planted/planted.go&#x22; &amp;&amp; { grep -rnE --include='*.go' --exclude='*_test.go' &#x22;$p&#x22; &#x22;$planted&#x22; | grep -q 'planted.go' || { echo 'c-tree-read-bound: the grep for IssueTreePageSize found no planted assignment'; exit 1; }; } &amp;&amp; { ! grep -rnE --include='*.go' --exclude='*_test.go' &#x22;$p&#x22; packages/envoy | grep -vE '^[^:]+:[0-9]+:[[:space:]]*//' | tee &#x22;$TMPDIR/tree-limit-set.log&#x22; | grep -q . || { echo 'c-tree-read-bound: a file outside _test.go sets Deps.IssueTreePageSize:'; cat &#x22;$TMPDIR/tree-limit-set.log&#x22;; exit 1; }; } &amp;&amp; echo 'c-tree-read-bound: no file outside _test.go sets Deps.IssueTreePageSize, and the grep found the planted assignment'; [ &#x22;$J1&#x22; != &#x22;$J2&#x22; ] &amp;&amp; [ &#x22;$J1&#x22; != &#x22;$J3&#x22; ] &amp;&amp; [ &#x22;$J2&#x22; != &#x22;$J3&#x22; ] || exit 1; for j in &#x22;${J1:?set J1}&#x22; &#x22;${J2:?set J2}&#x22; &#x22;${J3:?set J3}&#x22;; do q=&#x22;labels.\&#x22;k8s-pod/job-name\&#x22;=\&#x22;$j\&#x22; AND resource.labels.container_name=\&#x22;test\&#x22;&#x22;; pod=$(gcloud logging read &#x22;$q&#x22; --project &lt;project&gt; --freshness=3d --limit=1 --format='value(resource.labels.pod_name)') &amp;&amp; [ -n &#x22;$pod&#x22; ] &amp;&amp; gcloud logging read &#x22;$q AND resource.labels.pod_name=\&#x22;$pod\&#x22;&#x22; --project &lt;project&gt; --freshness=3d --format='value(textPayload)' &gt; &#x22;$TMPDIR/$j.log&#x22; || { echo &#x22;$j: no output of its newest pod&#x22;; exit 1; }; done; bash packages/dispatch/e2e/acceptance/tree-read-db-medians.sh &#x22;$TMPDIR/$J1.log&#x22; &#x22;$TMPDIR/$J2.log&#x22; &#x22;$TMPDIR/$J3.log&#x22; ;; *) exit 2 ;; esac" when="before_merge" negative_control="Twelve controls, one at a time in the scratch copies used by the three Jobs. (a) Let the no-view read include blocks of other documents again. The fixture reports a returned block from one of TREE-10's other documents. (b) Remove the 200-comment limit. The cursor walk of the TREE-7 fixture prints the returned comment count, not 200. (c) Run `refs.TreeFactsOf` and `refs.TreeNodeRows` twice for each no-view read. The test prints the loader and its calls per read, above one. (d) Let the kind read include an unselected block of another document. The test prints the unexpected node. (e) Read the facts of each comment in a separate statement in the large Spec view. The test prints its p90 above 200 ms. (f) Remove the byte cap but keep the node cap. The wide-node fixture prints the page's bytes, above 2,000,000. (g) Feed the median step three scratch logs whose Verification read of the largest-plan fixture has new times of 9 ms, more than twice its recorded median of 4.174 ms. It prints that fixture and view, the new median, the recorded median and an over-bound verdict. (h) Keep the cursor but omit `remaining`. The test prints the issue, filter and page, with `cursor present, remaining absent`. (i) Count bob's `remaining` over every node of the issue, alice's author-only lens included. The test prints the page, bob's `remaining` and the count of nodes bob may see after that page, and fails. (j) In the median stage, read the logs of every pod of a Job. Rerun one Job so that it has two pods. The median step prints that fixture and filter with two pairs in one log, and fails. (k) In `cmd/dispatch/main.go`, read the node limit from an environment variable and assign it to `deps.IssueTreePageSize`. The median stage prints `c-tree-read-bound: a file outside _test.go sets Deps.IssueTreePageSize:` with that line, and fails. (l) Break the second cut: let `readMembers` read the text of no parent that stands off the page, and answer that parent with no text, so that a node whose parent stands on an earlier page answers that parent without the first line that `parentOf` names. At the node limit of 2, `TestTheTwoCutsAnswerAsTheUncutWalk` prints the state, the read, the page and the first byte where the answer and the un-cut walk's answer differ, and fails."}
Run the `job` stage in three build Jobs as the root's `c-read-cost` runs it (`skill://running-heavy-jobs`). Use the same tested head and the same PR body's `BASELINE_SHA` in each Job. Each Job has its own Postgres sidecar, using the CI image and preloading `pg_stat_statements`, with `pg_stat_statements.track=all` and JIT off. The run uses the sidecar's test database, not the pod's Postgres. Each Job must print a named PASS. A missing measurement or any `--- SKIP` fails the check.

`TestTheTreeReadAnswersTheSkeletonWithinItsBounds` in `internal/dispatch/api` holds the tree reads to the bounds of R8 and the root’s read-cost rule. The test already exists in `api/tree_read_skeleton_bound_test.go` under the build tag `basebuild`. This child extends the test. It boots its two builds as the root's `c-read-cost` test boots them (`TestNoReadThisTreeMovesGetsSlower` and `startReadCostServer` in `api/tree_read_cost_test.go`, `legion/TREE-1-t22` at `ff601028`). It boots the build of `BASELINE_SHA` and seeds four issues through that build's own routes. Those routes are `POST /api/v1/issues`, `POST /api/v1/issues/{key}/artifacts`, `POST /api/v1/issues/{key}/comments` and `POST /api/v1/issues/{key}/asks`. A person writes each comment, so that each comment is a conversation node (R2). The sizes come from the census of production (dispatch://TREE-11/artifact/load-measure-md, sections 1 and 1b). The first issue is shaped like TREE-8. It holds a spec of 62 blocks (31 `requirement` blocks), a Verification document of 106 blocks (53 `check` blocks) and a plan of 2,786 blocks (1,393 `plan_task` blocks), 47 comments and 5 asks, 3,006 parts in all. Each typed block holds a paragraph, which the blocks read lists as a block of its own, so a document is at most half typed blocks; the corpus makes each role document half typed, which is heavier than TREE-8's own (14, 27 and 75 typed blocks). The second is shaped like TREE-7. It holds a spec of 3 `requirement` blocks and 9,252 comments. The third is shaped like TREE-10. It holds a plan of 730 `plan_task` blocks, 65 other documents of 45,008 blocks in all, 113 comments and 5 asks. The largest of its other documents holds 5,600 blocks. The census gives no split of its 730 role blocks, so the test puts them all in the plan. The fourth issue holds a spec of 2,786 blocks, 1,393 of them `requirement` blocks. Each role block is a typed block, because no query of the issue's tree answers the prose of a role document (R2, R16). A corpus of prose would measure less than the skeleton.

The old side is the build of `BASELINE_SHA`. The test reads it first (below). Then it stops that build and boots this head over the same database, as `c-read-cost` boots its second build. It waits until the boot's backfill is done, each of the four issues holds its mark in `issue_head_marks`, no document owes its block index, and no document and no item owes its windows, on both sides; it prints those counts and the idle interval beside each side's readings. Then, as the reader, it holds each corpus to its shape through the read with no view. The first issue answers its 2,954 role blocks, 47 comments and 5 asks, and `comments_before` null. The second answers its 3 role blocks and the 200 newest of its 9,252 comments, and a `comments_before` that names the oldest of those 200. The third answers its 730 role blocks, 113 comments and 5 asks, and no block of its 65 other documents. Its `document_nodes` lists each document of kind `doc` that the issue read lists. Each entry has the `block_count` that `GET /api/v1/artifacts/{id}/blocks` lists for that document, 5,600 for the largest. The spec view of the fourth issue answers its 1,393 requirements, and the plan view of the first issue answers its 1,393 plan tasks. Those are counts over the node-cursor walk, not counts that one response must hold. Keep `comments_before` fixed while following `cursor`; the older comment pages remain a separate read. A count that differs fails the test, which prints `<key> answers <count read> <kind>, not <count expected>`. The test records each failed assertion and goes on, so that one run prints every assertion it broke.

After `analyze`, measure 30 first-page reads after five warm-ups. The first page alone is the first load. Do not follow a cursor before the reader opens another page. The separate correctness walk tests those later pages. Use `Dispatch-Trees: 1`. On each side use the same issue and reader and verify JIT is off with `show jit`. Measure database time by the delta of `pg_stat_statements.total_exec_time` for the database and role, divided by the readings. Keep the idle interval reading beside it. Print p50, p90, p99, JSON bytes, statements and database time per read. Fail if the database time cannot be measured. For each fixture, measure R8's old page first load and its role tabs. The first load uses these nine reads. `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/comments`, `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/asks?state=all`, the spec's `GET /api/v1/artifacts/{id}`, `GET /api/v1/artifacts/{id}/text` and `GET /api/v1/artifacts/{id}/blocks`, `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/decisions`, `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/coverage`, `GET /api/v1/references?kind=part_of&to=<spec>` and `GET /api/v1/references/questions?kind=artifact&id=<spec>`. For the no-view and conversation kind reads, compare with that first load and the three tabs together, as R8 and R30 define the comparison. For Spec use the spec artifact, text and blocks reads. For Plan use its artifact, text, blocks and artifact comment reads. For Verification use the corresponding Verification reads and the issue's results read. For Decisions use the old issue Decisions read. Seed a readable role document and matching content on the old side where a fixture would not exercise a view. Use the same content on the new side. Keep the old request list with each timing.

In each Job the first read of each filter has a p90 of at most 200 ms on every fixture, including `?view=verification` and `?view=decisions`. A failure prints the issue, filter and p90. In each no-view read, each loader's statement (`refs.TreeFactsOf` and `refs.TreeNodeRows`) runs at most once. Use the existing checks of their statement text in `pg_stat_statements`. The median step below judges database time, not a single Job's ratio.

The two cuts of R8 keep every byte of each answer. `TestTheTwoCutsAnswerAsTheUncutWalk` in `internal/dispatch/api`, a Go test the implementer adds with no build tag, builds the 46 states of `TestTheHeadProjectionAnswersAsTheWalk` through the same writes, at this head: the 34 states that its `after` reads, the 8 that `releaseBefore` reads, two for each of its four writes of the release before, and the 4 that it reads with `requireAsWalk` alone. In each state it reads 7 read forms, the read with no view, the four views, the conversation's kinds and `kind=check&kind=result`, as each of 2 readers: 644 first pages at the default node limit, and every page at a node limit of 2 (below). The four views are `issueTreeViews` in `api/issue_tree_read.go`. The test logs the number of pages it compared, and it fails where it compared none. The test answers each read twice at the same cut: through the route, with both cuts, and through the un-cut walk. The un-cut walk is a reference read that the implementer adds behind a seam that only a test sets. It takes the issue's mark away for its length, as `walkRead` in `api/head_projection_test.go` does, so it walks the tuples. It reads the facts and the members of every node that the walk reaches, the blocks of the issue's other documents and the comments outside the comment page among them, and only then applies the skeleton, the comment page and the page window. Each answer equals the un-cut walk's answer, byte for byte. The test replays the reads at the default node limit, and again on a second test server over the same store whose node limit is 2 (the `testServerOptions` field below), where it follows each cursor to the end, so that the page window cuts real pages. Else the test prints the state, the read, the page and the first byte where the two answers differ. No commit before this head answers as the skeleton without the cuts, because the skeleton, the comment page, both cuts and `api/head_projection_test.go` landed in one commit, `69ffb131`. So the test compares two answers of this build, and it removes no member from either answer.

On the fourth fixture, write 9,252 comments on the spec blocks and measure the Spec view. Check p90 at most 200 ms and the 200 newest comments across its node pages. Then write the TREE-10 fixture's 12,050 plan tasks for the pagination test. Follow the plan-task filter's cursor to null. Check that each page stays below both caps and that all 12,050 tasks occur exactly once in walk order. A wide fixture must hit the byte cap before the node limit. A separate boundary case, on a test server with a smaller node limit, must hit the node limit first.

On each of the four seeded issues (`the largest plan`, `the most comments`, `the most blocks` and `the largest spec`, the names of `skeletonShapes` in `api/tree_read_skeleton_bound_test.go`), read the no-view, kind, Spec, Verification, Plan and Decisions forms. Check the uncompressed JSON length of every page, including the first. Check the page has at most `issueTreePageSize` nodes and at most 2,000,000 bytes, including tuples and context. Follow `cursor` under the same filter and cut. Require no duplicates, skipped nodes or reordering, and a null cursor only after the last node. Print the issue, filter, cursor and byte count on failure. Preserve the independent `comments_before` limit. For every page with a `cursor`, check that `remaining` is present, is positive and equals the number of nodes after that page in the expected read. Confirm that count by following the cursor on demand to the end. Check both byte-ended and node-ended pages. Check that the kind-filter walk includes no unselected block of another document. In a separate case, on a test server whose node limit is 2, read a small issue. Alice writes an author-only lens on one of its requirements (dispatch://TREE-6's R1). Bob reads the read with no view and follows its cursor. On each page with a `cursor`, `remaining` equals the number of nodes bob may see after that page, and it leaves out alice's lens. No page answers `remaining` 0 beside a `cursor`. Alice's read of the same issue counts her lens.

Both cases with a smaller node limit run on a test server that `newTestServer` in `api/server_test.go` starts in the same test, and not on the two booted builds. The limit comes from a new field of `testServerOptions`, which the implementer adds and which `newTestServer` hands to the server. A test that leaves the field unset reads pages of `issueTreePageSize` nodes (`api/issue_tree_read.go`). No flag, setting or environment variable of the server reaches that limit, so production cannot set it, and no run of this check sets one. The server's field is `Deps.IssueTreePageSize` (`api/server.go`), which the implementer adds under that name, and only `newTestServer` sets it. The median stage greps each Go file under `packages/envoy`, outside the `_test.go` files, for an assignment of that field, and fails on each line it finds, which it prints. Before that, it runs the same grep over a scratch file that assigns the field and finds that line, so a grep that matched nothing cannot read as clean.

Seed decisions and answered asks so the Decisions measurements are not empty. Measure `?view=decisions`, which replaces `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/decisions` when the root removes that route. The same byte and p90 bounds apply to Verification and to every other listed read.

Each Job prints one line per fixture and filter: `c-tree-read-bound: database time per reading: fixture=<name> read=<filter> old=<ms> new=<ms>`. Use stable fixture labels, not keys assigned during seeding. Set `TREE_READ_BOUND_STAGE=job` in each Job. After all three Jobs complete, run the same command in the pod with `TREE_READ_BOUND_STAGE=median` and their distinct names as `J1`, `J2` and `J3`. This stage reads the log of each Job's newest pod, as the root's `c-read-cost` reads it, so a Job that ran again gives one pair per fixture and filter. It then runs `packages/dispatch/e2e/acceptance/tree-read-db-medians.sh`, which the implementer adds. The check passes only after the median stage passes. It requires a named PASS in each log and exactly one numeric old/new pair per fixture and filter in each log. Missing, duplicate or unmeasured readings fail. It prints the median of the three old-side times and the median of the three new-side times. Each new median must be at most twice its recorded median, or no more than 1 ms higher than it when the recorded median is under 2 ms. The recorded medians are the 24 new medians of Jobs `infra-1253-tree-bound-dq7wv`, `infra-1253-tree-bound-9klm5` and `infra-1253-tree-bound-spbcz` at head `75c96d1b22` (dispatch://TREE-2/comment/f3e1abb1-d4c7-4431-8c76-28ce45890f2e). The implementer commits them in `packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/api/testdata/tree-read-bound-recorded.json`, with that head and those Job names, and `tree-read-db-medians.sh` reads them from that file. The owner accepted this rule in place of a comparison with the old page's reads: the page may use more database time than the old page while every read stays under 200 ms at p90 (dispatch://TREE-1/ask/4fa03306-8f00-4c13-af03-91e0aa995e98). Each line still prints the old side's median beside the new median and the recorded median. Apply the rule separately to each fixture and filter, not to a sum of new view reads. The read with `kind` naming the conversation's kinds is one of those filters, so it holds R8's rule of three medians too (R30).
:::

:::check{#c-comment-page serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-queries" surface="api" run="cd packages/envoy &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; go test ./internal/dispatch/api/ -run '^TestTheTreeReadPagesTheCommentsNewestFirst$' -count=1 -v 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/comment-page.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestTheTreeReadPagesTheCommentsNewestFirst ' $TMPDIR/comment-page.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q -- '--- SKIP' $TMPDIR/comment-page.log" when="before_merge" negative_control="Two controls, run one at a time, each in a scratch copy as this document's preamble states. First, order the comment page oldest first. The test fails printing `page 1 of &lt;key&gt; answers comment &lt;id&gt; of &lt;made_at&gt;, older than comment &lt;id&gt; it leaves out`. Second, answer a `comments_before` past the end with `200` and no comment. The test fails printing `comments_before past the end of &lt;key&gt; answered 200, not 400`."}
The run proves the test executed. It greps the run's own log for the test's `--- PASS:` line, and it accepts no `--- SKIP` line. A skip of the whole test, which `storetest.Open` writes when `DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL` is unset, leaves no `--- PASS:` line, so the run fails.

`TestTheTreeReadPagesTheCommentsNewestFirst` in `internal/dispatch/api` proves the comment page of R8. The test is new: the implementer writes it with this title. On a test server (`newTestServer`), a person creates an issue through `POST /api/v1/issues`, with a spec that holds one requirement. The same person writes one ask through `POST /api/v1/issues/{key}/asks`. Then the person writes 450 comments through `POST /api/v1/issues/{key}/comments`, one after another. The last comment is a reply to the first.

The test reads `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/tree` with no view, as that person. The first page holds the requirement, the ask and the 200 newest comments by `made_at` and id. Its `comments_before` names the oldest of them as `<made_at>,<id>`, with `<made_at>` in RFC 3339, UTC, with microseconds. A read with that `comments_before` answers the next 200 older comments, no comment of the first page, and neither the requirement nor the ask. Its own `comments_before` names its oldest comment. A third read answers the 50 oldest comments, and `comments_before` null. The three pages hold each of the 450 comments once, and they are the comments that `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/comments` lists. The reply on the first page names the first comment, which is on the third page, as its `parent`.

A `comments_before` that names the oldest comment, which is a position past the end, answers `400 INVALID_QUERY`, naming `comments_before` and its field, `<made_at>,<id>`. `comments_before=abc` answers the same, and so does a `comments_before` beside `cursor`. A `comments_before` beside `view=spec` answers the next page of the spec view's comments on text, as `c-comments-on-text` reads it. The description of the route in `api/routes_table.go` names `comments_before` and its field. Where the first page holds a comment older than one it leaves out, the test prints `page 1 of <key> answers comment <id> of <made_at>, older than comment <id> it leaves out`. Where a position past the end answers `200`, it prints `comments_before past the end of <key> answered 200, not 400`. Where any other of these does not hold, the test prints the page, the comment and what it expected. Each of these fails the test.
:::

:::check{#c-kind-filter serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-kind-filter dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-queries" surface="api" run="cd packages/envoy &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL=$LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN go test ./internal/dispatch/api/ -run '^(TestTheTreeReadFiltersByNodeKind|TestAKindFilterPutsEachContextNodeOnTheFirstPageThatNamesIt)$' -count=1 -v 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/kind-filter.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestTheTreeReadFiltersByNodeKind ' $TMPDIR/kind-filter.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestAKindFilterPutsEachContextNodeOnTheFirstPageThatNamesIt ' $TMPDIR/kind-filter.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q -- '--- SKIP' $TMPDIR/kind-filter.log" when="before_merge" negative_control="Nine controls, run one at a time. First, take `kind=block` as the name of every untyped block. The test prints `kind=block on &lt;key&gt; answered 200, not 400` and fails. Second, answer each node of a named kind with the issue as its parent, dropping its ancestors. The test prints the criterion written under the message, its stored part_of and the parent the read answered, and fails. Third, let the read with kind answer every node of the skeleton. The test prints H2's result, H's result and the plan task, which the conversation's kinds leave out, and fails. Fourth, count in `checks` the checks of the issue itself alone. The test prints R1, its `checks` 1 and the coverage read's 2, and fails. Fifth, let a comment on text bring in the node it is on. The test prints H's result, which the comment on its text brought into the conversation's answer, and fails. Sixth, carry no lens kind in the read with kind. The test prints the lens and its `has_kind` tuple with no lens_kind node in the answer, and fails. Seventh, let `callout` take every callout. The test prints the second callout in the answer of `kind=callout` and fails. Eighth, in `kindOrder` (`api/issue_tree_kinds.go`), answer the constraint that R's `constrained_by` names at its walk place, as this branch's head does. In the read with `kind=requirement`, TestAKindFilterPutsEachContextNodeOnTheFirstPageThatNamesIt prints `the constraint &lt;id&gt; stands on page &lt;n&gt;, and the first page that holds its constrained_by tuple is page &lt;m&gt;` and fails. Ninth, place by its tuple every node a tuple names, a node the read answers as a node of the tree among them. In the read with `kind=requirement&amp;kind=constraint`, TestAKindFilterPutsEachContextNodeOnTheFirstPageThatNamesIt prints `the constraint &lt;id&gt; stands on page &lt;n&gt;, and its walk place falls on page &lt;m&gt;` and fails."}
`TestTheTreeReadFiltersByNodeKind` in `internal/dispatch/api` is new; the implementer writes it with this title. On a test server (`newTestServer`), a person (alice), in the browser, creates an issue born converted whose spec opens with its memo callout and holds a second callout further down. She writes a message and a criterion K1 under it, a comment C and a criterion K2 under it, and an ask A that an agent session asked and she answers. The agent session writes a reading under A, and a decision D with `uncertainty="medium"` and an `uncertainty_reason`. Alice writes a requirement R1 under K1 and a requirement R2 under K2, a constraint of the issue with a `constrained_by` tuple from R1, a check H that serves R1 and R2 with one result recorded on it, a plan task T, a prose block P of the room's own fragment under K1, and a Summary paragraph of the spec. She files a child issue, places it under C through `PATCH`, and gives it a check H2 that serves R1, with one result recorded on it. She invokes a lens on R1 with one finding and one risk, writes a post on the issue tied to no text, to which the agent replies, and comments on the text of H's result through a node anchor (R31). The agent comments on R1's text, and alice writes 205 more posts on the issue. Through `graphstoretest` the test seeds one interaction with a `changed_by_run` tuple from R1.

The test reads `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/tree` with the kinds of the conversation: `kind=callout`, `ask`, `comment`, `reading`, `lens`, `finding`, `risk`, `criterion`, `requirement`, `check`, `decision`, `issue` and `prose`. It asserts by kind and id that the answer is exactly the nodes of those kinds that the read with no view answers, with each ancestor of each, less every callout but the memo: the memo stands first and the second callout is absent; the message stands as context with K1 under it; the posts and the agent's reply stand in it; H2 stands under R1, marked with the child's key, and H2's result is absent; H's result, the comment on its text, T and the Summary paragraph are absent; the agent's comment on R1's text stands under R1 as context; the constraint, the lens's kind and the interaction stand as context, each with its tuple. The answer holds the 200 newest comments it carries and a `comments_before`; the read with that `comments_before` and the same kinds answers the older ones and no other node. It asserts `checks` 2 on R1 and 1 on R2, equal for each to the number of checks `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/coverage` lists under it, on that read, on the read with no view and on `?view=spec`. The read with `kind=check&kind=result` answers H, H2, both results and the comment on H's result's text, under that result. `kind=callout` alone answers the memo alone. `kind=block`, an empty `kind`, `kind=spec`, `kind` beside `view=spec` and `kind` beside `v=1` each answer `400 INVALID_QUERY` naming `kind`. `TestACommentOnANodesTextHangsUnderThatNode` in `internal/dispatch/api` is new. On a test server, a person writes an issue whose spec holds a requirement and whose Verification document holds a check with one result. She invokes a lens on the requirement with one finding and one risk, an author-only lens of her own beside it, and a constraint of the issue. Each of those texts holds the word `bound` twice. She writes one comment through `POST /api/v1/issues/{key}/comments` on each of the lens, the finding, the risk, the constraint and the result, each with an anchor `{node, quote: bound, occurrence: 1}`, the zero-based second match. An agent replies to the comment on the lens. She writes a prose block in the room's own fragment and a comment anchored in it by `artifact`, which names the issue's tree artifact, the row of kind `tree`, and by `block_id`. That write answers `201`, not `400 NOT_DOCUMENT` (R31, new). Through `graphstoretest` the test writes, as a process of the release before would, a comments row anchored in the spec's requirement with no `anchored_in` and no `part_of`, and then runs the backfill's passes.

The read with no view answers each of the five comments under the node its anchor names, each with a `part_of` to that node in the store and an `anchor` holding `node`, `bound`, occurrence 1 and `orphaned` false; the agent's reply under the comment on the lens; the comment on the prose block under that prose block; and the row the backfill levelled under the requirement, with its `anchored_in` and its `part_of`. `comments.node_anchor` holds each node anchor and `comments.anchor` is null on each. The test then appends a finding text value through `graphstoretest` in a transaction that invokes the new node-anchor refresh. The new text holds `bound` once. The test checks the committed `comments.node_anchor.orphaned` value and the retractions of `anchored_in` and the anchor's `part_of` before it makes a tree read. The comments read with `node_anchor=true` answers the stored `orphaned: true`, with the same quote and occurrence. The tree answers the person's comment under the issue. The tree read does not change the stored state. `envoy-dispatch census --store` reads `comment_anchor_block` at zero differences. `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/comments` and `GET /api/v1/comments/{id}` answer each of the five with `anchor` null and no `node_anchor`; the test writes each answer to `NODE_ANCHOR_WIRE` for `CommentSchema`, and the payload of each `comment.created` event the writes appended for `WrittenCommentEventPayloadSchema` (strict, stripping only `main`'s own three routing members that `main`'s server emits and `main`'s strict schema does not declare: `suppress_route`, `suppressed_route` and `suppressed_route_session_id`, so any new key this branch adds is still refused). With `?node_anchor=true`, the same reads answer each of the five's `node_anchor`, its node, quote, occurrence and `orphaned`, which the test parses with this branch's `CommentWithNodeAnchorSchema`. Each of these answers `400 INVALID_ANCHOR` naming its field and writes no comment, which the comments read's count shows: `artifact` beside `node`; neither; `block_id` beside `node`; a `node` that is a requirement block; the author-only lens; a `gone` lens; a quote the node's text does not hold.

The quote matches the plain text of the node's own `text` (R31, new). She writes a second finding of the lens, whose text is `the **upper** bound of [the pool](https://example.com/pool)`. She writes a comment on that finding with an anchor `{node, quote: "upper bound of the pool"}`. The quote crosses the bold and the link of the finding's Markdown source and stands in the finding's plain text, so the write answers `201`. The read with no view answers that comment under the finding, with its `anchor` quote `upper bound of the pool` and `orphaned` false. Only the node's own `text` is quotable. The risk's `early_warning` holds the words `invoice grows`, and its heading, the risk's text, does not hold them. A comment on the risk with an anchor `{node, quote: "invoice grows"}` answers `400 INVALID_ANCHOR`, naming `quote`, and writes no comment, which the comments read's count shows. Else the test prints `quote across inline Markdown of <finding> answered <status> <code>, want 201`, or `quote of the early_warning of <risk> answered <status>, want 400 INVALID_ANCHOR`, and fails.

The comment page of `order=activity` answers the node anchor where this branch's base holds that page (R31, dispatch://TREE-13/spec#b-r-node-anchor). The test first sends `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/comments?order=activity`. Where the answer is a JSON list, as on a base without dispatch://TREE-13, the case logs `c-node-anchor: the base holds no order=activity comment page, so TREE-13 carries the node-anchored page`, and it asserts nothing more. Where the answer is the object `{threads, before, remaining}`, the case reads that page as alice twice, without and with `node_anchor=true`. Without the parameter, each of the five threads whose first comment has a node anchor answers that comment with `anchor` null and no `node_anchor`. With it, the page answers each of those comments' `node_anchor`, its node, quote, occurrence and `orphaned`. Both reads answer the same threads in the same order and the same `remaining`, so a comment with a node anchor counts as any other comment. The two reads answer different ETags, and the read with `node_anchor=true` that sends the other read's ETag in `If-None-Match` answers `200` with its page, not `304`. An agent session (`sessionActor` in `api/interactions_test.go`) then writes a comment on the constraint with a node anchor, and no person replies to it. `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/comments?order=activity&person=in` holds that agent's thread, because a comment thread whose first comment has a node anchor is a comment thread on text (dispatch://TREE-13/spec#b-r-person-comments). Else the test prints the read, what it answered and what it wants, and fails.

The tree read answers a document anchor's zero-based `occurrence` within its block (R31, new). She writes a paragraph of the spec that holds the word `limit` twice. She writes one comment anchored in it by `artifact`, `block_id` and `{quote: limit, occurrence: 1}`, the second `limit`, and a second comment anchored in it with `occurrence: 0`, the first. The read with no view answers the first comment's `anchor` with `occurrence` 1 and the second's with `occurrence` 0, beside their `block_id` and `quote`. The comments read answers neither with an `occurrence`, since `model.Anchor` stores none. She then edits the paragraph so that it holds the word `limit` once, the first, which orphans the first comment's mark. The read with no view then answers the first comment's `anchor` with `orphaned` true and no `occurrence`, and the second's with `occurrence` 0. Else the test prints `the tree read answers the anchor of <comment> with occurrence <n>, want <m>`, or `with no occurrence`, and fails.

The run compares the comments read with the strict schemas of `main` in a worktree of `origin/main`. It does that through a script this child adds, `packages/contracts/scripts/wire-against-main.ts`. The script reads one JSON value per line, parses each with the schema the line names, and prints `PASS: wire-against-main <n>`, or each line it refused with the schema's issue.

The test also creates a pre-mortem document with a risk and anchors a person's comment in a block of that document. It snapshots the comment's anchor, `anchored_in` and `part_of`. It sends `POST /api/v1/issues/{key}/artifacts/{slug}/premortem-convert`. After the conversion all three facts still name the original block. Only the document's address redirects to the lens. The skeleton shows the comment under the issue, with the anchor still naming the block. The comments read lists the comment. No comment moves to a risk.

`TestANodeAnchorOutlivesARollAndARollback` in `internal/dispatch/api` is new, a `basebuild` test, the tag this tree's children give their Go tests that build an earlier commit. It fails, and never skips, where `BASELINE_SHA` is unset or names no 40-character commit. It uses the preamble's `BASELINE_SHA` from the pull request body. It boots the build at `BASELINE_SHA`, the release before, beside this build over an empty database (as a roll in progress does, since with only this build up R5 creates the issue born converted and the release before refuses a comment on a born-converted spec with `409 DOC_SCHEMA`), writes an issue with a lens and a comment on the lens's text by node anchor through this build, and through the release before reads `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/comments`, which answers the comment with `anchor: null`; posts a comment with `node` to it, which answers `400 INVALID_ANCHOR` and writes nothing; and writes a comment anchored in the spec's requirement by `artifact` and `block_id`. It stops this build, so the release before serves alone, as after a rollback, and writes one more such comment through it. It boots this build again. The driver runs against the `dispatch:local` server of this document's preamble, because it seeds every issue it reads at this head and reads no row an earlier release wrote. `e2e/acceptance/coverage-states.sh` is new here.

The read says what proves a requirement and what does not. The driver seeds four requirements. The first has no check at all. The second has a check with no result. The third has a check whose newest result is a fail. The fourth has a check whose passing result was recorded against a text sum the check no longer holds. The driver makes that fourth case by editing the check after the result. It reads the four back as a gap, as unproven, as unproven, and as unproven. It reads a fifth requirement whose check holds a passing result against its current text, and reads that one proved. The broken state this case fails on is a build that counts any attached result as proof. That shows as the third and fourth requirements reading proved. It then retracts the fifth requirement's passing result through `POST /api/v1/results/{id}/retract`, with a reason. It reads that requirement uncovered, as unproven, because coverage counts a retracted result as no result. It reads the result node unchanged, with the reason as an appended value of its `retracted` attribute, and its `check_results` row unchanged.

The answer comes from the authoritative tuples and from no second cache. The driver retracts one `serves` tuple directly in the store. It reads the coverage answer losing that pairing on the next read, with no index rebuilt and no pass run. It appends the tuple again and reads the pairing back. A build that answers from a second stored copy fails here, because the answer does not follow the tuple.

It then deletes the serving check and reads the requirement uncovered again. It seeds a Verification document of more than two thousand blocks, which the write leaves to the reconciliation (`deferBlockIndexBlocks`). The write still writes each check's node and its `serves` tuples at once (R8). So right after the write, with no wait, the driver reads both checks listed by the coverage read, each with its `serves` tuples, and reads `owed_documents` of the coverage read and of the tree read naming that document and the version whose blocks wait. It then waits until `document_block_versions.version` of that document is not null. It polls every 2 s and fails after 300 s. It then reads both checks listed in tree order, each with its `serves` tuples, and no `owed_documents`. So the deferred write writes the checks and their tuples at once, and the reconciliation writes the rest.
