All five are open and in K, and each has a title and a body of its own words. It seeds A, open, in K, under P and blocked by X. It seeds B, `done`, in K and under P. It seeds R, `done`, filed from M through `--filed-from`. It then creates three open issues in this order: C, whose body is the canonical reference of M; H, filed from M; and Y, under N through `--parent`. Each of H, Y and R has a title and a body of its own words. It then writes updates, each a change of priority through `dispatch issue-update --priority`, which changes no word and no target, in this order: H, C and Y, and last P, X, N, Q and L. R gets no update: the driver closes it when it seeds it, so its close is older than the updates of H, C and Y. A and B get no update either, and their places do not depend on the order of the updates: A shares three targets and comes first, and B is the one done issue inside the five. Among C, H and Y, Y holds the newest update, then C, then H, and that order is not the order in which the driver created them. The five issues D links hold the newest updates. It creates a second project through `POST /api/v1/projects`, with `default_assignee` set to `alice`, as this document's preamble creates a project. In that project it seeds E, open, whose body is the canonical reference of M. It then creates D with `dispatch issue`: in K, under P, blocked by X, filed from M and a duplicate of Q, through `--components-json`, `--parent`, `--blocked-by`, `--filed-from` and `--duplicate-of`. D's spec body holds the reference of N and words of its own.

D's output names five neighbours, in this order: A, then Y, C and H, then B. The shared targets of each line are K, P and X for A, N for Y, M for each of C and H, and K and P for B, and the driver compares each line's shared targets with that set, exactly. Y inherits K from its parent N, but R24 counts an issue's own components alone, the ones its `affects` tuples name, so Y's set stays N. So a build that ignores blockers prints A with K and P alone, and a build that ignores a mention on either side, parents, components or filing origins prints a wrong set or a wrong order. Each fails. Open issues come before done ones: a build that orders by the shared count alone puts B second, and a build that leaves done issues out prints four lines. Each fails. Y, C and H share one target each, and the issue with the newer update comes first, so a build that breaks the tie by the time of creation or by the key fails. R, `done`, shares one target, M. It is the sixth candidate, and it is named nowhere, which proves the cap of five. Each line gives the issue's key, its status, its title, the shared targets and a link. No neighbour line names P, X, N, Q or L, which D already links, and the driver reads each one absent. Each of those five is open, shares K with D, and holds a newer update than Y, so a build without the rule of R24 that leaves them out names them after A and ahead of Y, and fails. The output names E nowhere, because E is an issue of another project.

It then seeds F, open, with a title of its own words and no graph target that D shares. It creates G with `dispatch issue --force`, and the title of G repeats the title words of F. `--force` keeps the near-copy gate from refusing G. The driver reads F named in the text lines of G's output, as today's text check names it. So the graph score stands beside the text search, and not in its place. G has no graph target, so the neighbourhood read of G finds no candidate, and the driver reads in G's output the line that says it found none.

It then makes the server's two test hooks hold the neighbourhood read for 15 s and the related search for 4 s, and creates one more issue, T, in K, with `dispatch issue`. This branch adds both hooks under `/_test/`, mounted only under `DISPATCH_TEST_HOOKS`, which `e2e/run-server.sh` sets for the server `bun run dispatch:local` starts. The driver records the time just before it starts the command, and it times the command's wall time. While the command runs, a second process of the driver lists the project's issues through `GET /api/v1/issues?project=CORE` every 100 ms. It finds T within 1 s of the command's start, so the create's write committed before either read ran. The command answers in at most the related search's allowance, 5 s, plus 2 s, which is 7 s. Its output holds the lines of the related search and the line that says the neighbourhood check did not run. A build that runs the two reads one after the other, each under an allowance of its own, takes at least 9 s, and fails. A build that runs them one after the other under one shared allowance answers in 5 s as a correct build does, and this run does not tell it apart. The driver and the server run on one host, so their clocks agree.

Last it runs `dispatch read --issue` on D. Within the `Links:` section it finds `child_of` P, `needs` X, `filed_from` M, `duplicate_of` Q and `affects` K, each exactly once, which proves a `filed_from` to an ask. D's mention of N is not in that section, because D's spec, and not D, holds it. The driver reads that the `Components:` line of the header names K and that the `Node:` line of the read's graph sections names P, as they do today. It counts nothing on those two lines for the rule of once within `Links:`.

The run proves the driver executed, because the command reads its closing `PASS: duplicate-neighbourhood.sh complete` line out of the kept output and fails on any `SKIP` line.
:::

:::check{#c-settlement-reads-back serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-versions-read-back" surface="api" run="cd packages/envoy &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; go test ./internal/dispatch/api/... -run '^TestABrowserEditThatDoesNotReadBackStoresNoVersion$' -count=1 -v 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/TestABrowserEditThatDoesNotReadBackStoresNoVersion.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestABrowserEditThatDoesNotReadBackStoresNoVersion ' $TMPDIR/TestABrowserEditThatDoesNotReadBackStoresNoVersion.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q -- '--- SKIP' $TMPDIR/TestABrowserEditThatDoesNotReadBackStoresNoVersion.log" when="before_merge" negative_control="Two controls, run one at a time. Second, let the conversion convert an issue whose newest spec version does not read back. The test reads that issue converted and fails naming it."}
The test seeds a spec holding a callout inside a list item, and connects a browser peer to its document socket, as `TestABrowserEditCanStoreAVersionThatDispatchCannotRead` of cybermonklabs/legion#4179 does. The peer moves the callout's text into a footnote definition inside the callout and closes its connection. Unless the renderer renders that tree in a form that reads back as the same tree, the artifact then holds no version 2, the log holds the settlement's line naming the room and the parser's error, and the newest version reads back through `pmdoc.ParseRendering`. The peer then moves the text back out of the footnote definition, changes one word of it so the markdown differs from version 1's, and closes again, and the artifact holds a version 2 that reads back and holds that word. Where the renderer does render that tree readably, the test reads version 2 stored and reading back as the edited tree instead.

The test then writes, straight into `artifact_versions`, a newest spec version of a second issue that the parser refuses, and runs the conversion. The conversion passes over that issue with the parser's error in its log line and converts the other issue. The run proves this test executed: it greps the run's own log for this test's `--- PASS:` line and fails on any `--- SKIP` line.
:::

:::check{#c-conversation-holds-the-discussion serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-queries dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-conversation-parent dispatch://TREE-1/spec#b-r-document-tree" surface="cli" run="cd packages/dispatch &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; DATABASE_URL=$INFRA_1253_DATABASE_URL DISPATCH_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8777 DISPATCH_TOKEN=e2e-token PROJECT=CORE DEV_SIGNIN_LOGIN=alice bash e2e/acceptance/conversation-view.sh 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/conversation-view.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^PASS: conversation-view.sh complete ' $TMPDIR/conversation-view.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q '^SKIP' $TMPDIR/conversation-view.log" when="before_merge" negative_control="Five controls, run one at a time. First, let a document version into the conversation graph. The driver prints that version's kind and id as a node the graph must not hold, and fails. Second, drop the remark nobody answered. The driver prints the missing prose node by its id and fails, so a graph that keeps only what produced something cannot pass. Third, let the spec query take every callout of the issue. Its ?view=spec answers the second callout, and the driver exits non-zero naming that callout's id. Fourth, judge a message of a thread the daemon began as `messageConversationStatement` does at 846bc799b13, which refuses only the daemon's own message and passes a person's reply on its thread. The driver prints the person's reply in the daemon's thread as a node the graph must not hold, with its id and its root, and fails. Fifth, answer the agent's comment on the requirement's text as a node of the tree, not as context. The driver prints the comment with its role and fails."}
The conversation view answers the discussion and nothing else. The driver seeds one issue carrying every node kind this model holds: a thread of comments with replies that a person wrote as `DEV_SIGNIN_LOGIN`, an ask with its answer, a remark nobody answered, a criterion the person wrote in that exchange, a requirement under that criterion, a decision an agent recorded with its `shaped` tuple to the requirement, a check and a plan task that serve it, a person's approval of the spec, two documents with several versions each, and a child issue. It reads the conversation graph and asserts by kind that it answers the comments, the asks with each answer held on its ask, the replies, the remark, the criterion, the requirement, the decision, the check and the plan task, because a requirement, a decision, a criterion and an element of the plan are revealed by going down the discussion and are nodes of that graph. It also seeds a message the Legion daemon's own session posts on the issue, and asserts that the conversation graph does not answer it, while the issue's messages still hold it. It seeds an agent's status comment at the top of the issue and an agent's reply inside a thread a person started, and asserts the tree leaves out the first and answers the second, while the issue's comments hold both. It seeds a message thread whose root the Legion daemon's session `legion-daemon:CORE` posts, a reply in that thread that the person writes as `DEV_SIGNIN_LOGIN`, and a reply in it by an agent session, and asserts that the conversation graph answers none of the three, with no view and with `kind=message`, while the issue's messages hold all three. It seeds an agent's comment on the requirement's text that no person answered, and asserts the tree answers it under the requirement as context and answers no node under it other than the comment's own blocks (`comment_block` nodes under `comment/<id>#`, R14/R30). It seeds the spec's Summary paragraph as a prose block of the spec document, and asserts the tree does not answer it, while its document version still renders it. It seeds the spec's first callout as its three-thing memo. It asserts the tree answers that `callout` node first, that `?view=spec` answers it first as a node of the query, and that a change to one of its three sentences moves the digest the spec approval records. The seed also holds a second callout, which is not the issue's first child. `?view=spec` does not answer that callout, and an edit of it moves no spec digest. A third issue's first child is a paragraph, and the issue holds a callout after it. Its `?view=spec` answers no callout at all. It makes every read of the tree through `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/tree`. It also seeds a second issue with as many role-document blocks, other-document blocks, comments, asks and messages as the largest of the ten issues R8 measures. Where that issue holds no other document, the seed still holds one other document of 1,000 blocks, so that the read below runs. The pull request body records those counts, and the driver holds them as constants. It reads that issue with no view and follows the node cursor to the end, without changing its comment cursor. Each response is at most 2,000,000 uncompressed bytes. That read answers the issue's skeleton, with its conversation and its newest 200 comments (R8). The driver then reads the older comments through `comments_before`, one page at a time, until `comments_before` is null. It asserts that the pages hold each of the issue's comments once. The driver reads the blocks of that issue's other documents, which R8 defines, through `GET /api/v1/artifacts/{id}/blocks`, for each such document that `document_nodes` lists. It asserts that each such read lists as many blocks as that document's `block_count`. It prints the page size, the node count, the number of comment pages and the number of blocks it read through the blocks read. It gives the seeded child issue an ask, and reads that ask in the child's tree, as a conversation node of that child. An answer is no kind of its own, because dispatch://TREE-1 R21 holds it as attribute tuples of its ask. It asserts that the conversation answers no artifact, no document version and no prose block of a role document, all of which are nodes of the issue and are reachable from it, so the assertion can fail and does when any is let in. It asserts nothing about a claim or a status move, because this model has no such node kind for one to appear as: a check that forbids what cannot exist proves nothing. It asserts nothing about a handoff either, because at this child's head no handoff node exists: dispatch://TREE-9 creates that kind after this child merges, and that issue proves the tree walk leaves it out. A node the tree must leave out, if it is in the answer, is printed with its kind and its id, and the driver fails. It asserts in the same read that a remark nobody answered, which produced no requirement and no decision, is present as a node of its own, since plain prose is a node and a view that drops it has made the discussion tidier than it was.
:::

The deployment runs this same read before the image switch. This test does not read production.

The walk and the tree read then answer the three seeded nodes and the lens under the step, and TestTheTreeWalkLeavesOutTheWorkflowsRecords fails, printing `the walk of &lt;key&gt; answers the step node &lt;id&gt;`. Thirteenth, answer QUERY_VERSION_NOT_FOUND for every version that holds no read_seq, as issueTreeCut does at 0f722e15. TestAQueryVersionWithNoRecordedRevisionAnswersNotRecorded then fails, printing `the spec query of &lt;key&gt; answers 404 QUERY_VERSION_NOT_FOUND at version 1, which it holds with no recorded revision, want 404 QUERY_VERSION_NOT_RECORDED`. TestTheDecisionsViewAnswersTheDecisionsQuery fails printing `&lt;case&gt;: ?view=decisions answers the reading &lt;address&gt; of the entry &lt;ask&gt; as null, want it once, the query's, under that entry's node`. The driver runs against the `dispatch:local` server of this document's preamble, because it seeds every issue it reads at this head. `e2e/acceptance/tree-read-views.sh` is new here. It makes every read of the tree through `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/tree`.

The driver seeds, writing as `DEV_SIGNIN_LOGIN` where a person writes, one issue holding a comment thread a person wrote, a criterion under it, a requirement under that criterion, a decision an agent recorded with its `shaped` tuple to the requirement and a reading under that decision, a constraint the requirement's `constrained_by` names, a check that serves the requirement with one result, a plan task that serves it, an ask alice answered, with an agent's reading under that answered ask, and a person's approval of the verification query. It seeds a child issue holding a plan task and a check that serve the parent's requirement, the check with one result. Both hang from the child issue, because they serve no requirement of their own issue.

It reads `converted: true` for the seeded issue, which was born converted. Its `?view=spec` answers, as context, the decision whose `shaped` tuple names the requirement and the constraint the requirement's `constrained_by` names. The driver also writes, through dispatch://TREE-6's write routes, a lens of kind `pre-mortem` on the requirement with its `has_kind` tuple. The tree read with no view answers that lens as the tree's node, and, marked as context, the `pre-mortem` `lens_kind` node and the constraint, each with its `has_kind` or `constrained_by` tuple; it answers no other `lens_kind` or `constraint` node of the catalogue. The requirement's constraint is not the `pre-mortem` kind's source constraint, and the driver reads that source constraint absent, because a context node brings in no further context; it also seeds a second constraint that nothing names and reads it absent. It then retracts that `shaped` tuple and reads `?view=spec&v=` at the earlier version. That answer still holds the tie, while the current answer does not, and a version the query does not have answers `404 QUERY_VERSION_NOT_FOUND`. On the seeded issue, which holds a child, `?view=plan` answers the child's plan task with the parent's own, in one order, each marked with its issue. Its `?view=verification` answers, through `serves`, the child's check that serves the parent's requirement, with its result, marked with the child, and with that requirement as the check's parent in the answer (R30, while its stored `part_of` hangs from the child issue under R3). The parent's coverage reads that requirement as covered. The parent's tree read with no view answers the child's plan task through its `serves` tuple to the parent's requirement, marked with the child, and with the child issue as its parent. The driver gives that child plan task the block id of one of the parent's own plan tasks, and a `needs` tuple of its own; the read answers the two plan tasks with different `id`s and the same `block_id`, and each `serves` and `needs` tuple names its ends by those `id`s, so the driver tells the child's tuples from the parent's. Each view answers exactly its fixed kinds and context, and each node carries its parent's id, supertag and first line. Every node of the read with no view carries `visibility` and `made_at`: the comment thread reads `project` and the time the driver wrote it, within one second, and the lens reads the visibility the driver wrote it with. Each node also carries `text_tree`, and for the requirement, the comment that heads the thread and the decision it equals byte for byte the display tree that kind's own read answers (`GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/artifacts/{slug}/blocks`, the comment read and the decisions read). The driver then seeds a second issue it does not convert, whose spec holds a requirement it sets `proposed` and whose Verification document holds a check it sets `overtaken`, through dispatch://TREE-6's `/state` route. The driver also writes, as alice, a comment anchored inside the paragraph of the decision, by its quote and the decision's `block_id`, after it has written the same quote once more in a block above the decision, so only the block names the place, and then two more comments on the issue, writing again until the later one's id sorts below the earlier one's. The read with no view answers the anchored comment with the decision as its `parent`, answers the two comments ahead of the issue's ranked children other than its memo callout, in the order they were written, and answers the decision with its review state, as `?view=decisions` does. The driver then keeps the decision as alice through the Keep route with the `text_sha256` that read answered, and the next read answers it `kept` by alice. That read with no view answers on the decision node every member `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/decisions` answers for it, each equal: `changed_at`, `kept` with `kept_by` and `kept_at`, `links` with each link's `stale`, and the rest of `model.Decision`; it answers the decision's `decided_by` tuple with its person as context. On the first issue's check that serves the requirement, it records a result, reads on the result node `verdict`, `retracted` null and `check_sha256` equal to the check node's `text_sha256`, then changes the check's words and reads the check's `text_sha256` and `changed_version` move while the result's `check_sha256` stays; it retracts the result and reads `retracted` with the reason. The driver then changes the words of the requirement that decision's `shaped` tuple names. The next read answers that link `changed_since_tie` true and `stale` false on the decision. The driver then changes the decision's own words. The next read answers that link `stale` true, and `changed_since_tie` still true. Each of these reads answers the link as `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/decisions` answers the same link, member for member. It writes an ask in the spec, answers it as alice, and gives it a `shaped` tuple to the requirement, and `?view=spec` answers that ask as context with the tuple. On the converted issue it writes a comment whose anchor names the converted spec's artifact id, a quote and its `block_id`, and the comment is written and hangs under that block. As alice it then writes a comment on the issue under a command-bar run's header, through dispatch://TREE-6's run route. Alice's read with no view answers that run's `interaction` node as context with the comment's `changed_by_run` tuple to it, and the issue node holds no `changed_by_run` tuple of its own for that run. Bob's read answers the comment and neither the tuple nor the interaction. A further comment whose anchor names the decision's `block_id` with a quote that block does not hold is refused `400 INVALID_ANCHOR` naming `block_id`, and the issue holds no such comment. That issue's tree read answers `converted` false and `tree` null, while the first issue's answers `converted` true and a `tree` equal to the `room` the artifact read answers for each of its documents. The first issue's `view_of` is null. The driver seeds a converted child of the first issue that holds no requirement of its own, reads its `view_of` naming the first issue, and reads a requirement write on it refused `409 REQUIREMENT_BELONGS_TO_ANCESTOR` naming that same issue. It reads `GET /api/v1/artifacts/{tree}` and its `/text` answering 200 for the first issue's tree artifact, the text holding the criterion the driver wrote into the issue, and the issue read's documents list not naming the tree artifact. That issue's tree read with no view answers each of the two block nodes exactly once, under the parent R1 gives it, with the state it was set to, its `visibility`, `made_at` and `text_tree`, and a `document` member naming its document's artifact id and slug with the position the blocks read gives it. Last, the driver signs in as alice and writes an author-only lens on the first issue's requirement and a `project` risk under that lens. Read as alice, the risk's `parent` is the lens. The driver signs bob in through `GET /auth/_dev/signin?login=bob`, which the harness's reset seeds as it seeds alice (the root's `c-visibility` signs both in the same way). Read as bob, the no-view read answers the risk with the requirement as its `parent`, after the requirement's own children, no node, `parent` or tuple in that answer names the hidden lens's id, so neither its `has_kind` nor its `part_of` tuple appears, and its verdict and its findings' text appear nowhere in it. The hidden lens is a `pre-mortem` lens, because the risk route places a risk only under one, so the `pre-mortem` `lens_kind` is in bob's answer once, as the context of the visible lens. `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/decisions` still answers through this release. It answers the same decision nodes, each with the same review state, as `?view=decisions` of the tree read, because both read one query. The script then searches `packages/dispatch/web/src`, `packages/envoy-client/src` and `packages/daemon` for a caller of that route and finds none that is not marked `kept for one release: decisions-route` on its line or the line above, after it finds a planted unmarked caller in a scratch copy of one file, so a search that matched nothing cannot read as a clean tree. The tree read's one answer carries the `serves`, `shaped`, `needs` and `constrained_by` tuples among the nodes it returns, and `?view=plan` carries each plan node's position, needs and size. `?view=verification` answers each check and result marked as the query's and each requirement above them marked as context, and the digest the approval records walks the query's nodes alone: a change to a context requirement's words leaves that digest unchanged. A second result recorded on the child's check leaves that digest unchanged too, because the parent's record holds no node of the child.

It gives the seeded child issue a design block. On the child issue, `?view=spec` answers the child's design blocks and the ancestor's requirements its checks serve, marked as context.

It then reads the spec, verification, plan and decisions views, which are filters of that one graph rather than trees of their own, and asserts each answers its own kinds out of it: the spec view the memo callout first where the issue has one, then the criterion and requirement nodes, the verification view the check and result nodes with each requirement they serve as context, the plan view the plan tasks, and the decisions view the asks with their answers, the decisions and the reading under each decision, a person's answered ask included, with the agent's reading under that answered ask, which the driver reads by its id. It asserts that a node reaches a view only through the graph, so no view answers a node the graph does not, and that the spec view carries under each requirement the decisions an agent annotated as informing it, whether or not those decisions are its parents.

It proves that the walk leaves out the records of the workflow (R8). `TestTheTreeWalkLeavesOutTheWorkflowsRecords` in `internal/dispatch/api`, a Go test the implementer adds, creates through `POST /api/v1/issues` an issue born converted whose spec holds one requirement. In one transaction it first seeds the three types, which no migration of the store holds, through `graphstoretest.SeedSupertags` in `graphstore/graphstoretest/graphstoretest.go`, because the store's writer takes a node only of a type the store holds (`graphstore.ErrSupertagNotHeld`). It then writes one node of each kind `step`, `plan` and `handoff` (`KindStep`, `KindPlan` and `KindHandoff` in `workflowstore/workflowstore.go`) through `graphstore.PlanUncaused` and `graphstore.QueueNodes` in `graphstore/write.go`, which write the nodes and hold their stated tuples for an event, one `part_of` tuple from each node to the issue's node, and appends those tuples with `graphstore.Caused` under the event that created the issue, as `graphcensus/orphans.go` appends a write's tuples after its `QueueNodes`. So the store holds the three as the root's move of the workflow store and dispatch://TREE-9 will write them. It writes one lens node too, visible to the project, a kind the walk answers wherever it reaches one, with its `part_of` tuple to the step node appended the same way. It first reads, in `graph_tuples`, the standing `part_of` tuple from each of the three nodes to the issue's node, so the case proves the walk's rule and not a write that did not land, and fails printing `the store holds no part_of from the <kind> node to <key>` otherwise. It walks the issue's tree at the head (`docs.WalkIssueTree`) and reads `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/tree` with no view. Neither answers the step, the plan, the handoff or the lens, or a tuple that names one, and both answer the requirement. Else the test fails, printing `the walk of <key> answers the <kind> node <id>`, `the tree read of <key> answers the <kind> node <id>`, or `the walk of <key> answers no requirement`.

It proves that a version of a query that holds no recorded revision answers apart from a version the query does not have (R8). `TestAQueryVersionWithNoRecordedRevisionAnswersNotRecorded` in `internal/dispatch/api`, a Go test the implementer adds, runs on a test server built with `newTestServer(t, testServerOptions{settle: time.Hour})`, which starts no block-index reconciliation. It creates through `POST /api/v1/issues` a converted issue whose spec holds a list of 2,000 items (`deferralList` with `itemsOverTheBlockBound` in `api/block_index_deferral_test.go`), so the create defers the spec's index and version 1's `version_renders` row holds no `read_seq`. It reads `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/tree?view=spec&v=1` and gets `404 QUERY_VERSION_NOT_RECORDED`, naming version 1. It writes, by SQL, a version 2 of the issue's spec query node with no `version_renders` row, as a process of the release before writes a version, and reads `&v=2` answer `404 QUERY_VERSION_NOT_RECORDED`, naming version 2. It reads `&v=99`, a version the query node does not have, and gets `404 QUERY_VERSION_NOT_FOUND`. Else the test fails, printing `the spec query of <key> answers <status> <code> at version <n>, which it holds with no recorded revision, want 404 QUERY_VERSION_NOT_RECORDED`, `the refusal of version <n> of the spec query of <key> does not name the version: <body>`, or `the spec query of <key> answers <status> <code> at version 99, which it does not hold, want 404 QUERY_VERSION_NOT_FOUND`.

`TestTheDecisionsViewAnswersTheDecisionsQuery` in `internal/dispatch/api` holds the same rule in Go: `?view=decisions` answers the agent's reading under a person's answered ask once, the query's reading, under the ask's node. The driver also reads the issue's top-level children in the order the read answers them: its comment and its ask first, in the order they were written, then its ranked requirements by rank. It reads a requirement whose `From:` line names that comment under the comment, and exits non-zero naming any node out of that order.
:::

:::check{#c-child-placement serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-queries dispatch://TREE-1/spec#b-r-document-tree" surface="api" run="cd packages/dispatch &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; DATABASE_URL=$INFRA_1253_DATABASE_URL DISPATCH_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8777 DISPATCH_TOKEN=e2e-token PROJECT=CORE DEV_SIGNIN_LOGIN=alice bash e2e/acceptance/child-placement.sh 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/child-placement.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^PASS: child-placement.sh complete ' $TMPDIR/child-placement.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q '^SKIP' $TMPDIR/child-placement.log" when="before_merge" negative_control="Two controls, run one at a time. First, leave the child's part_of to the comment standing when child_of moves it under another parent. The tree read answers the child under the comment of its old parent, and the driver exits non-zero naming the child, the comment and the new parent. Second, answer `placement_seq` null for a child issue that holds no `part_of`, as R8 answered it before this change. The driver reads null where it wants the `seq` of the child's current `child_of`, prints the child and the answer, and exits non-zero."}
The driver runs against the `dispatch:local` server of this document's preamble, because it seeds every issue it reads at this head. `e2e/acceptance/child-placement.sh` is new here.

It seeds, as `DEV_SIGNIN_LOGIN`, one issue with a comment a person wrote, a child issue filed from that comment, a second child with no placement, and a second parent issue outside the first issue's tree.

It places the child issue under the comment that filed it through `PATCH /api/v1/issues/{key}/nodes/{id}` with the body `{parent}` and an `If-Match` naming the node's `placement_seq`, with `{key}` the first issue's key and `{id}` the child issue's store address, percent-encoded as one path segment. It sends that `PATCH` with the browser cookie its dev sign-in as `DEV_SIGNIN_LOGIN` gives. Before that move the child holds `child_of` and no `part_of`, so the tree read answers its `placement_seq` as the `seq` of its current `child_of` tuple, which the driver reads from `graph_tuples` beside it (R8, new). The `PATCH` names that tag and is taken. A repeat of the same `PATCH` with the same tag answers `412 PRECONDITION_FAILED`, because the move wrote the child's first `part_of`, and it moves nothing. It asserts the tree answers the child under that comment. It then moves that placed child under the second parent issue by writing its `child_of`. It reads the child hanging from that new parent issue, with its `part_of` to the comment retracted. The second child, with no placement, hangs from the first issue, and the tree read answers its `placement_seq` as the `seq` of its current `child_of` tuple.
:::

:::check{#c-conversion-scope serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-conversion-scope dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-child-view dispatch://TREE-1/spec#b-r-document-tree" surface="cli" run="cd packages/dispatch &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; DATABASE_URL=$INFRA_1253_UPGRADE_DATABASE_URL DISPATCH_TOKEN=e2e-token PROJECT=CORE DEV_SIGNIN_LOGIN=alice bash e2e/acceptance/conversion-scope.sh 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/conversion-scope.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^PASS: conversion-scope.sh complete ' $TMPDIR/conversion-scope.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q '^SKIP' $TMPDIR/conversion-scope.log" when="before_merge" negative_control="Four controls, run one at a time. First, let the converter rewrite the `done` issue's spec. Its document digest moves, the driver prints each changed document with its issue key and fails. Second, let the conversation view answer a comment an agent wrote. The driver's read of the child's conversation answers the child's agent comment, prints it and fails, so a child drawn into a discussion thread cannot pass. Third, leave one requirement of the in-flight parent hanging under no exchange. The driver's count of redrawn requirements falls short, it prints that requirement's id, and fails, so a half-redrawn parent cannot pass. Fourth, hold the step in the automatic case: boot this head there with DISPATCH_TEST_HOOKS=1 and DISPATCH_TEST_HOLD_ISSUE_ROOM_STEP=1. The driver reads converted: false for the in-flight parent after 300 s, and exits non-zero naming that issue."}
The converter touches the issues it must and leaves the rest exactly as they are. The driver seeds four issues through the base-commit server this document's preamble states, because the documents it converts must be ones the earlier release wrote. The first is `done`, with its spec, plan and Verification documents, one ask and one comment thread a person wrote, and no decisions document, because dispatch://TREE-4 has converted and deleted every one of those before this child opens, and with the decision nodes TREE-4 made of its sections. The second is an in-flight parent with a discussion and three documents. The third is a child of that approved parent, with one comment an agent wrote and no ask. The fourth is a second child of the parent, which holds a requirement node of its own. The driver writes the parent's comments, the done issue's thread and the approval through the base-commit server as `DEV_SIGNIN_LOGIN`, which that server's dev sign-in admits. It records the byte digest of every document of all four, boots this branch's server, and waits for the backfill as this document's preamble states, runs `envoy-dispatch convert-issues --project CORE`, and reads the digests again after. The `done` issue's spec, plan and Verification documents are byte-identical and its room count is unchanged; any difference is printed with the issue key and the document name and fails the run. The in-flight parent is redrawn, and the driver reads every part of it rather than a sample: its discussion is a graph, every requirement and every verification node of it hangs under an exchange that produced it, its spec view answers those nodes and no prose node, and the count of its requirements before and after is equal. The parent's spec was approved by a person before the conversion. After the redraw it still reads approved, by a carried review at the new version, and every requirement's and every check's words read the same as before. A redraw that changes a requirement's words fails this check. The parent's seeded requirements cite, in their `From:` lines, one ask of the parent, one comment of it, and one ask of an unrelated issue. A fourth requirement cites an unrelated issue's ask first and a comment of the parent second, and hangs under that comment. The `done` issue's `?view=decisions` answers its decision nodes, their readings and their review state, though it did not convert. Its tree read answers `converted: false`, its three document ids, its ask and the thread a person wrote in. After the redraw the first two hang under the ask and the comment they cite, the third hangs from the issue, every author reads as before, and the parent holds no criterion node. A redraw that writes a criterion fails this check. A parent left half redrawn, with one requirement hanging under no exchange, is printed by that count and by the orphan's id, and fails. The child has no conversation tree of its own and carries no approval request of its own. The seeded child raised no ask, so the driver asks for the child's conversation view and reads an empty answer. It then reads `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/asks` of the child and finds no ask of kind approval. An ask raised on a child would be in that child's tree, as R23 says and `c-conversation-holds-the-discussion` proves, so the empty answer here is the seed's and not a rule. A planted conversation node under a child, and a planted approval request on a child, are each found by the same two reads, so the absences the check reports are ones its searches could have found.

The second child converts as it stands and is not a view. After the conversion its own requirement node is kept on it, and its spec view answers that requirement as the query's. The driver then proves the automatic case of R6, in a second pass over an emptied `infra_1253_upgrade`. Through the base-commit server it seeds the same four issues, and it keeps that server live. It boots this head beside it without `DISPATCH_TEST_HOLD_ISSUE_ROOM_STEP`, and it runs no command. It waits until this head's log holds two lines in which the step names the live process that lists no `issue_room` and converts nothing. It then reads `converted: false` in the tree read of each of the four issues. It stops the base-commit server. It polls every 2 s, and fails after 300 s, until the tree read answers `converted: true` for the in-flight parent and for each child. It reads `converted: false` for the `done` issue, and finds that issue's documents byte-identical to the capture. It finds in this head's log one line for each issue: converted for the parent and for each child, and passed over, with its reason, for the `done` issue.
:::

:::check{#c-child-view serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-child-view dispatch://TREE-1/spec#b-r-document-tree" surface="api" run="cd packages/envoy &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; go test ./internal/dispatch/api -run '^(TestARequirementPastedIntoAViewIsAGapOfItsOwnKind|TestAChildWhoseSpecIsItsOwnNeverBecomesAView|TestAChildsRequirementWrittenThroughTheRoomMakesItsSpecItsOwn|TestAChildWhoseCreateDeferredItsIndexKeepsItsSpecItsOwn)$' -count=1 -v 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/pasted-requirement.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestARequirementPastedIntoAViewIsAGapOfItsOwnKind ' $TMPDIR/pasted-requirement.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestAChildWhoseSpecIsItsOwnNeverBecomesAView ' $TMPDIR/pasted-requirement.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestAChildsRequirementWrittenThroughTheRoomMakesItsSpecItsOwn ' $TMPDIR/pasted-requirement.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestAChildWhoseCreateDeferredItsIndexKeepsItsSpecItsOwn ' $TMPDIR/pasted-requirement.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q -- '--- SKIP' $TMPDIR/pasted-requirement.log &amp;&amp; cd ../dispatch &amp;&amp; DATABASE_URL=$INFRA_1253_DATABASE_URL DISPATCH_URL=http://127.0.0.1:8777 DISPATCH_TOKEN=e2e-token PROJECT=CORE bash e2e/acceptance/issue-tree-child-view.sh 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/issue-tree-child-view.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^PASS: issue-tree-child-view.sh complete ' $TMPDIR/issue-tree-child-view.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q '^SKIP' $TMPDIR/issue-tree-child-view.log" when="before_merge" negative_control="Five controls, run one at a time. First, let the store accept a requirement node on the first child through any of the four writes. The driver reads that write accepted where it expects 409, and exits non-zero with a FAIL line naming the child, the write and the requirement it wrote. Second, drop the gap kind: let the coverage read and the coverage read over the tuples name no gap for a requirement on a view. The child's coverage then answers no line for the pasted block, and TestARequirementPastedIntoAViewIsAGapOfItsOwnKind fails, printing `the coverage of &lt;child&gt; holds no gap for the pasted requirement &lt;block id&gt;: &lt;gaps&gt;`. Third, set no own-spec mark, neither in a write through the API nor in a pass of the block index. The child of TestAChildWhoseSpecIsItsOwnNeverBecomesAView then becomes a view once its parent takes a requirement: its tree read answers view_of naming the parent and its own requirement reads as the gap, and the test fails, printing `the tree read of &lt;child&gt; answers view_of &lt;parent&gt; after &lt;parent&gt; took a requirement, want null`. Fourth, set the own-spec mark in the writes through the API alone, and in no pass of the block index. The child of TestAChildsRequirementWrittenThroughTheRoomMakesItsSpecItsOwn, whose requirement no write through the API carried, then holds no mark and becomes a view once its parent takes a requirement, and the test fails, printing `the tree read of &lt;child&gt;, whose requirement came through the room, answers view_of &lt;parent&gt; after &lt;parent&gt; took a requirement, want null`. Fifth, set the own-spec mark in the reconciliation's pass alone: in no write through the API, and not in the deferred write's own pass (planTypedPasses in docs/reference_excerpts.go). The create of the child of TestAChildWhoseCreateDeferredItsIndexKeepsItsSpecItsOwn then sets no mark, since its index is deferred and its own typed pass marks nothing, so once its parent takes a requirement the child is a view before the reconciliation runs, and the test fails, printing `the tree read of &lt;child&gt;, whose create deferred its index, answers view_of &lt;parent&gt; before the reconciliation, want null`."}
The driver runs against the `dispatch:local` server of this document's preamble, because it reads the head's own store and boots no earlier release. `e2e/acceptance/issue-tree-child-view.sh` is this child's own driver and is new here.

It seeds a parent with two requirement nodes and a first child whose one check serves the first of them. That check hangs from the first child, because it serves no requirement of its own issue. The parent's `?view=verification` answers it through `serves`, marked with the child. It reads the child's Spec view and finds the first requirement and no other, drawn from the parent, and no requirement node on the child.

It writes a requirement block into the first child's spec through each write of the API that can carry one: an upload of the spec (`POST /api/v1/issues/{key}/artifacts`), each of the two edit routes (`POST /api/v1/artifacts/{id}/edits` and `POST /api/v1/issues/{key}/artifacts/{slug}/edits`), and `POST /api/v1/issues` creating a second child of the parent whose spec holds one. It reads `409 REQUIREMENT_BELONGS_TO_ANCESTOR` naming the parent from each, and no second child created. It then reads the first child and finds it unchanged.

It reads the parent's coverage and finds the first requirement served by the child's check and the second served by nothing. It records a passed result on the child's check. The parent's verification query then stands at the same version, with the same digest `artifact_version_text_sha256` answers for it, because the parent's record holds no node of the child. It records a passed result on a check of the parent that serves the second, and reads every requirement of the parent covered by a passed check.

It seeds another child under an ancestor that is `done`, writes a requirement node on it, and reads the write accepted.

It proves that a requirement block a paste brings into a view stays a requirement node and is shown as a gap of its own kind (R23). `TestARequirementPastedIntoAViewIsAGapOfItsOwnKind` in `internal/dispatch/api`, a Go test the implementer adds, creates through `POST /api/v1/issues` a parent whose spec holds one requirement and a child of it, born converted, whose one check serves that requirement, so the child is a view and its tree read answers `view_of` naming the parent. It connects a browser peer to the child's spec (`connectBrowserPeer` in `api/browser_peer_test.go`) and writes into the spec's fragment a requirement block, the tree a client that skips the editor's creation gate leaves, so no route's check sees it. It settles the child's documents (`SettleIssueDocuments` in `docs/ask_lifecycle.go`), which writes a version of the spec holding the block, and waits until the block index states it. The child's tree read answers the block as a `requirement` node under the child, as its text and its type say. The child's coverage read (`GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/coverage`) answers among its `gaps` the line `<block id> is a requirement on a view`, the coverage read over the tuples answers the same line, and the child's coverage lists no requirement but the parent's that its check serves. The child's tree read still answers `view_of` naming the parent, and a requirement written to the child's spec through `POST /api/v1/artifacts/{id}/edits` after the paste is still refused `409 REQUIREMENT_BELONGS_TO_ANCESTOR` naming the parent, because the pasted requirement does not end the view. Else the test fails, printing `the tree read of <child> answers the pasted block <block id> as <type>, want requirement`, `the coverage of <child> holds no gap for the pasted requirement <block id>: <gaps>`, `the coverage over the tuples of <child> answers <gaps>, want the line <line>`, `the coverage of <child> counts the pasted requirement <block id> as a requirement of the view`, `the tree read of <child> answers view_of <value> after the paste, want <parent>`, or `a requirement write on <child> after the paste answered <status>, want 409 REQUIREMENT_BELONGS_TO_ANCESTOR`.

It proves that a child whose spec is its own never becomes a view (R23). `TestAChildWhoseSpecIsItsOwnNeverBecomesAView` in `internal/dispatch/api`, a Go test the implementer adds, creates through `POST /api/v1/issues` a parent whose spec holds no requirement, and a child of it, born converted, whose spec holds one requirement. The create of the child is taken, because no ancestor of it holds a requirement, so the child is no view, and the create, whose spec holds a requirement, sets the child's own-spec mark in its own transaction, as the pass of the block index that indexes the requirement does again. The parent then takes a requirement, written into its spec through `POST /api/v1/artifacts/{id}/edits`. The child's tree read answers `view_of` null. The child's coverage read (`GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/coverage`) lists the child's own requirement as a requirement of the child, counted as every requirement is, and no line of its `gaps` reads `is a requirement on a view`. A second requirement written to the child's spec through the same route is taken, not refused `409 REQUIREMENT_BELONGS_TO_ANCESTOR`. Else the test fails, printing `the tree read of <child> answers view_of <parent> after <parent> took a requirement, want null`, `the coverage of <child> reads its own requirement <block id> as a gap: <line>`, `the coverage of <child> lists no requirement <block id> of its own: <requirements>`, or `a second requirement write on <child> answered <status>: <body>`.

It proves that a requirement that reaches a child through the room's settlement makes the child's spec its own (R23). `TestAChildsRequirementWrittenThroughTheRoomMakesItsSpecItsOwn` in `internal/dispatch/api`, a Go test the implementer adds, creates through `POST /api/v1/issues` a parent whose spec holds no requirement, and a child of it, born converted, whose spec holds one paragraph and no requirement, so no write through the API sets the child's own-spec mark. It connects a browser peer to the child's spec (`connectBrowserPeer` in `api/browser_peer_test.go`), writes a requirement block into the spec's fragment, settles the child's documents (`SettleIssueDocuments` in `docs/ask_lifecycle.go`), and waits until the block index states the requirement, while no ancestor of the child holds a requirement, so the child is no view and the index pass sets the mark. The parent then takes a requirement, written into its spec through `POST /api/v1/artifacts/{id}/edits`. The child's tree read answers `view_of` null, its coverage read lists the requirement as the child's own, and no line of its `gaps` reads `is a requirement on a view`. Else the test fails, printing `the tree read of <child>, whose requirement came through the room, answers view_of <parent> after <parent> took a requirement, want null`, `the coverage of <child> reads its requirement <block id>, which came through the room, as a gap: <line>`, or `the block index did not state the requirement <block id> of <child> after its settlement`.

It proves that a child whose create defers its index keeps its spec its own (R23). `TestAChildWhoseCreateDeferredItsIndexKeepsItsSpecItsOwn` in `internal/dispatch/api`, a Go test the implementer adds, runs on a test server built with `newTestServer(t, testServerOptions{settle: time.Hour})` (`api/server_test.go`), the seam that holds the block-index reconciliation off: the document service an API test builds starts no reconciliation, which only the server's process starts (`RunBlockIndexReconciliation`, from `cmd/dispatch/main.go`), so no tick runs but the one the test calls through `ReconcileBlockIndex(ctx, docs.BlockIndexCursors{}, nil)`, as `TestADocumentPastTheBlockBoundLeavesItsBlocksToTheReconciliation` in `api/block_index_deferral_test.go` calls it, and the hour's settle delay keeps a settlement of the room from running in between. It creates through `POST /api/v1/issues` a parent whose spec holds no requirement, and a child of it, born converted, whose spec holds a list of 2,000 items (`deferralList` with `itemsOverTheBlockBound` in the same file, 2,001 blocks) and one requirement, so the room holds more blocks than a write indexes in its own request and the create leaves the room's blocks to the reconciliation (R15). It reads the child's spec owed its index (`blockIndexVersion` in that file answers nil), so the case runs inside the window it proves, and fails printing `the create of <child> indexed its blocks in its own request at version <n>, so no index was deferred` otherwise. The create's own write still writes the requirement's node at once (R8), and that write's pass marks the child's spec its own, as the create's own mark does (R23). The parent then takes a requirement, written into its spec through `POST /api/v1/artifacts/{id}/edits`, and the test reads the parent's spec indexed at that version (`requireIndexedAt`), so the parent holds a requirement node while the child's index is still deferred. The child's tree read answers `view_of` null. The test then runs one tick of the reconciliation, reads the child's spec indexed, and reads the child's tree read answer `view_of` null again, its coverage read list the requirement as the child's own, counted as every requirement is, and no line of its `gaps` read `is a requirement on a view`. Else the test fails, printing `the tree read of <child>, whose create deferred its index, answers view_of <parent> before the reconciliation, want null`, `the tree read of <child>, whose create deferred its index, answers view_of <parent> after the reconciliation, want null`, `the coverage of <child> reads its requirement <block id>, whose index the create deferred, as a gap: <line>`, or `the reconciliation left the spec of <child> owed its index`.

Each of those reads prints one `PASS:` or `FAIL:` line, and none of them prints `SKIP`, because every section is one this check depends on.
:::

The run proves the spec executed: it reads the run's own `passed` count and fails on a `skipped`, `flaky` or `failed` count. `e2e/view-requirement-paste.e2e.ts` is this check's own spec and is new here. `openWithCaret` in `e2e/editor.ts` creates an issue of its own (`openIssue`), so the spec opens the case's own issues with `asUser` and `page.goto` and puts the caret with `placeCaret`. The run takes the chromium the preamble installs under `PLAYWRIGHT_BROWSERS_PATH`, and it calls Playwright through `bunx`, as `packages/dispatch/README.md` gives the command, since no step puts `node_modules/.bin` on `PATH`.

It proves that the page's editor makes no requirement block on a view, and makes one on the view's ancestor (R23). `e2e/view-requirement-paste.e2e.ts`, a Playwright spec the implementer adds, creates through the API (`createIssue` in `e2e/api.ts`) a parent whose spec holds the paragraph `Parent words.` and one requirement, and a child of it, born converted, whose spec holds the paragraph `Child words.` and whose one check serves that requirement, so the child's tree read answers `view_of` naming the parent. It signs alice in (`asUser` in `e2e/users.ts`), opens the child's issue page with `page.goto` at `/issues/<child key>`, puts the caret after the words `Child words.` in the spec's editor with `placeCaret` (`e2e/editor.ts`), and pastes a requirement block as an editor's clipboard carries one, its HTML `<section data-proof-block-type="requirement"><p>Pasted words.</p></section>` with its markdown as the plain text, through the `paste` helper of `e2e/editor.ts`. The editor reads the HTML, as it reads every paste that carries HTML, and holds the words `Pasted words.` as text and no `[data-proof-block-type="requirement"]` element. Once the spec's stored text holds those words, the blocks read of the child's spec (`GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/artifacts/{slug}/blocks`) answers no `requirement` block, and the child's coverage read answers no line `<block id> is a requirement on a view`. It then opens the parent's page the same way, puts the caret after `Parent words.`, pastes the same clipboard into the parent's spec, and finds a `[data-proof-block-type="requirement"]` element holding `Pasted words.`, and once the parent's stored spec holds those words, its blocks read answers them as a `requirement` block. Else the test fails, printing `the spec editor of <child> made a requirement block of the paste`, `<child> holds a requirement block after the paste: <block id>`, `the coverage of <child> answers a gap for the paste: <line>`, or `the spec editor of <parent> made no requirement block of the paste`, each naming the issue by its key.
:::

A result is a node. The test records a result through `recordCheckResult` with two screenshots and reads the node back. The node carries ten values. Those are the verdict, the surface, the run, the observed text, the commit, the role, the three counts and the negative control. The check, the recorder, the session and each screenshot are tuples out of the node, one for each. The result points at the check and at no requirement. The test reads that for a check serving three requirements, and finds one result node under one check.

It reads the `check_results` row written in the same transaction and finds every column equal to the node and its tuples. It rolls that transaction back and finds neither the node, nor a tuple, nor the row. The `check_results` rows an earlier release wrote are read by `c-tree-census`, a driver, because a Go test cannot build an earlier commit.

:::check{#c-query-drain serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-reparent-and-state dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-result-node dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-approval-bytes dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-render-at-version" surface="api" run="cd packages/envoy &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL=$LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN go test ./internal/dispatch/api/ -run '^TestIssueQueryMarksDrainAfterCommit$' -count=1 -v 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/TestIssueQueryMarksDrainAfterCommit.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestIssueQueryMarksDrainAfterCommit ' $TMPDIR/TestIssueQueryMarksDrainAfterCommit.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q -- '--- SKIP' $TMPDIR/TestIssueQueryMarksDrainAfterCommit.log &amp;&amp; DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL=$LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN go test ./internal/dispatch/api/ -run '^TestVersionRecordDigestFillsAfterCommit$' -count=1 -v 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/TestVersionRecordDigestFillsAfterCommit.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestVersionRecordDigestFillsAfterCommit ' $TMPDIR/TestVersionRecordDigestFillsAfterCommit.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q -- '--- SKIP' $TMPDIR/TestVersionRecordDigestFillsAfterCommit.log &amp;&amp; DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL=$LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN go test ./internal/dispatch/docs/ -run '^TestTheTreeRendersAPostCutoverVersionFromItsTuples$' -count=1 -v 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/TestTheTreeRendersAPostCutoverVersionFromItsTuples.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestTheTreeRendersAPostCutoverVersionFromItsTuples ' $TMPDIR/TestTheTreeRendersAPostCutoverVersionFromItsTuples.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q -- '--- SKIP' $TMPDIR/TestTheTreeRendersAPostCutoverVersionFromItsTuples.log" when="before_merge" negative_control="Eleven controls, run one at a time. First, leave the newest tuple sequence unset when a `PATCH` at `graphstore.NoEvent` marks the issue. The test prints `PATCH mark cause sequence &lt;got&gt;, want &lt;seq&gt;` and fails. Second, omit the tick's drain. The test prints `issue_query_marks still owed after the tick` with the issue and cause. Third, call the server's local publish of `artifact.version` before the fill. The test prints `artifact.version published locally while its row still owes its digest` with the version. Fourth, omit the tick's repair of digests. The test prints `digest_owed still true after the tick` with the version. Fifth, fill from head instead of the saved cut. The test prints the version and its head digest instead of its saved-cut digest. Sixth, revise and clear a mark while an earlier query digest is still owed. The test prints `query mark cleared with digest_owed=true` with the issue and version. Seventh, omit `artifact.version` for a drained version. The test prints `drained version &lt;n&gt; has no artifact.version event` and fails. Eighth, make a request drain use the first mark's writer. The test prints the writer on the drained version and its event, and the `who` of the `graph_tuples` row at the mark's `greatest_seq`, and fails. Ninth, let `fillOwedDigests` record the digest and append no `artifact.digest`. The test prints `no artifact.digest for &lt;ref&gt;@v&lt;n&gt; after its fill` and fails. Tenth, let `POST /reviews` record an approval of a version whose digest is owed without filling it first. The approve-while-owed case prints `approval of &lt;ref&gt;@v&lt;n&gt; pinned the markdown digest while its digest was owed` and fails. Eleventh, put `result` nodes back into the Verification query. The result case reads a drained version of the Verification query and its `artifact.digest` with `approval_current: false`, prints `a result moved the verification record of &lt;key&gt;`, and fails."}
The implementer adds `TestIssueQueryMarksDrainAfterCommit` and `TestVersionRecordDigestFillsAfterCommit` in `internal/dispatch/api`. The cases use a converted issue and the real write routes through `newTestServer`. The tests stop at the transaction and publish boundaries through hooks. They read committed rows on a separate connection. They do not infer the order from elapsed time or from the order of event ids.

`TestIssueQueryMarksDrainAfterCommit` drives a node `PATCH`, a node `DELETE`, a result record and a result retract on converted issues. The node `PATCH` and the node `DELETE` each change a query answer. The result record and the result retract change none, because the Verification query takes `check` nodes alone. Its trace shows that each write batch inserts or updates `issue_query_marks` and does not insert a drained query version. On a separate connection just after COMMIT, the change and mark are visible but no new query version is. The routes' own node tuples and states use `graphstore.NoEvent`; for a `DELETE` that removes a block from a document's text, that document's version index pass states the removed block `gone` under the version's `artifact.version` event. For a `PATCH` or a `DELETE` that writes no document version, the mark's `greatest_seq` names the newest tuple sequence and `greatest_event` is null; for a `DELETE` that writes a document version, the mark may also carry that version's `artifact.version` in `greatest_event`. A result record or retract puts its event id in `greatest_event`. Check separately the `artifact.version` events of any document versions the DELETE itself writes.

The trace shows the drain first commits each owed fill under the owner lock, then opens the revision transaction. That transaction takes `store.LockOwner` before `docs.LockQueryRooms`. It reads before its batch, then commits the versions with their digests, appends each version's `artifact.digest` after its `artifact.version`, and clears the mark. Every new version appends `artifact.version` and advances an open request to the new version. The drain writes no carried review, and the earlier approval reads changed since, with `approval_current: false` on the version's `artifact.digest`. In a separate case a result is recorded on an approved Verification document and then retracted. The drain clears each mark and writes no version of the Verification query. The Verification digest stays where it was, the approval still reads current, and no `artifact.approved` and no carried review is written. Its facts use `greatest_event` as `source_event`, or `graphstore.NoEvent` if `greatest_event` is null.

For each node route, check at `api/server.go`'s local `publish` that the version and event are committed, the request names the new version and the mark is gone. For each result route, check there that the mark is gone and that no query version was written. The outbox may publish committed events earlier. Suppress the request drain and send a `PATCH` followed by a result to the same issue. Read both cause columns on the same mark: the result's event id and the greatest tuple sequence of either write. The test observes order by `greatest_seq`. The tick through `docs.Service.ReconcileBlockIndex` writes the version for the final state under the result event, advances the request and clears the mark. Test two eventless marks too. A second tick with no new mark adds no version.

`TestVersionRecordDigestFillsAfterCommit` writes a version with a query record. Pause after COMMIT and before the fill. The committed `version_renders` row holds `at` and `read_seq`, with `record_sha256` null and `digest_owed` true. `artifact_version_text_sha256` returns the SHA-256 of the stored markdown. Change the head record before releasing the fill. It commits the digest at the saved cut and sets `digest_owed` false. It does so before local publication of `artifact.version`. The function then returns that record digest. While the fill is paused, `GET /api/v1/artifacts/{id}` answers `digest_owed: true` and `current_sha256` on its `approval`; after it, `digest_owed: false` and `current_sha256` equal to the record digest. The fill appends one `artifact.digest` carrying `artifact_id`, `name`, `version`, `content_sha256`, `approval_current`, `approved_version` and `approved_sha256`, with `approval_current` as `ApprovalStand.Approves` reads it, and it appends no `artifact.approved`.

Repeat with the request fill suppressed. The reconciliation tick fills the owed row at its saved cut and appends its `artifact.digest`. In a separate drain case, leave a query version's digest owed before a marked change. Hold the fill and check that the drain neither revises nor clears the mark while it waits. Release the fill. Read its separate COMMIT before the drain acquires its revision locks, revises and clears the mark. No drain transaction holds a lock that the fill needs. Distinguish rows with a null digest by `at`, `digest_owed` and `tree_mismatch`. A row with `at` set and no query record has `digest_owed` false. A deferred row has no `at` and no mismatch. A mismatch row has no `at` and `tree_mismatch` true (`TestTheTreeRendersAPostCutoverVersionFromItsTuples` in `internal/dispatch/docs`, which this check's `run` also executes). The digest fill does not consume either kind of row with no `at`: that `docs` test also asserts that running the fill over a `tree_mismatch` row leaves `at` null and `tree_mismatch` true.

In the approve-while-owed case, a person approves that version through `POST /reviews` after COMMIT and before the fill. The route fills the owed digest first, so the row reads `digest_owed` false before the review is written and the review pins the record digest at its insert. No carried review is written for it, and the only `artifact.approved` is the person's own. The current approval reads approved. Repeat with the request fill and the tick both suppressed, so the route's own fill is the only one.

On a converted query document a write under an approval carries nothing in its batch. A prose edit under an approved spec, paused before its fill, has written no review, no `artifact_review_carries` row and no `artifact.approved`; after the fill its `artifact.digest` reads `approval_current: true`. The cutover carry of R14 is the one carry a batch still holds. It starts pinned to the markdown digest. Pause its fill after COMMIT and record the review, carry row and events. Release the fill and read the record digest on the same review's `artifact_review_carries.record_sha256`. Its original review and digest stay unchanged. No second review and no `artifact.approved` appears, and the fill's one event is its `artifact.digest`. The current approval comparison uses the carry row's digest. Repeat through the tick. A restore of the approved text owes its digest like any other write, and its fill appends `artifact.digest` with `approval_current: true`, as `c-approval-bytes` checks.

Use distinct credentials in the two-write case. Hold the first request before revision, then record the second mark. A request's drain writes the newest marking write's credential on its drained version and on the matching `artifact.version`. It reads that credential from the `who` column of the `graph_tuples` row at the mark's `greatest_seq` (migration `20261109013400_graph_store`). The test reads that row on a separate connection and compares its `who` with the writer of the version and of the event. Do not use the first request's credential merely because its request started the drain. In a separate tick case, leave both marks owed and invoke reconciliation. Its new version and event both name the drain's system actor, of kind `system`, not either request writer.
:::

`TestXidWindowsUnderTheParentStatusRule` prints a PASS and window summaries for create under a parent and close with open asks. `TestXidWindowDeliveries` prints a PASS and the summaries of its delivery steps. Each uses the baseline bound for that step. `TestXidWindowRouteTable` prints a PASS, the route and the measured windows of each row. The upload and edit under an approval request keep `XidBatchedWindow`. The two route-table rows for the upload and edit that restore approved text keep `storetest.XidBatchedWindow`, as the dedicated upload test does. The three issue-create rows changed by `8db5078b518` return to their baseline limits.

The implementer also adds `TestXidWindowsOfTheNodeRoutesTheDrainAndTheFill` in `internal/dispatch/api`. Measure successful node `PATCH` and `DELETE` operations that change a query and writes that run a drain and a fill, including a write under an approved query, which writes no carry. Identify each committed transaction by its statements. Print the operation, the phase and the measured window. The node move has two phases. A flat move writes tuples alone, such as a paragraph indented under a paragraph. A move that Markdown can show also writes a document version under the room locks in the same transaction (R7). Require all five phases to be observed: the flat move, the move that writes a version, node delete, drain and fill. Hold every node `PATCH`, node `DELETE`, drain and fill window to `storetest.XidBatchedWindow`, not the result route's three-statement limit, with no larger window for a node `DELETE` under an approval. The test prints the phase with any window failure.

The run requires each test's own `--- PASS:` and a window summary from `storetest.AssertXidWindows`. The summary records duration, statement count and largest gap. Reject skips or unexpected violations. The four tests that require readable thread clocks run in `c-xid-gap-rig`, not in the pod. Every test in the pod run must print its named PASS with no `--- SKIP`. Record when the rig judges shape alone; that run does not prove the gap bound.

Additional files and tests at `main`'s bounds: `docs/xid_window_test.go`: `TestXidWindowRigPassesBackToBackStatementsAfterTheFirstWrite`, `TestXidWindowSettlementVersionWrite`, `TestXidWindowClosedIssueSettlementVersionWrite`, `TestXidWindowEditNoticeSweep`, `TestXidWindowReconcileTaskProgress`, `TestXidWindowBlockIndexWindowArm`. `docs/anchor_blocks_xid_window_test.go`: `TestXidWindowAnchorBlockBackfill`. `api/issue_ask_repair_xid_window_test.go`: `TestXidWindowIssueAskRepairWithdrawal`, `TestXidWindowIssueAskRepairRestoration`. `delivery/xid_window_test.go`: `TestXidWindowDeployedEventRecorded`, `TestXidWindowAttributionMoveRecorded`. `refs/grammar_reindex_xid_window_test.go`: `TestTheGrammarReindexTakesItsTransactionIdOnlyAtItsWritePhase`.

:::check{#c-shared-id-census serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-move-safe dispatch://TREE-1/spec#b-r-document-tree" surface="api" run="cd packages/dispatch &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; DATABASE_URL=$INFRA_1253_UPGRADE_DATABASE_URL DISPATCH_TOKEN=e2e-token PROJECT=CORE bash e2e/acceptance/issue-tree-census.sh 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/issue-tree-census.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^PASS: issue-tree-census.sh complete ' $TMPDIR/issue-tree-census.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q '^SKIP' $TMPDIR/issue-tree-census.log" when="before_merge" negative_control="Seed one issue whose plan-md and whose verification-md each hold a block with id b-r1, take the fresh-id minting out of the merge, and run it. The merged document then holds two nodes under one id, and the driver states that issue, b-r1 and both nodes, and exits non-zero. The same collision with the minting left in is lawful stored data, because document_blocks is keyed (artifact_id, block_id), so the driver reports the count and exits zero; a control that failed on that state would make lawful data a defect."}
The driver publishes, for the whole instance, the count of block ids that each stand in two or more of three documents of one issue. The three are the documents that move into the issue's room: the spec, `verification-md` and `plan-md`. It states each issue and each id behind a count above zero. The published count includes the seeded issue and `b-r1`; a count without them fails the run. It takes the count twice and compares the two. It takes it once from the stored rows, keyed as `document_blocks` keys them on `(artifact_id, block_id)`, and once from the blocks the server reads back.

The rows it counts are rows the earlier release wrote, in the pod's test PostgreSQL. They are the corpus the base-commit server seeded, which this document's preamble states: issues carrying a spec, a `verification-md` and a `plan-md`, one of them holding the block id `b-r1` in both its `plan-md` and its `verification-md`. A run whose rows this branch's writer made would prove nothing about the ids already stored. So the driver asserts the source of each row it counted and prints it.

That second read is `GET /api/v1/artifacts/{id}/blocks` for the spec, the Verification document and the plan of the same issue, read after the upgrade and before the conversion, once the backfill the preamble states has run. The two counts must agree exactly, so a count taken from rows a converter has already touched cannot pass for the documents' own. The driver also runs the `.census.sql` this child adds beside the migration that makes block ids unique within an issue, the single `select` the repository runs before a deploy, and reads zero from it. It refuses to report a count it took over no issue.

It then converts that issue with `envoy-dispatch convert-issues --project CORE` and reads every block id of the issue's tree once. One `b-r1` keeps its id, the other holds a fresh id, and the old address of each resolves through its `moved_to` tuple.
:::

:::check{#c-redirects serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-move-safe dispatch://TREE-1/spec#b-r-document-tree" surface="api" run="cd packages/dispatch &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; DATABASE_URL=$INFRA_1253_UPGRADE_DATABASE_URL DISPATCH_TOKEN=e2e-token PROJECT=CORE bash e2e/acceptance/issue-tree-redirects.sh 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/issue-tree-redirects.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^PASS: issue-tree-redirects.sh complete ' $TMPDIR/issue-tree-redirects.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q '^SKIP' $TMPDIR/issue-tree-redirects.log" when="before_merge" negative_control="Make the move mint a fresh id for one block whose old id no other block of the issue holds. Leave that block's moved_to tuple out. The room join of moved_to_reach then finds no block of the issue's room under the old id, so it cannot resolve the old address. The unresolved_citations line of envoy-dispatch census --store reads one more than before the move, the citation of that node answers 404 NOT_FOUND, and the driver exits non-zero with the old address."}
No citation of a moved node dangles. The citations it tests were written by the earlier release, through the base-commit server this document's preamble states. So the addresses it resolves are addresses that writer stored. The driver writes a comment there that cites a block of the issue's Verification document. Through that server it also writes the five structured pointers at a block of that document: a `refs` row and a `block_refs` row from the citation, an ask with `block_artifact_id` set on that block, a comment whose `anchor` points at the document, and a result on one of its checks, whose `check_results` row holds the `check_artifact_id` and `check_block_id` pair. It plants one prose `#b-` citation of a block no version holds. It records the text each resolver returned and the five pointer columns, `refs.to_id`, `block_refs.to_id`, `asks.block_artifact_id`, `comments.anchor` and that pair, and stops that server. It boots this branch's server and waits for the backfill as this document's preamble states. Before the move it reads the five pointer columns as it captured them, so no migration rewrote a pointer. It converts the issue with `envoy-dispatch convert-issues --project CORE`, which moves that document's blocks into the issue's tree, and reads the citation again. The citation resolves, it reaches the same block at its new address, and the text it returns equals the text captured before the upgrade. Each of the five pointers is a tuple of the store after the move, each projection row equals its tuple, and each points at the node's new home.

It takes that read four ways: the three resolvers R13 names, and `blockReferenceNode` pinned to a version of the old document. Those are the reference read `blockReferenceNode` in `packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/api/references.go`, the block-link read `refs.BlockLinks` behind `GET /api/v1/block-links`, the issue's reference closure, and the same reference pinned to a version of the old document. It also takes the backlink read `GET /api/v1/references?to=`. The closure takes a target's document out of the node id with `split_part(r.to_id, '#', 1)` in `refs.Closure`'s `documentOfTarget`.

One appended `moved_to` tuple records each pair, the old address and the node, with the time of the move. It runs from the old address to the node, which is the direction dispatch://TREE-4 already writes. The driver reads it once and finds no second row for the same move. Before the first move it resolves one citation of a dispatch://TREE-4 move through each resolver, which is what dispatch://TREE-4 shipped. The dangling-citation counter is the `dangling_citations` line of `envoy-dispatch census --store`, run against `infra_1253_upgrade`. Each run of `census --store` the driver makes also reads the census's line `census: versions …` print `tree_mismatch=0` and `tree_mismatch_repaired=0`, since no writer of the product writes a version whose tree does not render as its stored markdown and the driver drops no update (R16), and the driver exits non-zero printing that line otherwise. After the move it reads the same count as before the move, so no citation this move touched dangles. It is not a whole-instance zero: a healthy instance already carries dangling prose `#b-` citations and blocks whose indexing is deferred, which dispatch://TREE-4's own check measured, so a whole-instance zero is a gate no correct build could pass. This child leaves that line unchanged. That line does not count the planted prose `#b-` citation, as dispatch://TREE-4's `TestTheDanglingCounterReadsBothSetsAroundAMove` asserts. So `census --store` also prints a line of its own, `unresolved_citations n=<n>`, which this child builds. It counts every block citation whose address resolves to no node, and leaves out one whose target is a block of a document that still owes its block index by either mark (R13). So the driver reads `n` only when nothing is owed. Each read follows a wait until `select count(*) from document_block_versions where version is null or store_owed_at is not null` reads 0, polling every 2 s and failing after 300 s: the first read after the preamble's wait for the backfill, and the second after the conversion. Before the move `n` reads 1 or more, counting the planted citation, so a counter that is always zero because it counts nothing fails here. After the move `n` reads the same count, with the planted citation still in it. It also proves the order, because the tuples, the resolvers and the counter answer before the first node moves.
:::

The run proves this test executed. It greps the run's own log for this test's `--- PASS:` line and fails on any `--- SKIP` line, which `storetest.Open` writes when `DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL` is unset.

`TestAMoveOfOneParagraphKeepsEveryBlockID` in `internal/dispatch/api` is new, and this child adds it. `carryBlockIDs` in `pmdoc/carry_block_ids.go` carries an id only to an unchanged block at its paired place on `main` at `f19175da`; at `810aa47b` also to an untyped container kept there though its contents changed (`carryKept`). So a version that moves one paragraph gives a fresh id to that paragraph and to each paragraph it passes: 1,491 fresh ids when paragraph 250 of 2,000 moves to after paragraph 1740.
