A `block_refs` pointer and an ask anchor into a passed paragraph then resolve to nothing (dispatch://TREE-2/artifact/measure-carry-removal-md). This child carries ids by an alignment of the old and the new block sequences, so the moved paragraph and each paragraph it passes keep their ids.

On a server that `newTestServer` starts, the test uploads `big.md` to an issue through `POST /api/v1/issues/{key}/artifacts`: 2,000 paragraphs, each with a text of its own. A document of a second issue cites paragraph 1000 and paragraph 250, each by `dispatch://<key>/artifact/big-md#b-<id>`, which writes a `block_refs` row for each. An ask on the first issue is anchored by quote on paragraph 1200 (`POST /api/v1/issues/{key}/asks`). The test then uploads version 2 through the same route, with the precondition token, with paragraph 250 moved to after paragraph 1740. The move passes paragraphs 251 to 1740, 1,490 paragraphs, and paragraphs 1000 and 1200 are among them. The test then runs the block-index reconciliation (`docs.Service.ReconcileBlockIndex`) until it indexes nothing. It does all of this twice: with the 2,000 paragraphs alone, which the upload indexes itself, and with a heading above them, 2,001 blocks, more than `deferBlockIndexBlocks` in `docs/reference_excerpts.go`, so that the reconciliation indexes them.

After the move, `GET /api/v1/artifacts/{id}/blocks` answers each paragraph, found by its text, under the id it had at version 1, the moved paragraph included. Else the test prints the first passed paragraph whose id changed, as `passed paragraph <n> changed id <old> to <new>`, the count of passed paragraphs whose ids changed, and `moved paragraph 250 changed id <old> to <new>` where the moved paragraph's id changed.

`GET /api/v1/artifacts/{id}/blocks/{block_id}` answers 200 with paragraph 1000 and with paragraph 250 for the id that each `block_refs` row names. `GET /api/v1/asks/{id}` answers `anchor_block` with the block of paragraph 1200. Else the test prints `the block_refs pointer at paragraph <n> answers <status> <code>` or `the ask anchored on paragraph 1200 answers no anchor_block`.

The test counts the rows that the upload and the reconciliation add to `graph_nodes` and to `graph_tuples`. They add no node of kind `block`. Each tuple they append out of a block node is out of the node of the moved paragraph (R1), and each other tuple they append is out of the new version's node. Else the test prints `the move appended <n> tuples out of <m> blocks other than the moved one`. At `810aa47b` the same move appends 16,407 tuples: 11 for each of 1,491 blocks with a fresh id, and 6 for the version.

The test prints the time of the request that uploads version 2. The pull request body gives that time at `main` and at the head, each from one run of this test, on a scratch copy of `main` for the first. At `810aa47b` that request took 18.68 s in one run and 10.82 s in a second, against 0.82 s at `main` (dispatch://TREE-2/artifact/measure-carry-removal-md).
:::

:::check{#c-approval-bytes serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-approval-bytes dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-serves-coverage dispatch://TREE-1/spec#b-r-approval-hash dispatch://TREE-1/spec#b-r-document-tree" surface="cli" run="cd packages/envoy &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; go test ./... -run '^(TestApprovalCoversTheDigestOfOneQuerysRecord|TestTheRecordOfOneNodeIsItsLayoutByteForByte|TestAVersionAnswersTheDigestAnApprovalCovers|TestHashGateEmitsDigestAndDropsSyntheticCarries|TestAPreCutoverRestoreCarriesOnce)$' -count=1 -v 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/approval-bytes.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestApprovalCoversTheDigestOfOneQuerysRecord ' $TMPDIR/approval-bytes.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestTheRecordOfOneNodeIsItsLayoutByteForByte ' $TMPDIR/approval-bytes.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestAVersionAnswersTheDigestAnApprovalCovers ' $TMPDIR/approval-bytes.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestHashGateEmitsDigestAndDropsSyntheticCarries ' $TMPDIR/approval-bytes.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestAPreCutoverRestoreCarriesOnce ' $TMPDIR/approval-bytes.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q -- '--- SKIP' $TMPDIR/approval-bytes.log &amp;&amp; cd ../envoy-client &amp;&amp; bun test src/__tests__/dispatch-execute.test.ts --reporter=junit --reporter-outfile $TMPDIR/approval-bytes-bun.xml 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/approval-bytes-bun.log &amp;&amp; grep -q 'name=&#x22;doc-read names the version bytes, its digest and the approval' $TMPDIR/approval-bytes-bun.xml &amp;&amp; grep -q 'testsuites name=&#x22;bun test&#x22;.*failures=&#x22;0&#x22; skipped=&#x22;0&#x22;' $TMPDIR/approval-bytes-bun.xml" when="before_merge" negative_control="Twenty controls, run one at a time. First, build the record from each node's values and body alone, leaving its tuples out. The test retargets one check's serves pointer, reads the digest unchanged, and fails, printing the two targets and the one digest. Second, append the approves tuples and leave the row's approval.documents empty. The test reads the row beside the tuples and fails, naming the ask and the entry the row lacks. Third, leave visibility and state out of the record's values again, as recordLeftOut leaves them at 325bfe8a2eb9. TestApprovalCoversTheDigestOfOneQuerysRecord changes the visibility value of a check, reads the verification digest unchanged, and fails printing `the verification digest held still across a change of visibility of &lt;node&gt;`. Fourth, write the text value among the values as well as in its own field. TestTheRecordOfOneNodeIsItsLayoutByteForByte fails printing `the spec record of PIN-1 reads &lt;record&gt; want &lt;record&gt;` and `the spec record of PIN-1 digests to &lt;digest&gt;, want &lt;digest&gt;`. Fifth, let refs.TreeNodeType take a block's type from its node's supertag. docs.WalkIssueTree at the cut of the version before the retype types the retyped block as check, and TestApprovalCoversTheDigestOfOneQuerysRecord fails printing `the walk at version &lt;n&gt; types block &lt;address&gt; as check, want requirement`. Sixth, leave placement out of the record's values. TestApprovalCoversTheDigestOfOneQuerysRecord changes the placement value of a check, reads the verification digest unchanged, and fails printing `the verification digest held still across a change of placement of &lt;node&gt;`. Seventh, put `result` nodes back into the Verification query. TestApprovalCoversTheDigestOfOneQuerysRecord records a result on a check, reads the verification digest moved, and fails printing `the verification digest moved across a recorded result &lt;address&gt;`, and the result subtest of TestHashGateEmitsDigestAndDropsSyntheticCarries reads `approval_current: false` and fails. Eighth, take definition_version out of graphstore.QueryNode. TestApprovalCoversTheDigestOfOneQuerysRecord reads the spec query node and fails printing `query node &lt;ref_key&gt; holds definition_version none, want 1`. Ninth, let `ApprovalStand.Approves` ignore definition_version. TestApprovalCoversTheDigestOfOneQuerysRecord reads the verification approval current at the version written after the definition changed, and fails printing `the approval of verification at version &lt;a&gt; reads current at version &lt;b&gt;, whose definition_version is 2, not 1`. Tenth, let owedVersionNodes give VersionFacts the definition_version of the query node as it stands at the run. TestApprovalCoversTheDigestOfOneQuerysRecord fails printing `the query version &lt;id&gt;, which the backfill wrote for a version written before its document was a query, holds definition_version 1, want none`. Eleventh, let the issue create build the owner of a spec's first version with no Query, as createIssue in api/issue_create.go builds it at 325bfe8a2e. TestApprovalCoversTheDigestOfOneQuerysRecord fails printing `the version 1 of &lt;ref_key&gt;, a spec created converted, is a document version holding definition_version none, want a query version holding 1`. Twelfth, leave text_rank and text_parent out of the record: add text_rank to recordLeftOut and write no text_parent relation in the relations field. TestApprovalCoversTheDigestOfOneQuerysRecord moves the requirement before the paragraph in the spec's text, with the tree unchanged, reads the spec digest unchanged, and fails printing `the spec digest held still across a change of text_rank of &lt;node&gt;`. Thirteenth, emit a synthetic text-carry review in Transaction 1 on a converted query document. The one-settlement criterion plus ask-attribute subtest of TestHashGateEmitsDigestAndDropsSyntheticCarries reads an `artifact.approved` for the moved record and fails. Fourteenth, let a restore of the approved text on a converted query document check its record and carry before its COMMIT, as the deleted restore exception did. The restore subtest of TestHashGateEmitsDigestAndDropsSyntheticCarries reads more statements than `storetest.XidBatchedWindow`'s 2, or a synthetic `artifact.approved`, and fails. Fifteenth, let `fillOwedDigests` record the digest and append no `artifact.digest`. Each write subtest of TestHashGateEmitsDigestAndDropsSyntheticCarries fails printing `no artifact.digest for &lt;ref&gt;@v&lt;n&gt; after its fill`. Sixteenth, let `POST /reviews` record an approval without first filling the version's owed digest. The approve-while-owed subtest of TestHashGateEmitsDigestAndDropsSyntheticCarries reads the review pinning the stored markdown's sha256 and fails. Seventeenth, leave `current_sha256` and `digest_owed` off the `approval` of `GET /api/v1/artifacts/{id}`. The artifact-read subtest of TestHashGateEmitsDigestAndDropsSyntheticCarries fails naming the missing member. Eighteenth, let the write's own pass carry a pre-cutover review again. TestAPreCutoverRestoreCarriesOnce fails reading two carried reviews. Nineteenth, let the version read and the version list answer the sha256 of the stored markdown as digest. TestAVersionAnswersTheDigestAnApprovalCovers fails printing `version 1 of the converted spec: the version read answers digest &#x22;&lt;digest&gt;&#x22;, want &lt;digest&gt;` and the same line for `the artifact read's version list`. Twentieth, print the Digest line before the Content line in docReadCommand. The Bun case fails at its `Content:` then `Digest:` assertion (dispatch-execute.test.ts:10259), and the junit file counts one failure."}
The run proves each of the five Go tests and the Bun case executed. It greps the run's own log for the `--- PASS:` line of each test by itself, and fails on any `--- SKIP` line, which `storetest.Open` writes when `DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL` is unset.

An approval covers the digest of one query's record, in the tree's own order. The test seeds an issue, approves its spec query, and reads the review. The review pins `content_sha256`, the digest `artifact_version_text_sha256` takes of that version's record. The test builds the record again and gets that digest.

The test pins the relation facts, which is the gap this case exists for. It retargets one check's `serves` pointer from requirement A to requirement B. It changes no word of any node, no value, no identity and no position in the walk. It reads the verification digest and finds it moved. It reads the standing approval of the verification query stale. The broken state this case fails on is a record built from values and body text alone. The digest holds still there while the claimed coverage has changed.

It takes two more changes the same way. It moves a check under a different requirement, with every word unchanged, and reads the digest moved. It removes a check and reads the digest moved and the approval superseded. It then records a result on a check of the approved Verification document, and later retracts it. After each it reads the verification digest unchanged and the approval of the verification query still current, with no carried review and no `artifact.approved` written, because the verification query takes `check` nodes alone. Else the test prints `the verification digest moved across a recorded result <address>`.

The test pins the order. It reads the record and finds each node before its children, and siblings in increasing rank. It re-ranks two siblings, builds the record again, and reads the two in their new order. It gives two siblings ranks that differ only in case at one position (`a`, `B`) and reads `B` first, because ranks compare byte for byte. The test refuses to run where `select 'a' < 'B'` is false, since such a database cannot tell byte order from its own collation. It writes two siblings holding one rank through the store, builds the record, and reads the lower address first, comparing addresses byte for byte.  It writes a value holding the record's own field separators and a value holding a length prefix of its own. It reads two distinct digests, because each field carries its length. It asserts the head record and the record at the approved version run through one builder.

The test pins current approval, not only the historical review. After each change above that moves the digest, it reads the current query's approval state and finds it unapproved; after the recorded result and its retraction it finds it approved. It then reads the issue read's design gate (`issueDesignGatesStatement`, `api/issue_queries.go`) and calls `docs.NamedDocumentsApproved` (`docs/approval_review.go`), and reads each refused, with the query and the digest it compared quoted. It reads the historical review still approved for its own version at the same time. The broken state this case fails on is a build where the old review stays readable, as required. The application there still treats the changed current query as approved.

The test pins what each query takes. The verification query answers the issue's check nodes alone, and no result node. The spec query answers the memo callout first, where the issue has one, then its criterion and requirement nodes. An edit of one word inside a check node changes the verification digest and leaves the spec approval standing. An edit of a requirement changes the spec digest.

The test pins the move and the column. An approval given before the move still reads approved after it, through the carry Dispatch records in that person's name at the new version, and not through a digest match: a pre-cutover review holds the sha256 of stored markdown, which the length-prefixed record cannot reproduce. The same carry runs for a review whose `content_sha256_source` is `backfill`, so a digest `docs.FillReviewContentHashes` filled at boot decides as one taken at the approval does. A digest comparison applies only to a review taken after the cutover, its version's pass and its digest fill. For such a review the test leaves the query untouched, builds its record again and reads the digest the review already holds. The test reads `artifact_reviews` out of the catalog. It finds `content_sha256` still `text` under the check `^[0-9a-f]{64}$`, with both triggers in place. The migration set runs no statement against that table.

The request's own pointer is a tuple. The test opens an approval request over two queries of one issue. It reads one `approves` tuple per query version node. It reads the `asks` row's `approval.documents` equal to those tuples: one entry for each, holding the artifact uuid and the version integer of that query version node. It reads `asks_approval_kind_check`, `asks_normalize_approval_documents` and its trigger out of the catalog and finds each as the release before left it. It inserts an approval row in the shape the release before writes, and the check admits it. The approval ask's read answers `artifact_id` and `version` equal to the query version node's artifact id and version number, beside `requested_version`. It reads the store revision pinned beside the digest. A person's own answer to an ask block still carries as it does today on an issue that has not converted. After the move it writes no carried review: the answer changes no node the spec query takes, so the approval stands by its unchanged digest. The test takes that case once before the move and once after, and reads the approval standing both times.

The test pins which values the record holds, as R14 states them. It changes the `visibility` value of one check, and reads the verification digest moved and the approval of the verification query stale. It changes the `state` value of another check the same way, with the same reads. It then changes the `placement` value of a third check while that check's `part_of` stays as it was, with the same reads. Else the test prints `the verification digest held still across a change of <attribute> of <node>`.

The test pins the text order, which the tree does not hold (R1, R14). It writes a spec whose text holds a criterion `k1`, a callout, a paragraph, and a requirement whose `parent` attribute names `k1`, and approves the spec query. `k1` is the issue's first child in the tree's order, so the callout is no memo. It then moves the requirement before the paragraph in the spec's text through `POST /api/v1/artifacts/{id}/edits`. The requirement's `part_of` still names `k1`, every rank stands as it stood, and a walk of the tree reads every node in the order it read before. Only the requirement's `text_rank` value moved. The test reads the spec digest moved and the approval of the spec query stale. It approves the spec query again, moves the requirement into the callout's text, again with the tree unchanged, and reads the digest moved and the approval stale again: the requirement's `text_parent` names the callout now. Else the test prints `the spec digest held still across a change of <text_rank|text_parent> of <node>`.

The test pins the type a record gives a block at a cut. It retypes a requirement into a check through a version of the spec, which restates the block's node with the supertag `check` (R26). It then walks the issue's tree with `docs.WalkIssueTree` at the cut of the version before the retype, and reads that block's `TreeNode.Type` as `requirement`, as its text at that cut opens. Else the test prints `the walk at version <n> types block <address> as <type>, want requirement`. It reads the type from the walk because the spec record alone cannot show a wrong type: a block typed `check` is no node the spec query takes, so the record would lose the block rather than state the type. The spec record at that version holds the block, and its digest equals the digest taken at that version. Else the test prints `the spec record at version <n> holds no block <address>`, or `the spec record at version <n> digests to <digest>, want <digest>`.

The test pins the query's version. It reads the `definition_version` value of the issue's spec, verification, plan and decisions query nodes, and finds 1 on each. It approves the spec query, and reads the query version node that the review names by its `artifact_id` and `version`. Through the review's `ask_id` it reads the approval request, whose `approves` tuple names the same node. That node holds `definition_version` 1, and the review holds the digest of that version's record. Else the test prints `query node <ref_key> holds definition_version <value>, want 1`, or `the query version <id> that the review of <ask> names holds definition_version <value>, want 1`, where `<value>` reads `none` for a node that holds no such value. It then creates a second issue at this head, which is born converted, so its spec's node is a query node from the create on. The version 1 of that spec, which the issue create itself writes, carries the supertag `query version` and holds `definition_version` 1. It approves that version 1, and reads the review name that query version node by its `artifact_id` and `version`. Else the test prints `the version 1 of <ref_key>, a spec created converted, is a <supertag> holding definition_version <value>, want a query version holding 1`, or `the review of <ask> names <artifact_id> at version <n>, want version 1 of <ref_key>`. It approves the verification query at its current version, which holds `definition_version` 1. It then restates the verification query node with `definition_version` 2 in the store, edits one paragraph of the Verification document's text, and reads the version that edit writes holding `definition_version` 2. That version's record digest equals the approved one, since no check changed, and the approval of the verification query reads stale all the same, its `artifact.digest` carrying `approval_current: false`, with no carried review. Else the test prints `the approval of verification at version <a> reads current at version <b>, whose definition_version is 2, not 1`. Last, it writes by SQL, in the shape the release before stores, a version of a document of a second issue whose node is no query node and that holds no version node. It then restates that document's node as a query node (`graphstore.QueryNode`) and runs `graphcensus.Backfill`. The version node the backfill writes carries the supertag `query version` and holds no `definition_version`. Else the test prints `the query version <id>, which the backfill wrote for a version written before its document was a query, holds definition_version <value>, want none`.

`TestTheRecordOfOneNodeIsItsLayoutByteForByte` in `internal/dispatch/api` pins one node's record byte for byte. It writes a tree of one requirement whose every value is written straight into the store, `state`, `visibility` and `placement` among them, and reads its spec record back as the record the test writes out by hand, field by field, with that record's digest. The implementer writes the pinned record for the values R14 keeps. A change to the layout fails the test, printing `the spec record of PIN-1 reads <record> want <record>`, or `the spec record of PIN-1 digests to <digest>, want <digest>`.

`TestHashGateEmitsDigestAndDropsSyntheticCarries` in `internal/dispatch/api`, the test the root's `c-hash-gate` names, drives Dispatch's side of R14's hash gate on a converted issue. A prose edit, an ask-attribute rewrite, a reading and a restore of the approved text each commit in `storetest.XidBatchedWindow` (2 statements), emit `artifact.version` with `digest_owed: true` and zero synthetic `artifact.approved`, and emit `artifact.digest` from `fillOwedDigests` with `approval_current: true`. One settlement that both adds a criterion and changes an ask attribute emits zero `artifact.approved` and emits `artifact.digest` with `approval_current: false`. The test compares Dispatch's emitted JSON for `GET /api/v1/artifacts/{id}`, `artifact.version` and `artifact.digest` against `packages/contracts/fixtures/hash-gate/`, checks that `approval.state` reads `approved` with `approval.version` below `latest_version` when the approval digest is current and `digest_owed` is `false`, checks that an unconverted or non-query document omits `digest_owed`, and checks Dispatch's event order (`artifact.version` before its fill's `artifact.digest`, and the fill before `POST /reviews`'s `artifact.approved` or `artifact.changes_requested`). `POST /reviews` on a version whose digest is owed fills that digest before it records the approval, so the review pins the record's digest. Recording a `result` on an approved Verification document leaves its approval digest unchanged, `approval_current: true`, with zero carried review. `GET /api/v1/artifacts/{id}` answers `current_sha256` and `digest_owed` beside `content_sha256` on its `approval`. Each `artifact.digest` carries `artifact_id`, `name`, `version`, `content_sha256`, `approval_current`, `approved_version` and `approved_sha256`. Else the test prints the subtest, the version and the event or the member it read.

The cutover carry is written once (R14). `TestAPreCutoverRestoreCarriesOnce` in `internal/dispatch/docs` restores from a version with no `version_renders` digest and reads exactly one carried review in the write batch. It pins the markdown's sha256. The write's own pass does not carry again. The fill pins the record's digest on that carry's row of `artifact_review_carries` and appends `artifact.digest` with `approval_current: true`. A deferred pass follows R14's separate rule, the move of one version's approval to its record's digest that `c-render-at-version` checks.

The version read names the digest an approval covers (R14). `TestAVersionAnswersTheDigestAnApprovalCovers` in `internal/dispatch/api` creates an issue born converted. Version 1 of its spec answers a `digest` equal to its record's digest, which is not the sha256 of its markdown, on `GET /api/v1/artifacts/{id}/versions/1` and in the version list of `GET /api/v1/artifacts/{id}`. Its `sha256` is the sha256 of its markdown. Version 1 of an uploaded `notes.md`, which no query covers, answers the sha256 of its stored markdown as both. alice's approval of version 1 pins that digest, and the artifact read's approval names it. A version 2 of the spec written by SQL, as an older build wrote one, which no pass has stated, answers the sha256 of its stored markdown.

For the cutover carry of `TestAPreCutoverRestoreCarriesOnce`, read the review id, its unchanged `content_sha256` and its `artifact_review_carries` row before the fill. After the fill the same carry row has `record_sha256` equal to the saved record's digest. No second review and no `artifact.approved` was written, and the fill's one event is `artifact.digest`. The current approval uses the carry row's digest. This case must fail if a fill changes the immutable review, adds a review, or leaves the carry row unpinned.
:::

:::check{#c-daemons-carry-hash-gate serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-approval-bytes dispatch://TREE-1/spec#b-r-approval-hash" surface="api" run="m=$(gh pr list -R cybermonklabs/legion --head legion/TREE-14 --state merged --json mergeCommit -q '.[0].mergeCommit.oid') &amp;&amp; test -n &#x22;$m&#x22; &amp;&amp; gh api --paginate '/orgs/cybermonklabs/packages/container/legion-worker/versions?per_page=100' --jq '.[] | [.name, (.metadata.container.tags | join(&#x22; &#x22;))] | @tsv' &gt; $TMPDIR/infra1253-worker-tags.tsv &amp;&amp; lacks=0 &amp;&amp; for d in $(kubectl -n legion get deploy -o name | grep -E -- '-daemon$'); do IFS='|' read -r want gen seen upd avail img &lt;&lt;&lt; &#x22;$(kubectl -n legion get $d -o jsonpath='{.spec.replicas}|{.metadata.generation}|{.status.observedGeneration}|{.status.updatedReplicas}|{.status.availableReplicas}|{.spec.template.spec.containers[0].image}')&#x22;; if [ &#x22;${want:-0}&#x22; = 0 ]; then echo &#x22;idle: $d runs no daemon&#x22;; continue; fi; tag=$(grep -F &#x22;${img#*@}&#x22; $TMPDIR/infra1253-worker-tags.tsv | grep -o 'sha-[0-9a-f]*' | head -1); st=$(test -n &#x22;$tag&#x22; &amp;&amp; gh api &#x22;repos/cybermonklabs/legion/compare/$m...${tag#sha-}&#x22; --jq .status); if { [ &#x22;$st&#x22; = ahead ] || [ &#x22;$st&#x22; = identical ]; } &amp;&amp; [ &#x22;$seen&#x22; = &#x22;$gen&#x22; ] &amp;&amp; [ &#x22;$upd&#x22; = &#x22;$want&#x22; ] &amp;&amp; [ &#x22;$avail&#x22; = &#x22;$want&#x22; ]; then echo &#x22;carries: $d at ${tag#sha-}&#x22;; else echo &#x22;lacks: $d tag ${tag:-none} compare ${st:-none} generation $gen observed $seen updated $upd available $avail of $want&#x22;; lacks=1; fi; done; test &#x22;$lacks&#x22; = 0 &amp;&amp; echo PASS" when="before_merge" negative_control="Run the command while dispatch://TREE-14 has not merged or while any running `-daemon` Deployment in namespace `legion` runs an image whose commit is behind dispatch://TREE-14's merge commit: the command prints a `lacks:` line (or empty merge commit) and exits 1."}
Proves the rolling-deploy precondition of R14 and dispatch://TREE-14 before cybermonklabs/legion#4180 merges: dispatch://TREE-14 has merged to `main` and every running Legion daemon (`legion-*-daemon` with `replicas > 0` in namespace `legion`) carries that merge commit, with its rollout complete, so no live daemon still closes design gates on version numbers alone once Dispatch stops writing synthetic carries on converted documents. Run with a 600-second timeout.
:::

:::check{#c-carried-from serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-carried-from dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-approval-bytes" surface="api" run="cd packages/envoy &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; go test ./... -run '^(TestACarriedReviewNamesTheVersionItCarriesFrom|TestAnUnfilledCarriedReviewTakesItsSourceFromItsReason|TestCensusHoldsEveryCarriedReviewsSourceVersion|TestAskAdviceNamesACarriedReviewAndTheVersionItsReasonGives)$' -count=1 -v 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/carried-from.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestACarriedReviewNamesTheVersionItCarriesFrom ' $TMPDIR/carried-from.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestAnUnfilledCarriedReviewTakesItsSourceFromItsReason ' $TMPDIR/carried-from.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestCensusHoldsEveryCarriedReviewsSourceVersion ' $TMPDIR/carried-from.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestAskAdviceNamesACarriedReviewAndTheVersionItsReasonGives ' $TMPDIR/carried-from.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q -- '--- SKIP' $TMPDIR/carried-from.log" when="before_merge" negative_control="Five controls, run one at a time. First, let writeCarriedReview insert no artifact_review_carries row. TestAnUnfilledCarriedReviewTakesItsSourceFromItsReason fails printing `the review of version 5 carried from the approval of version 4 holds no artifact_review_carries row`, though the reviews route still answers 4 through the reason. Second, let the reviews route and the approval read take carried_from_version from the reason alone (docs.CarriedFromVersion) where a row stands. TestACarriedReviewNamesTheVersionItCarriesFrom reads 4 for the review whose row names 3, and fails naming that review and both versions. Third, let the backfill pass insert a missing row and leave a row whose version is not the one the reason names. TestCensusHoldsEveryCarriedReviewsSourceVersion reads one difference of kind review_carried_from after the next pass, and fails naming the review. Fourth, let the backfill pass keep a row whose review is gone. TestCensusHoldsEveryCarriedReviewsSourceVersion reads one difference after the next pass, and fails naming the row's review id. Fifth, let Dispatch's advice read the reason in place of the row. TestAskAdviceNamesACarriedReviewAndTheVersionItsReasonGives reads the reason's version in its case whose row and reason differ, and fails naming both versions."}
The run proves the four tests executed. It greps the run's own log for each test's `--- PASS:` line by itself, and fails on any `--- SKIP` line, which `storetest.Open` writes when `DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL` is unset.

A carried approval says that it is carried (R27). `TestACarriedReviewNamesTheVersionItCarriesFrom` in `internal/dispatch/api`, a Go test the implementer adds: alice approves version 4 of the spec of an issue that has not converted. The issue's conversion writes version 5 of its spec query, and the one-time cutover carry of R14 carries her approval to version 5. `GET /api/v1/artifacts/{id}/reviews` answers the review of version 5 with `carried_from_version` 4, the review of version 4, her own act, with null, and a plan review's approval with null. The approval read answers 4 after the carry, and null after alice's own approval of a later version. On a second issue that has not converted, `main`'s text carry still runs: alice approves version 4 of its spec, an upload changes the text as version 5, and an upload of version 4's text as version 6 carries her approval to version 6, naming 4. A carry of that carry, an upload of the same text as version 7, names 4. The `artifact.approved` event of each carry carries 4. Beside each read, the test reads the `artifact_review_carries` row of the review of version 5 by SQL. A review whose row, written by SQL, names version 3 while its reason names 4 reads 3 through the reviews route and the approval read, so a reader that parses the reason alone fails.

Rows written before this build read the same. `TestAnUnfilledCarriedReviewTakesItsSourceFromItsReason` in `internal/dispatch/api`, a Go test the implementer adds, writes a review as the release before writes it, with the carried reason and no row. It answers 4 through the reviews route and the approval read before the backfill, and it holds its row naming 4 after the backfill. A person's own review with no row answers null.

The census holds the table to the reviews. `TestCensusHoldsEveryCarriedReviewsSourceVersion` in `internal/dispatch/graphcensus`, a Go test the implementer adds, reads the census kind `review_carried_from`. A carried review with no row is one difference before the backfill and none after it. A row whose version an SQL `update` changes is one difference, and the next pass of the backfill rewrites it to the reason's version, so the census reads zero after it. A row whose review an SQL `delete` removes is one difference, and the next pass deletes the row. The pass reads `artifact_reviews` in batches of `backfillBatch` (200) rows, in the index-led keyset order of (`artifact_id`, `docs.ReviewOrder`) (`artifact_id, event_seq desc nulls last, created_at desc, artifact_reviews.id desc`), over the index `artifact_reviews_by_artifact_event_seq`, as `latestReviewsStatement` in `api/reviews.go` orders its read. `TestEveryReviewReadOrdersByReviewOrder` in `api/review_order_guard_test.go` requires `docs.ReviewOrder` of every ordered read of that table, and it admits that order.

Dispatch's advice reads the member. `TestAskAdviceNamesACarriedReviewAndTheVersionItsReasonGives` in `internal/dispatch/api` holds the advice, with a case whose row and reason name different versions, so a read of the reason fails it.

T14's cutover carry and the first pass's move of a deferred version's approval to its record's digest each assert the `artifact_review_carries` row of the review they write, in `TestApprovalCoversTheDigestOfOneQuerysRecord` and `TestAPreCutoverRestoreCarriesOnce` (`c-approval-bytes`) and in the deferred-version and repair cases of `TestTheTreeRendersAPostCutoverVersionFromItsTuples` (`c-render-at-version`).
:::

:::check{#c-render-at-version serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-render-at-version" surface="cli" run="cd packages/envoy &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; go test ./... -run '^(TestTheTreeRendersAPostCutoverVersionFromItsTuples|TestTheBackfillMarksEachUnstatedDocumentOnceAndTheCensusReadsZeroAfterIt|TestTheDecisionsQueryVersionsRenderTheirAnswerAsOfTheirRow|TestADocumentNoQueryRecordCoversRecordsNoDigest|TestAnEditAboveTheBoundDefersItsIndex|TestXidWindowRouteTable)$' -count=1 -v 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/render-at-version.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestTheTreeRendersAPostCutoverVersionFromItsTuples ' $TMPDIR/render-at-version.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestTheBackfillMarksEachUnstatedDocumentOnceAndTheCensusReadsZeroAfterIt ' $TMPDIR/render-at-version.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestTheDecisionsQueryVersionsRenderTheirAnswerAsOfTheirRow ' $TMPDIR/render-at-version.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestADocumentNoQueryRecordCoversRecordsNoDigest ' $TMPDIR/render-at-version.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestAnEditAboveTheBoundDefersItsIndex ' $TMPDIR/render-at-version.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestXidWindowRouteTable ' $TMPDIR/render-at-version.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q -- '--- SKIP' $TMPDIR/render-at-version.log" when="before_merge" negative_control="Thirty-three controls, run one at a time. First, read the newest text_rank value of each member in place of the newest at or before the row's time. The test re-orders the text of two top-level siblings, renders the first version again, and fails, because the two come back in the order they have now, printing `the render of &lt;ref&gt;@v&lt;n&gt; differs from its stored bytes from byte &lt;n&gt;`. Second, count in the class of unstated rows a row of a document of an issue that has not converted whose document_block_versions row a pass of rule 2 has stated. TestTheBackfillMarksEachUnstatedDocumentOnceAndTheCensusReadsZeroAfterIt retracts the text value of a block of the spec of CORE-1, which the reconciliation has stated, reads no row difference of kind block_text, and fails, printing among its lines `with block &lt;block&gt; broken the census reads 0 row difference(s) of kind block_text, [], want the one naming it`. Third, render the members in the tree's order, by part_of and rank, in place of text_parent and text_rank. The render of version 1 of the spec of CORE-1 puts the requirement before the paragraph, under k1, and differs from the stored bytes from byte 47. TestTheTreeRendersAPostCutoverVersionFromItsTuples fails, printing `the render of CORE-1/spec@v1 differs from its stored bytes from byte 47` and `the census reads a difference at version CORE-1/spec@v1: the stored markdown (165 bytes) and the render of the tree at the row's time (165 bytes) differ from byte 47`. The census counts that difference among whatever others the test's database holds, and the test reads the difference at version CORE-1/spec@v1 alone. Fourth, drop the rule that leaves out a member whose state is gone. The render of version 3 prints the criterion k2, which that version dropped, and the test fails, printing `the render of CORE-1/spec@v3 holds the text of &lt;k2&gt;, a block whose state is gone at that version`. Fifth, take a member's text parent from its part_of in place of its text_parent, so that a member prints at the document's level only where its part_of names no member of the document. The requirement of version 1, whose part_of names k1, then prints nowhere, because the text of k1 does not hold it, and the test fails, printing among its lines `the render of CORE-1/spec@v1 holds the text of &lt;requirement&gt; 0 times, want once`, which the count assertion of version 1's case prints, and the same line of version 2 for its fourth requirement. Sixth, decide which member stands inside which by their texts, as spec version 138 did: a member whose text the text of an earlier member holds prints inside it and not again. The render of version 4 then prints the second `Same words.` paragraph and the second `---` rule nowhere, and the test fails, printing `the render of CORE-1/spec@v4 differs from its stored bytes from byte &lt;n&gt;`. Seventh, render a version whose row holds no time from the tree, as of the version row's created_at. No member holds a text value at that time, so the deferred version renders as no bytes, and the test fails, printing `version &lt;n&gt; of &lt;ref&gt; renders 0 bytes from tree, want its &lt;m&gt; stored bytes from stored`. Eighth, let the reconciliation's pass carry no approval. The approval of the deferred version, taken before its pass, reads stale after the pass although its render equals its stored bytes, and the test fails, printing `the approval of &lt;ref&gt; at version &lt;n&gt;, taken before its pass, reads stale after a pass whose render equals its stored bytes`. Ninth, read the newest text_parent tuple of each member in place of the newest at or before the row's time. After version 5, the render of version 4 prints the third requirement twice, inside the callout's text and again at the top level, and the moved `Same words.` paragraph not at all, and the test fails, printing `the render of CORE-1/spec@v4 differs from its stored bytes from byte &lt;n&gt;`. Tenth, give a block of a fragment of an issue room its slice of the room's joined rendering, as indexRoom gives it at e3d53f38. The render of version 1 of the converted issue's plan then opens its list with `*`, and the render of version 1 of its spec opens with `---`, and the test fails, printing `the render of &lt;plan ref&gt;@v1 differs from its stored bytes from byte 0` and `the render of &lt;spec ref&gt;@v1 differs from its stored bytes from byte 0`. It prints no such line for the Verification document, whose blocks read alike in both renderings. Eleventh, let the pass record its time, its seq and its digest on the row of a version whose stored markdown is not the rendering of the tree it states. That version then renders the live tree's text from the source tree, and the test fails, printing `version 1 of &lt;ref&gt; renders &lt;k&gt; bytes from tree, want its &lt;m&gt; stored bytes from stored`. Twelfth, count such a row in the census's class deferred. The test fails, printing `the census counts version 1 of &lt;ref&gt; as deferred, want tree_mismatch`. Thirteenth, let the reconciliation's pass carry an approval of an earlier version across to the version it states, as `carryUnmovedEarlier` did. The pass over version 2 of the third issue's spec then writes a carried review at version 2, and the test fails, printing `the pass over version 2 of &lt;ref&gt; wrote a carried review, want none`. Fourteenth, let StoreReport.Refused leave out the class tree_mismatch. Its verdict over a report that holds the census of the rendered versions alone, in its field VersionRenders, then reads false over the mismatched version's corpus while that census reads tree_mismatch=1, and the test fails, printing `the census holds tree_mismatch=1 and is not refused`. Fifteenth, drop from indexOwedDocument the test of the room's updates not yet stored. The tick of the race case then finds no pending row once its drain has classified the browser's update, states the room's live text, which holds the browser's paragraph, at version 2, whose stored markdown lacks it, and marks version 2's row tree_mismatch, and the test fails, printing `the tick marked version 2 of &lt;ref&gt; tree_mismatch while its room held an update not yet stored`. Sixteenth, drop from indexOwedDocument the drain of the room's update log. The tick of the race case then never waits for the replica's lock and reads both counts at zero while the update observer still waits, finds no pending row, states the room's live text at version 2, and marks version 2's row tree_mismatch, and the test fails, printing the same line. Seventeenth, drop from indexOwedRoom the test of the room's updates not yet stored. The room of the room race case holds no pending row, so no other way leaves it live ahead, and the tick states the room's live text, whose spec fragment holds the browser's paragraph, at version 3 of the spec, whose stored markdown lacks it, and marks version 3's row tree_mismatch, and the test fails, printing `the tick marked version 3 of &lt;ref&gt; tree_mismatch while its room held an update not yet stored` for the room's spec. Eighteenth, drop from indexOwedRoom the drain of the room's update log. The tick of the room race case then reads both counts at zero while the update observer still waits, finds no pending row, states the room's live text at version 3 of the spec, and marks version 3's row tree_mismatch, and the test fails, printing that line for the room's spec. Nineteenth, drop the repair from the reconciliation's tick. Version 1 of the mismatched version's document then still holds tree_mismatch after the later quiet tick, and the test fails, printing `version 1 of &lt;ref&gt; still holds tree_mismatch after a quiet tick`. Twentieth, let the repair restate and never close. Version 1 of the fifth issue's spec, whose blocks version 2's pass has moved past, then keeps its mark after the later tick, and the test fails, printing that line for that spec. Twenty-first, render the decisions query node by its members, as RenderAt does at 0f722e15. Version 1 of the decisions query then renders no bytes from the source tree, and TestTheDecisionsQueryVersionsRenderTheirAnswerAsOfTheirRow fails, printing `version 1 of &lt;decisions ref&gt; renders 0 bytes from tree, want its &lt;m&gt; stored bytes from tree`. Twenty-second, order the decisions rendering by the nodes' place in the tree in place of each node's made_at, then its id, in the version write and the renderer alike. The move of the second decision's block then puts it before the ask in that order, version 3 stores other bytes than version 2, and TestTheDecisionsQueryVersionsRenderTheirAnswerAsOfTheirRow fails, printing `version 3 of &lt;decisions ref&gt;, written for the move of &lt;decision&gt;, differs from version 2 from byte &lt;n&gt;`. Twenty-third, let the pass record on the row of a version of an upload the digest of the record of its issue's spec query. artifact_version_text_sha256 then answers that digest for the upload's version 1, the approval pins it, and TestADocumentNoQueryRecordCoversRecordsNoDigest fails, printing `the version_renders row of &lt;upload ref&gt;@v1 holds &lt;at&gt;, &lt;read_seq&gt; and &lt;record_sha256&gt;, want a time, a seq and no digest` and `the approval of &lt;upload ref&gt; at version 1 pins &lt;digest&gt;, want the stored markdown's &lt;digest&gt;`. Twenty-fourth, set the deferral flag (versionWrite.deferLarge in docs/mutation.go) for every write of a version, a settlement's version and the decisions step's restore among them. TestAnEditAboveTheBoundDefersItsIndex fails naming the settlement's version left owed and the restore's dangling moved_to. Twenty-fifth, leave the edit route's NamedVersion call unmarked. TestAnEditAboveTheBoundDefersItsIndex fails naming the edit's named version indexed inline. Twenty-sixth, let the anchored pin of a deferred version of a converted query document carry the approval it finds to the version it pins. TestAnEditAboveTheBoundDefersItsIndex fails naming the carried review the pin wrote. Twenty-seventh to thirty-first, one for each write that defers (the edit of the deep spec, the anchored comment, the accept of a suggestion, the named-version route and the rebuild): leave that write's context unmarked, so that its index runs inline again. The row of TestXidWindowRouteTable's documents table for that write fails naming its statement count and its largest gap. Thirty-second, run the deferred write's read of the typed nodes in the write phase, after the batch. The two rows of the Verification upload above the bound, on an issue that has not converted and on a converted issue, fail naming the extra statement. Thirty-third, let the pass that first states a deferred version append no `artifact.digest`. The deferred version's case reads no `artifact.digest` for version 1 after its pass, and the test fails, printing `no artifact.digest for &lt;ref&gt;@v1 after its first pass`."}
The run proves all six tests executed. It greps the run's own log for each test's `--- PASS:` line and fails on any `--- SKIP` line, which `storetest.Open` writes when `DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL` is unset.

A version the store wrote renders again from the tree. The test writes a subtree, records its rendering and its digest, then re-parents one node, re-orders the text of two top-level siblings and edits the text of a third. It renders the first version again and gets the first bytes, character for character. It renders it twice at different times and gets one byte string both times.

It proves each of the renderer's reads in turn. It takes a node whose text changed and finds the text value of the earlier version. It takes the re-ordered pair and finds the `text_rank` values they held then. It takes the re-parented node and finds it at one place in the text in both renders, because the renderer's branch for a document reads no `part_of` tuple. It gives two members `text_rank` values that differ only in case at one position (`a`, `B`) and reads `B` first, because a `text_rank` compares byte for byte, as a rank does. The test refuses to run where `select 'a' < 'B'` is false, since such a database cannot tell byte order from its own collation. It retracts an `in_document` tuple after the version's time and renders again, and the node is still in the rendering, because the retraction is later than the version.

It proves that a version of a document renders in the text order its author wrote (R15). It writes, through the real version write, version 1 of the spec of CORE-1: a criterion `k1`, then a paragraph, then a requirement whose `parent` attribute names `k1`, 165 bytes in all. In the tree the requirement stands under `k1`, before the paragraph. It renders version 1 and gets its 165 stored bytes, character for character. It finds the text of `k1`, of the paragraph and of the requirement once each, at the byte offset where the stored bytes hold it. It reads the census of the rendered versions (`docs.ReadVersionRenderCensus`, which `census --store` prints), which compares the stored markdown of each version whose `version_renders` row holds a time with a render as of that time (R16), and finds no difference at version `CORE-1/spec@v1`. Else the test fails, printing `the render of <ref>@v<n> differs from its stored bytes from byte <n>`, `the render of <ref>@v<n> holds the text of <node> <count> times, want once`, or `the census reads a difference at version <ref>@v<n>: <cause>`.

It proves that each member renders once, at its place in the text, wherever its parent stands. It writes version 2 of that spec, which holds a second criterion, `k2`, and four requirements more. The `parent` attribute of the first names a block of the issue's Verification document, which the test writes first. That of the second names an ask of the issue, which the test opens first. The third stands inside a callout, and its `parent` names `k1`. The `parent` of the fourth names `k2`. It renders version 2 and gets its stored bytes, character for character, and it finds the text of each of the four once, at the byte offset where the stored bytes hold it. It then writes version 3, which drops `k2` and leaves the fourth requirement as it was. The write takes it, because `pmdoc.CheckBlockPointers` never refuses a pointer that a write leaves unchanged, and the pass states `k2` `gone`. It renders version 3 and gets its stored bytes: the fourth requirement once, at its place in the text, under a parent whose `state` is `gone`, and no text of `k2`. It renders version 2 again and gets the bytes it got before, `k2` among them, because `k2` went `gone` after that version. Else the test fails, printing `the render of <ref>@v<n> holds the text of <node> <count> times, want once`, or `the render of <ref>@v<n> holds the text of <node>, a block whose state is gone at that version`, or the line of a render that differs from its stored bytes.

It proves that a member is placed by its id and not by its words. It writes version 4 of the spec, which holds, beside what version 3 holds, two top-level paragraphs that each read `Same words.` and two `---` rules, each after one of the two paragraphs. It renders version 4 and gets its stored bytes, character for character: each of the four once, at its own place. Else the test fails, printing `the render of CORE-1/spec@v4 differs from its stored bytes from byte <n>`.

It proves that a member's place in the text is read as of the row's time. It writes version 5 of the spec, which moves the third requirement out of the callout to the top level, after the callout, and moves the first `Same words.` paragraph into the callout, after the callout's other blocks. The third requirement's `text_parent` then names the document's node, and that paragraph's names the callout. It renders version 5 and gets its stored bytes, character for character. It then renders version 4 again and gets the bytes it got before, character for character: the third requirement once, inside the callout's text, and that paragraph once, at the top level. Else the test fails, printing `the render of CORE-1/spec@v<n> differs from its stored bytes from byte <n>`.

It proves that a fragment of an issue room renders its own bytes (R1). The room renders its own fragment first, then its documents in the order the room lays them out: the Verification document, the plan, the spec, then every other document (`roomLayoutSQL` in `docs/service.go`, `roomLayout.fragments` in `docs/tree.go`). In an issue born converted the test writes, through the issue's room and its settlement, a Verification document whose text ends with a `-` list, a plan whose text opens with a `-` list, and a spec whose text opens with a `---` rule and holds a second rule later. The settlement writes version 1 of each from its own fragment's rendering. In the room's joined rendering the plan's list follows the Verification document's list and takes the `*` marker (`otherListMarkers`), where the plan's own rendering writes `-`. The spec's opening rule is written `---` there, where the spec's own rendering writes `***`, because its second rule would close front matter that a `---` opening the spec would open. The Verification document's blocks read alike in both, so it is the control of the case. The test renders version 1 of the Verification document, the plan and the spec, and gets each one's stored bytes, character for character. It reads the text value of the plan's first block and of the spec's first block each equal to that block's slice of its own document's stored bytes. Else the test fails, printing `the render of <ref>@v<n> differs from its stored bytes from byte <n>`, or `the text value of <block> is <text>, want its slice of <ref>@v<n>, <text>`.

A `PATCH` can change the head render without changing the bytes of an earlier version (R7, R15). Save the render and digest of the spec version that holds a requirement with `parent=` naming `k1`. Move it under a different criterion through `PATCH` with the current `If-Match`. Read the changed `parent=` in the head and in the new version. The earlier version still renders its saved bytes. Then move a room paragraph under another paragraph. The tree places it under the other paragraph, but its Markdown stays flat and its text facts are unchanged. `c-reparent-and-state` checks the document version event and the open request for moves that change text.

It proves the boundary is a row and not a clock. Each version the writer rendered from the tree holds a `version_renders` row, written in the same transaction. The test confirms that by rolling the transaction back and finding neither the version nor the row. It reads the row's time no earlier than the time of every text value, `text_parent` tuple and `text_rank` value its pass wrote, and the row's digest equal to the digest of the version's record. It deletes one such row and renders that version again, and the renderer answers the stored markdown and says so. It appends a tuple dated before a pre-cutover version and renders that version. The answer is unchanged, because no tuple moves a version across the boundary. It reads the digest of a pre-cutover version and finds it taken over that version's stored markdown. It reads the digest of a post-cutover version and finds it taken over that version's record.

It proves what a deferred version renders, and what becomes of an approval taken before its pass (R14, R15). The head has no test hook that lowers `deferBlockIndexBlocks`, a constant of 2,000 in `docs/reference_excerpts.go`. So the test writes 2,001 list items into version 1 of the spec of a second issue as the issue create writes a spec's version 1 (`createIssue` in `api/issue_create.go`): it seeds the text through `service.SeedText`, queues the version through the ledger's `QueueVersion`, and indexes it through `service.IndexDocumentReferences`. That call leaves a version of more than 2,000 blocks to the block-index reconciliation, as it leaves the document `writeDocumentThroughTheRequestPath` in `docs/block_index_writers_test.go` writes with `deferredItems` items, one more block than the bound. A write through `writeVersionTx` whose context carries no mark to defer would index the version in its own transaction whatever its size, as a settlement's version and the decisions step's restore do (R15). It reads that version's `version_renders` row, which holds no time and no digest, and reads the version through `docs.RenderVersion`: its stored bytes, byte for byte, from the source `stored`. It reads the census of the rendered versions count that row in its class `deferred` and print no difference at that version. It approves that version through the approval route, and reads the review's `content_sha256` equal to the sha256 of the version's stored markdown. It then runs the block-index reconciliation until no document owes its index, as `drainOwed` in `docs/issue_tree_index_test.go` runs it. The row then holds a time no earlier than every text value of the version, and the digest of the version's record. The version renders from the source `tree`, and its render equals its stored bytes. The newest review of the spec is a review carried to that same version, whose reason reads `Carried forward from the approval of version 1: this version's text is that version's, unchanged.` and whose `content_sha256` is the record's digest, and the approval of the spec stands. The pass appends one `artifact.digest` for version 1 with `approval_current: true`. Last it writes version 2 of that spec with 2,001 items more and then version 3 with one paragraph, each by an upload, as `storeArtifact` in `api/artifacts.go` writes an upload over a document: `service.ReplaceText` with the token of the version it replaces, the version queued through the ledger's `QueueVersion`, `service.IndexDocumentReferences`, and `CarryUploadedApproval`, before the reconciliation runs. Version 2 defers by its size, and version 3's own write indexes it. It runs the reconciliation again. Version 2's row still holds no time, version 2 still answers its stored bytes from the source `stored`, and the census still counts it in `deferred`. Else the test fails, printing `version <n> of <ref> renders <k> bytes from <source>, want its <m> stored bytes from <source>`, `the census counts version <n> of <ref> as <class>, want deferred`, `the approval of <ref> at version <n>, taken before its pass, reads stale after a pass whose render equals its stored bytes`, or `no artifact.digest for <ref>@v1 after its first pass`.

It proves that a version whose tree does not render as its stored markdown keeps its stored bytes until a repair, and that the census refuses on it while its mark stands (R15, R16). No route of the head writes such a version, because an upload stores the text that `SeedText` or `ReplaceText` answers (`storeArtifact` in `api/artifacts.go`). The test builds one with a single input the product never gives: it writes a document as the upload route writes one, and hands the version write markdown other than the text `SeedText` answers. It seeds the text `Seeded words.`, and the other markdown is the renderer's own rendering of a document that holds one paragraph, `Other words.` (`documentMarkdownWithOffsets` in `docs/tree.go`). It picks that markdown because the repair case below restates a version only where its stored markdown parses and renders back as its own bytes (R15), and a lone paragraph of plain words holds nothing the parser reads otherwise than the renderer wrote it. The test asserts that before it writes the document, and fails printing `the mismatched markdown does not render back as itself` otherwise. It creates the `artifacts` row of the spec of an issue with no `document_rooms` row, as `treeDocument` in `docs/issue_tree_index_test.go` creates an issue's spec with `primary` set, so the version has a record of R14 (R15), whose digest the repair case below reads. In one transaction joined to the service (`service.Join`), it seeds the document's text through `service.SeedText`, and queues version 1 through the ledger's `QueueVersion` with that other markdown, as `storeArtifact` queues its version. So the version write records version 1's `doc_update_version` at the head the seed left (`queueVersionInsert` in `docs/mutation.go`) and inserts the version's `version_renders` row (R15), as it does for every upload. It then calls `service.IndexDocumentReferences` with that markdown, which logs `the tree its transaction wrote does not render as the version's markdown` and leaves the version's blocks to the reconciliation (`docs/reference_excerpts.go`), and commits. It approves version 1, as the case above approves its deferred version, and reads the review's `content_sha256` equal to the sha256 of the stored markdown. The seed left a `doc_settlements_pending` row, as every upload's does, and while it stands the reconciliation reads the document as live ahead of its version and states nothing (`indexOwedDocument` in `docs/block_index.go`). So the test runs the document's settlement as the product runs it, through `service.settleOwedNow`. It reads no content changed since version 1's `doc_update_version` (`contentChangedSinceVersion`), writes no version, and deletes the pending row (`clearSettlementPending` in `docs/persistence.go`, which the settlement runs). The test chooses this over deleting the pending row by SQL, which a test helper does (`settle` in `docs/block_index_test.go`), because that delete is a second write the product never makes, where the settlement is the product's own. It then runs the block-index reconciliation until no document owes its index (`drainOwed`). The version's row then holds no time, no digest and no seq, and holds `tree_mismatch` true. The version renders its stored bytes, byte for byte, from the source `stored`. It reads the census of the rendered versions through `docs.ReadVersionRenderCensus`, as `census --store` reads it: `tree_mismatch=1`, that one version printed at its address, counted in no other class, and no difference at it. It reads the verdict that census alone decides, `(&graphcensus.StoreReport{VersionRenders: &renders}).Refused()` over the census it read, and finds it true. It does not read the verdict of the whole store census (`graphcensus.StoreCensus`), which refuses over this database whatever `tree_mismatch` holds, because the database holds no row of kinds the census covers, the comments among them (`StoreReport.Unpopulated`). The approval of version 1 still stands, its `content_sha256` the stored markdown's digest, and no review was carried to it. Else the test fails, printing `version 1 of <ref> renders <k> bytes from <source>, want its <m> stored bytes from stored`, `the census counts version 1 of <ref> as <class>, want tree_mismatch`, `the census reads tree_mismatch=<n> at <versions>, want 1 at version 1 of <ref>`, `the census holds tree_mismatch=1 and is not refused`, or `the approval of <ref> at version 1 reads stale after a pass whose tree does not render as its stored bytes`.

It proves that a later quiet tick repairs that mark from the version's stored bytes, carries the approval, and keeps the mark visible as a count (R14, R15, R16). After the readings above, the test runs one more tick of the block-index reconciliation (`reconcileBlockIndex`). No room of the document holds an update in flight, no pending row stands, no pass is owed, and the document's blocks still stand at version 1, so the tick restates version 1 from its stored markdown. The version's row then holds a time no earlier than every text value of the version, the digest of the version's record and a seq, with `tree_mismatch` false and `tree_mismatch_repaired_at` set. The version renders from the source `tree`, and its render equals its stored bytes, byte for byte. The census of the rendered versions reads `tree_mismatch` down by 1 and `tree_mismatch_repaired` up by 1 from the reading above, prints no `tree_mismatch` line at version 1 of `<ref>`, and counts that version among `rendered_from_tree` with no difference at it. The newest review of the document is a review carried to version 1, whose reason reads `Carried forward from the approval of version 1: this version's text is that version's, unchanged.` and whose `content_sha256` is the record's digest, and the approval stands. The repair appends one `artifact.digest` for version 1 with `approval_current: true`. Else the test fails, printing `version 1 of <ref> still holds tree_mismatch after a quiet tick`, `version 1 of <ref> renders <k> bytes from <source>, want its <m> stored bytes from tree`, `the census reads tree_mismatch=<n> tree_mismatch_repaired=<m> after the repair, want <n0> and <m0>`, or `the approval of <ref> at version 1 reads stale after the repair restated it`.

It proves that the repair closes a mark that a later version's pass has moved past (R15, R16). It builds a second mismatched version the same way, version 1 of the spec of a fifth issue that has no `document_rooms` row, settles it through `service.settleOwedNow`, and runs the reconciliation until no document owes its index, which marks version 1's row `tree_mismatch`. Before any further tick it writes version 2 of that spec through the real version write (`writeVersionTx`), which indexes it in its own transaction, so the document's blocks stand at version 2. It reads the census of the rendered versions and runs one more tick. The revision fence refuses any pass at version 1 now, so the tick closes its mark: the row still holds no time, no digest and no seq, `tree_mismatch` is false and `tree_mismatch_repaired_at` is set. Version 1 renders its stored bytes, byte for byte, from the source `stored`. The census reads `tree_mismatch` down by 1, `tree_mismatch_repaired` up by 1 and `deferred` up by 1 from the reading before that tick, and prints no `tree_mismatch` line at version 1 of that spec. Else the test fails, printing `version 1 of <ref> still holds tree_mismatch after a quiet tick`, `version 1 of <ref> renders <k> bytes from <source>, want its <m> stored bytes from stored`, or `the census reads tree_mismatch=<n> tree_mismatch_repaired=<m> deferred=<d> after the repair, want <n0> <m0> <d0>`.

It proves that a version of the decisions query renders the query's answer as of its row's time, and that a move the `PATCH` of R7 takes changes no byte of it (R15, R7). `TestTheDecisionsQueryVersionsRenderTheirAnswerAsOfTheirRow` in `internal/dispatch/api`, a Go test the implementer adds, creates through `POST /api/v1/issues` a converted issue whose spec holds a criterion, an ask and two `decision` blocks, in that order, the first decision citing a second issue the test creates (`dispatch://<other key>`), so the decisions query's answer holds nodes at the create. It reads version 1 of the issue's decisions query node: its `version_renders` row holds a time and a seq, `docs.RenderVersion` answers it from the source `tree`, and the render equals its stored bytes, byte for byte, which hold the ask and the two decisions. It answers the ask through `POST /api/v1/asks/{id}/answer`, so the decisions query's answer changes and `DrainOwedQueries` writes version 2, and it reads the same of version 2. It then moves the second decision's block under the criterion through `PATCH /api/v1/issues/{key}/nodes/{id}` with the body `{parent}` and an `If-Match` naming the node's `placement_seq`, which changes that decision's place in the tree, before the ask in the tree's order, and not its `made_at` or its id. The move revises the decisions query, whose record moves, so `DrainOwedQueries` writes version 3, whose stored bytes equal version 2's, byte for byte, and whose row's record digest differs from version 2's. It reads the members of the decisions query node in the tree at the head (`refs.TreeMembers` in `refs/tree_walk.go`) and finds none, and it reads the members of the issue's spec through the same read and finds the criterion, the ask and the two decisions among them, so a read that finds nothing cannot pass. It reads `GET /api/v1/references?from=<decisions ref>&kind=mentions` and finds no mention, since the create's index of version 1 indexes no reference (R15). It names the kind because the same read without one answers the decisions document's `attached_to` edge to its issue, as the `from=` read of every document of an issue does (`api/empty_document_test.go`). It then reads `GET /api/v1/references?from=dispatch://<key>/spec&kind=mentions`, as `api/block_references_test.go` reads a spec's mentions, and finds the mention of the second issue: a mention is written from the innermost block that holds it, the paragraph inside the first decision and not the `decision` block, and a document's read answers its blocks' mentions. So that read cannot pass by finding nothing. The census of the rendered versions reads no difference at any of the three versions and counts none of them as `deferred`. Else the test fails, printing `version <n> of <decisions ref> renders <k> bytes from <source>, want its <m> stored bytes from tree`, `the census reads a difference at version <decisions ref>@v<n>: <cause>`, `the census counts version <n> of <decisions ref> as deferred`, `version 3 of <decisions ref>, written for the move of <decision>, differs from version 2 from byte <n>`, `the tree holds <n> members of the decisions query node of <key>, want none`, `the tree holds no member of the spec of <key>, so the read of members finds nothing`, `the references read from <decisions ref> answers <n> mentions, want none`, or `the references read from the spec of <key> answers no mention of <other key>, so the read finds nothing`.

It proves that a version of a document no query record covers records no digest (R15, R14). `TestADocumentNoQueryRecordCoversRecordsNoDigest` in `internal/dispatch/api`, a Go test the implementer adds, reads three such versions: version 1 of a document it uploads to a converted issue (`POST /api/v1/issues/{key}/artifacts`) under the name `notes.md`, a name no role uses, since an upload named `plan.md` or `verification.md` joins the issue's room (`documentJoinsIssueRoom` in `api/issue_create.go`) and has a record, version 1 of a project document (`POST /api/v1/projects/{key}/artifacts`), and version 1 of the issue's tree artifact, which the create writes. For each it reads the version's `version_renders` row holding `at` and `read_seq` and a null `record_sha256`, `artifact_version_text_sha256` answering the sha256 of the version's stored markdown, and `docs.RenderVersion` answering from the source `tree`, with the render equal to the stored bytes, byte for byte. The census of the rendered versions reads no difference at any of the three and counts none of them as `deferred`. It approves the upload's version 1 through the approval route and reads the review's `content_sha256` equal to the sha256 of the stored markdown. Each read reports its own failure, and the test goes on to the next read. Else the test fails, printing `the version_renders row of <ref>@v1 holds <at>, <read_seq> and <record_sha256>, want a time, a seq and no digest`, `artifact_version_text_sha256 answers <digest> for <ref>@v1, want the stored markdown's <digest>`, `version 1 of <ref> renders <k> bytes from <source>, want its <m> stored bytes from tree`, `the census counts version 1 of <ref> as <class>`, or `the approval of <upload ref> at version 1 pins <digest>, want the stored markdown's <digest>`.

It proves that the reconciliation reads an update of a room that is not stored yet as live ahead, and marks no row, also where no observer has classified the update yet (R15). It makes the spec of a fourth issue that has no `document_rooms` row as the carry case below makes its third: version 1 through the real version write, and version 2 by an unchanged upload, which leaves version 2's row with no time. It reads the census of the rendered versions through `docs.ReadVersionRenderCensus`. The case runs on the test's one database and its one service, which settles after an hour (`Settle` in `newTestServiceInstance`, `docs/settlement_credit_test.go`), so no settlement timer takes the document's owner lock and then waits on the room's lock during the holds below, which would hold the tick back. It connects a browser to the spec's room (`connectBrowser` in `docs/settlement_credit_test.go`) and finds the room's replica once it holds a copy (`listedReplica` in `docs/room_residency_test.go`). In a transaction of its own it takes the room's advisory lock (`lockDocumentRoom` in `docs/persistence.go`), which every durable append of the room takes first, and holds it, as `TestABrowserEditQueuedBehindAnOpenVersionIsNotCreditedAgainAfterAReopen` in `docs/settlement_credit_test.go` holds it. It also takes the replica's lock (`renderedReplica.mu`) and holds it, as `keptAndFreshRendering` in `docs/room_behind_head_test.go` takes it. The browser then sends a paragraph (`writeParagraph` in `docs/issue_room_test.go`). The room commits the update and appends it to its update log, and the room's update observer waits for the replica's lock, which the test reads as the replica's `waiting` count at 1. The test reads the replica's log holding one update it has not classified (`log.Pending()`), and `service.hasPendingUpdates` and `service.hasDurableAppend` of the room false: the room holds the update and counts nothing of it yet. It runs one tick of the block-index reconciliation (`reconcileBlockIndex` in `docs/block_index_test.go`) on a goroutine of its own. The tick takes the document's owner lock and no room lock, and its read of the stored head takes no lock (`readStoredHead` in `docs/stored_head.go`), so it runs while both holds stand. Its live read takes a copy of the room, which holds the browser's paragraph, and its drain of the room's update log then waits for the replica's lock. The test waits until the replica's `waiting` count reads 2 or the tick ends, and then releases the replica's lock. The drain classifies the update, the room counts its durable append, which waits behind the hold of the room's lock, and the tick reads the document as live ahead and states nothing: version 2's row still holds no time and `tree_mismatch` false. The test then releases the room's lock, waits for the room's durable appends (`waitForDurableAppends`), and runs the document's settlement (`settleOwedNow`), which writes version 3 with the browser's paragraph and indexes it in its own transaction. It runs the reconciliation until no document owes its index and reads the census again. Its `tree_mismatch` count and its `tree_mismatch_repaired` count are the ones the test read before the browser connected, it prints no `tree_mismatch` line at a version of the fourth issue's spec, and it counts version 2 of that spec in `deferred`, a version a later version replaced before its pass. It compares `tree_mismatch_repaired` too, because a mark the tick set and a later tick's repair closed counts there and in `deferred`, and no longer in `tree_mismatch`. It compares two readings and does not read a total of zero, because every case of the test runs on that one database, whose earlier cases leave rows of their own in each class. Else the test fails, printing `the tick marked version 2 of <ref> tree_mismatch while its room held an update not yet stored`, `the tick stated version 2 of <ref> while its room held an update not yet stored`, `the census reads tree_mismatch=<n> after the race, want the <m> it read before`, `the census reads tree_mismatch_repaired=<n> after the race, want the <m> it read before`, `the census marks <ref>@v<n> tree_mismatch after the race`, or `the census counts version 2 of <ref> as <class>, want deferred`.

It proves the same of the reconciliation's pass over an issue room (`indexOwedRoom`, R15). It writes an issue room of its own, under a number no other case of the test takes, as `createIssueRoom` in `docs/issue_room_test.go` writes one: each document's version 1 is empty, and the plan's fragment holds `Plan seed.` (`planSeed`). It writes version 2 of the room's spec, 2,001 list items, by an upload, as `storeArtifact` in `api/artifacts.go` writes an upload over a document: `service.ReplaceText` with the token of the version it replaces, the version queued through the ledger's `QueueVersion`, `service.IndexDocumentReferences`, and `CarryUploadedApproval`. That upload changes the spec's fragment, so it credits its writer and leaves the room's `doc_settlements_pending` row, and it leaves the room owed, since the plan's fragment reads otherwise than the plan's version 1 (`indexDocumentInRoom` in `docs/reference_excerpts.go`). The test then runs the room's settlement (`settleOwedNow`). The room's content changed since the tree artifact's latest version, which records no update (`contentChangedSinceVersion` in `docs/mutation.go`), so the settlement writes version 2 of the plan, which holds `Plan seed.`, writes no version of the spec, whose fragment reads as its version 2, states the room in its own room pass (`commitRoomVersions` in `docs/settlement.go`), and deletes the room's pending row (`clearSettlementPending` in `docs/persistence.go`). It runs the reconciliation until no document owes its index (`drainOwed`). Every fragment of the room then reads as its document's latest version, and the room owes nothing.

It then writes version 3 of the spec by an upload of version 2's stored markdown, as above. The replacement changes nothing (`ReplaceText` in `docs/mutation.go`), so the upload writes no tree of the room, appends no update and credits no one, and no pending row is written. Every fragment reads as its document's latest version, so `indexDocumentInRoom` reaches its count of the room's blocks, more than 2,000 over every fragment, and leaves them to the block-index reconciliation (`indexDeferredVersion`, which owes every document of the room its index). So the room owes its index, and version 3's row holds no time. The test reads that the room holds no `doc_settlements_pending` row and owes its index, and fails printing `the room of the race case holds a pending row before the race` or `the room of the race case owes no index before the race` otherwise. It reads the census of the rendered versions. It connects a browser to the spec, which joins it to the room (`connectBrowser`), finds the room's replica under the tree artifact's id, which names the room (`listedReplica`), takes the room's advisory lock in a transaction of its own and the replica's lock, and holds both, as the case above does. The browser then sends a paragraph into the spec's fragment (`writeParagraph`). Once the room's update observer waits for the replica's lock, the test reads the replica's log holding one update it has not classified, and `service.hasPendingUpdates` and `service.hasDurableAppend` of the room false. It runs one tick of the block-index reconciliation on a goroutine of its own.

`indexOwedRoom` in `docs/block_index.go` has three ways to leave a room live ahead, and the case shuts each but the one under test. First, a tick counts as live ahead, without reading it, a document that an earlier tick of its loop found live ahead and that is listed again unchanged (`stillLiveAhead`). `reconcileBlockIndex` hands the tick an empty set of those, so this way does not hold. Second, the pass leaves the room live ahead where the room's pending row stands and a fragment reads otherwise than its document's latest version (`markedAt` in `indexOwedRoom`). No pending row stands: the settlement deleted it, the unchanged upload wrote none, and the browser's append, which writes one with the update in its own transaction (`docs/append_writes.go`), waits behind the hold of the room's lock. So this way does not hold either. The third way is R15's drain and count test, which this case proves. The pass's other early return, where the room's revision, its marks or its documents moved since the tick listed it, leaves nothing live ahead and does not hold: nothing writes a version or a mark of the room between the listing and the pass. The tick's pass reads the room's live text through a copy, whose spec fragment holds the browser's paragraph, and its drain of the room's update log then waits for the replica's lock. The test waits until the replica's `waiting` count reads 2 or the tick ends, and then releases the replica's lock.
