The drain classifies the update, the room counts its durable append, and the tick reads the room as live ahead and states nothing: version 3's row still holds no time and `tree_mismatch` false. The test then releases the room's lock, waits for the room's durable appends, and runs the room's settlement, which writes version 4 of the spec with the browser's paragraph and states the room in its own room pass. It runs the reconciliation until no document owes its index and reads the census again: its `tree_mismatch` and `tree_mismatch_repaired` counts are the ones the test read before the browser connected, it prints no `tree_mismatch` line at a version of the room's spec, and it counts version 3 of that spec in `deferred`. Else the test fails, printing `the tick marked version 3 of <ref> tree_mismatch while its room held an update not yet stored`, `the tick stated version 3 of <ref> while its room held an update not yet stored`, `the census reads tree_mismatch=<n> after the race, want the <m> it read before`, `the census reads tree_mismatch_repaired=<n> after the race, want the <m> it read before`, `the census marks <ref>@v<n> tree_mismatch after the race`, or `the census counts version 3 of <ref> as <class>, want deferred`, each for the room's spec.

It proves that an unchanged upload of the approved text over a deferred version carries nothing and stands by its digest (R14). It makes the spec of a third issue that has no `document_rooms` row as `treeDocument` in `docs/issue_tree_index_test.go` makes a document: its `artifacts` row, its text seeded, and its version 1 written through the real version write (`writeVersionTx`), which indexes it in its own transaction, so its row holds its time and its record's digest. It approves version 1. The issue has no issue room because an unchanged upload of a room document is indexed in the upload's own transaction (R15), so version 2 would hold its time before any pass. It writes version 2 by an upload of version 1's text, as `storeArtifact` in `api/artifacts.go` writes an upload over a document: `service.ReplaceText` with the token of the version it replaces, the version queued through the ledger's `QueueVersion`, `service.IndexDocumentReferences`, and `CarryUploadedApproval`. The replacement changes nothing, so the upload writes no tree, and `IndexDocumentReferences` leaves version 2's blocks to the reconciliation (`docs/reference_excerpts.go`), whose row then holds no time. The document is a converted query document, so the upload writes no carried review and no `artifact.approved`. The test reads both: version 2's row with no time, and no review at version 2. It runs the reconciliation until no document owes its index. The pass states version 2, whose render equals its stored bytes, and records its time and its record's digest, which equals version 1's. It writes no carried review, because the newest review approves version 1, an earlier version, and it appends one `artifact.digest` for version 2 with `approval_current: true` and `approved_version` 1. Else the test fails, printing `version 2 of <ref> holds a time before its pass`, `the upload of version 2 of <ref> carried <reason>, want no carry`, `the pass over version 2 of <ref> wrote a carried review, want none`, or `the artifact.digest of version 2 of <ref> carries approval_current <value>, want true`.

It reads the head rendering through the same renderer with the time set to now and finds the current tree. It compares `document_block_texts` with the appended text values over a converted issue and finds zero differences in both directions. It writes by SQL, in the shape the release before this one stores, `document_block_texts` rows of a document whose issue has no `document_rooms` row, and whose `document_block_versions` row holds `stated_version` and `stated_rule` null, so no pass of rule 2 has stated it. The census prints those rows as the class of unstated rows of issues that have not converted, with their count, and counts none of them as a difference. That class holds no other row. `TestTheBackfillMarksEachUnstatedDocumentOnceAndTheCensusReadsZeroAfterIt` in `docs/issue_tree_index_test.go` retracts the text value of a block of the spec of CORE-1, an issue with no `document_rooms` row whose spec the reconciliation has stated at rule 2. It reads one row difference of kind `block_text`, naming that block. Else it fails, printing `with block <block> broken the census reads <n> row difference(s) of kind block_text, <differences>, want the one naming it`. It reads the catalog and finds the table's columns as `packages/envoy/internal/dispatch/store/migrations/0121_block_graph.up.sql` creates them.

It proves which writes defer their block index above `deferBlockIndexBlocks` (R15). `TestAnEditAboveTheBoundDefersItsIndex` in `internal/dispatch/api`, a Go test the implementer adds, writes a document of 2,001 blocks. On each path, an edit with no summary and an edit with a summary, the pin of an anchored comment and of an anchored ask, the accept of a suggestion, the named-version route and the rebuild each leave the document owed: its `document_block_versions.version` reads null, and `owed_documents` names it. The reconciliation then indexes it. An anchored pin of a deferred version of a converted query document writes no carried review, and an approval of that version given before its pass pins the sha256 of the version's stored markdown. A settlement's version and a decisions step's restore of the same document each index the version in their own transaction, and the restore's `moved_to` resolves through its blocks' rows.

`TestXidWindowRouteTable` in `internal/dispatch/api` passes whole at the main bounds from `BASELINE_SHA`. Use the declaration comparison in `c-windows-kept`. An upload or edit under an approval request keeps `storetest.XidBatchedWindow`. The two restore rows keep `storetest.XidBatchedWindow` (2 statements) too, as `TestXidWindowUploadRestoringTheApprovedText` does in `c-windows-kept`, since root R29 holds no restore exception under root R28's hash gate. The other rows stay at `main`'s bounds. Its documents table (`api/route_xid_window_documents_test.go`) holds a row for the Verification upload above the bound on an issue that has not converted, and one on a converted issue, each with its declared window. It also holds one row for each write that defers, each on a spec of 4,682 blocks nested six deep: the edit under an open approval request, the anchored comment, the accept of a suggestion, the named-version route and the rebuild. Each such row is declared at `storetest.XidBatchedWindow`, with no statement-free gap over `storetest.XidMaxGap`, and reads the document owed.
:::

:::check{#c-pass-growth serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-render-at-version dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-artifacts-in-tree" surface="cli" run="cd packages/envoy &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; go test -tags memory ./internal/dispatch/docs -run '^TestThePassLockTimeGrowsLinearlyWithTheRoom$' -count=1 -v 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/pass-growth.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestThePassLockTimeGrowsLinearlyWithTheRoom ' $TMPDIR/pass-growth.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q -- '--- SKIP' $TMPDIR/pass-growth.log" when="before_merge" negative_control="Two controls, run one at a time. First, put back the read of the room's blocks in planRoomBlocks as a join of issue_room_blocks on block_id_key (refs/block_nodes.go at 61882eda), in place of its probe of each wanted row. Second, put back refs.blockAuthors' read with MovedRoomBlockSQL in place of its probe. Under each, at least one of the test's two runs reads a ratio above the bound, and the test fails naming the run, the ratio and the bound."}
The run proves this test executed. It greps the run's own log for this test's `--- PASS:` line, and fails on any `--- SKIP` line, which `storetest.Open` writes when `DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL` is unset.

The reconciliation's pass stays one transaction, and its cost grows in proportion to the room (R15). `TestThePassLockTimeGrowsLinearlyWithTheRoom` in `internal/dispatch/docs`, under the build tag `memory`, a Go test the implementer adds, writes a room of 4,682 blocks and a room of 20,000 blocks in the deep spec's shape, each through the real write and the real tick. It times the transaction of the reconciliation's pass that holds the owner lock. The ratio of the time over 20,000 blocks to the time over 4,682 blocks stays at or under the bound written in the test's comment, beside the measurement the bound was set from. Each time is the median of 3 runs. The test measures twice: once with the tables analyzed after the seed, and once with the statistics of a near-empty `graph_tuples`, analyzed before the rooms are written, so the planner's estimate cannot rescue a read whose cost grows with the square of the room. Else the test fails, naming the run, the ratio and the bound.

CI's memory job runs this test too: the implementer adds to the step `Memory tests of the Dispatch server` of `.github/workflows/ci-job-dispatch-memory.yaml` a second `go-tagged-tests.sh memory ./internal/dispatch/docs` call and its own `go test -tags memory` run of `./internal/dispatch/docs`, since the script takes one directory.
:::

:::check{#c-old-versions-render serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-render-at-version dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-approval-bytes dispatch://TREE-1/spec#b-r-approval-hash" surface="cli" run="cd packages/dispatch &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; DATABASE_URL=$INFRA_1253_UPGRADE_DATABASE_URL DISPATCH_TOKEN=e2e-token PROJECT=CORE DEV_SIGNIN_LOGIN=alice bash e2e/acceptance/version-render-boundary.sh 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/version-render-boundary.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^PASS: version-render-boundary.sh complete ' $TMPDIR/version-render-boundary.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q '^SKIP' $TMPDIR/version-render-boundary.log" when="before_merge" negative_control="Render one pre-cutover version from the tuples instead of returning its stored bytes. The driver compares that render with artifact_versions.markdown, finds them unequal, and exits non-zero with the artifact, the version number and the first byte that differs."}
Every version written before the cutover still answers the bytes it holds, and every standing approval still covers them. The driver runs against the pod's test PostgreSQL, over a corpus the earlier release wrote. It builds and boots the base-commit server as this document's preamble states. Through that server's API it writes markdown documents of the shapes `c-tree-census` lists, with several versions each, and one image upload, whose version holds no markdown. It also writes one document holding a block written author-only. It records an approval of the newest version of some of those documents, so the corpus holds standing approvals, and it stops that server. It then boots this branch's server, which migrates those rows forward, and waits for the backfill as this document's preamble states, and from then on it writes nothing. It first prints the two counts this child's first step took over that corpus. Those are the count of `artifact_versions` rows with a markdown body and the count of standing approvals, each with the time it was taken. A count of zero fails the run, because the corpus holds both.

It then renders every version row with a markdown body, and prints how many it rendered. For each version it calls the one renderer and compares the answer with `artifact_versions.markdown`, byte for byte. That comparison is made as a reader who may see every block of the version. A version stored before this child's cutover can still hold a block written author-only, because dispatch://TREE-6 lands first. So the driver also renders such a version as a reader the block is hidden from, and reads that block absent, with the rest of the version byte for byte as stored. The run fails unless at least one rendered version holds a block written author-only. Every version must match. One mismatch fails the run, and the driver prints the artifact, the version number and the offset of the first byte that differs. It also asserts that no rendered version holds a `version_renders` row, so the set is the pre-cutover side and not the new one.

It then takes the approvals. For each standing approval over a rendered version it recomputes the digest `artifact_version_text_sha256` takes of the stored markdown and compares it with `artifact_reviews.content_sha256`. Every one must be equal, and one difference fails the run. That comparison tests that the stored bytes did not change, and it is not a test of an approval digest, because a review taken before the cutover is carried rather than digested again, as R14 states. It reads the update trigger on that column out of the catalog and finds it in place. Last it reads a version whose `markdown` is null (the image upload) and finds it served as plain file bytes with no `Dispatch-Render-Source` header, rather than rendered as an empty document.
:::

:::check{#c-tuple-indexes serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-tuple-indexes" surface="cli" run="cd packages/envoy &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; go test ./... -run '^TestEveryAsOfReadOfThisChildUsesAnIndexOfTheStore$' -count=1 -v 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/tuple-indexes.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestEveryAsOfReadOfThisChildUsesAnIndexOfTheStore ' $TMPDIR/tuple-indexes.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q -- '--- SKIP' $TMPDIR/tuple-indexes.log" when="before_merge" negative_control="Write the as-of render's read without its kind predicate. The test reads a Seq Scan on graph_tuples in that read's plan and fails, naming the read."}
The run proves this test executed. It greps the run's own log for this test's `--- PASS:` line and fails on any `--- SKIP` line, which `storetest.Open` writes when `DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL` is unset.

Every read this child makes is served by an index child one created. The test reads the five read index definitions out of the catalog and compares them with the five spellings the spec states, column for column, order for order and predicate for predicate. A missing index fails the test and prints which read it served.

It then takes the plan of each read. Those reads are the as-of read of a node's values, its text, its rank, its `text_rank` and its `state` among them, and of its relations, its `part_of` and its `text_parent` among them, each at a record's seq and as of a render's time. They are also the blocks of a document as of a render's time, the members whose `in_document` names it, which the renderer of R15 reads, and the children of a node in rank order at a time. They are also the `moved_to` resolve, the `needs` walk in both directions, the coverage walk over `serves`, and the backlink count. It seeds 50,000 tuples over 500 nodes and runs `analyze graph_tuples`. For each read it runs `explain (analyze, buffers)`, and asserts that the plan uses the stated index as an `Index Scan`, `Index Only Scan` or `Bitmap Index Scan`, with no `Seq Scan on graph_tuples` anywhere in it. A read that binds no kind is written into the test as a case that must fail. The test reads that case falling to a scan. Among the seeded siblings, two have ranks that differ only in case at one position (`a`, `B`), and the children read returns `B` first, because ranks compare byte for byte. The test refuses to run where `select 'a' < 'B'` is false, since such a database cannot tell byte order from its own collation.

Last it reads the migration set of this child with `pgmigrate.TouchedTables`. It finds no statement against the tuple table outside the type migrations that `typeMigrations` lists in `packages/envoy/cmd/dispatch/supertag_nodes_test.go`, and only `insert` statements in those.
:::

:::check{#c-artifacts-in-tree serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-artifacts-in-tree dispatch://TREE-1/spec#b-r-document-tree" surface="api" run="cd packages/dispatch &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; DATABASE_URL=$INFRA_1253_UPGRADE_DATABASE_URL DISPATCH_TOKEN=e2e-token PROJECT=CORE bash e2e/acceptance/issue-artifacts.sh 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/issue-artifacts.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^PASS: issue-artifacts.sh complete ' $TMPDIR/issue-artifacts.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q '^SKIP' $TMPDIR/issue-artifacts.log &amp;&amp; cd ../envoy &amp;&amp; go test ./internal/dispatch/docs/ -run '^TestAVersionWrittenAfterTheTickListedItsDocumentStaysOwed$' -count=1 -v 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/owed-no-version.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestAVersionWrittenAfterTheTickListedItsDocumentStaysOwed ' $TMPDIR/owed-no-version.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q -- '--- SKIP' $TMPDIR/owed-no-version.log" when="before_merge" negative_control="Leave one uploaded image out of the tree, as a row with no node. The driver walks the issue's tree, counts one artifact the walk does not reach, and exits non-zero with that artifact's ref key. A second control: let this head's pass over a marked document write no version node. The version the release before wrote has no node after the tick, and the driver exits non-zero naming it. A third control: make this head's tick mark by store_version alone, as markVersionedDocuments marks under rule 1, and leave BlockIndexMarkingRule, the backfill's marking and every pass as they are. The cases of this head's first boot pass. The new version the release before then writes to a document whose mark this head's pass has already cleared is marked by no tick, so after this head's next reconciliation tick that version has no document version node, and the driver exits non-zero there, naming that version, its store_version and its stated_version. A fourth control: build the release before, as lib-baseline.sh builds it, from a scratch copy of BASELINE_SHA in which queueStand clears store_owed_at whatever store_owed_rule holds. That build's index of the new version it writes clears the mark this head's backfill set, and the driver exits non-zero naming the document and store_owed_at, which it reads cleared where the mark of rule 2 stood. A fifth control: let markStaleDocuments and markStaleBatch mark only on a run that began with no row of rule 2 in graph_backfill_horizon, so the first run of rule 2 marks and every later run marks nothing. The first boot's backfill marks the spec of the second paragraph's issue, and the case of the build of rule 1 passes. The issue the release before created while this head was held is marked by no run, so after the restart and the wait for the backfill its spec's blocks hold no rank and its row's stated_version reads null. The driver exits non-zero there, naming that issue, its spec document and its stated_version. A sixth control: let the room clear of indexOwedRoom write no stated_version and no stated_rule. The last case's second run of the backfill marks the retired document again, the owed count reads above 0, and the driver exits non-zero naming that document. A seventh control: drop the not exists predicate from the statement of indexOwedDocument that clears a document with no markdown version. TestAVersionWrittenAfterTheTickListedItsDocumentStaysOwed fails in its second case, printing `the statement that clears a document with no version cleared &lt;document&gt;, which holds version &lt;n&gt;`. An eighth control: let indexOwedDocument clear a document that the tick listed at version 0 before lockArtifactOwner and with no predicate, where its early return stands at 325bfe8a2e. TestAVersionWrittenAfterTheTickListedItsDocumentStaysOwed fails in its first case, printing `the tick that listed &lt;document&gt; at version 0 cleared the mark of version &lt;n&gt;, written while it was held`. Its second case then fails at the bound of its wait, printing `the tick never reached beforeNoVersionClear within 30 s`, because the tick clears the document before it takes the lock. A ninth control: remove the statement of indexOwedDocument that clears a document with no markdown version, and keep the case on the locked path. TestAVersionWrittenAfterTheTickListedItsDocumentStaysOwed fails in its third case, printing `the tick left &lt;document&gt;, which holds no markdown version, marked: version &lt;v&gt;, stated_version &lt;s&gt;, stated_rule &lt;r&gt;`."}
Every artifact of an issue is in the tree. The driver uploads a markdown document, an image and a file to one issue, and walks the issue's tree. It reaches all three as nodes under the issue. It reads the image node and finds its mime, its size and its sha256 as values of the node. It reads the image's bytes back through `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/artifacts/{slug}/versions/{number}`, byte for byte.

It repeats the whole walk over an issue the earlier release wrote. It builds and boots the base-commit server as this document's preamble states. It uploads the same three artifacts through that server's API, records each artifact's ref key, bytes and version count, and stops it. It boots this branch's server, which migrates those rows forward, and waits for the backfill as this document's preamble states, and walks that issue's tree. Every artifact that writer stored is a node, and each one's bytes and version count equal the capture. The broken state this ordering catches is a migration that reaches every artifact its own writer made. Such a migration can still miss one shape the earlier release stored.

It reads the markdown document and finds its body as a subtree of block nodes, rendered by one query. It writes a new version and reads the document version node appended for it, with the rendering stored in `artifact_versions.markdown` as the cache. It compares that stored markdown against a fresh render of the tree as of the time that version's `version_renders` row records, and finds them equal. It takes that comparison over the versions whose row holds a time, and asserts the census counts a row that holds none in its class `deferred` and claims nothing about a version with no row. It reads the census's line `census: versions …` print `tree_mismatch=0` and `tree_mismatch_repaired=0` over its corpus, since no writer of the product writes a version whose tree does not render as its stored markdown and its driver drops no update (R16). It reads the second because the server's reconciliation repairs a mark on its next quiet tick, after which only `tree_mismatch_repaired` shows it. Else it fails, printing `the census reads tree_mismatch=<n> tree_mismatch_repaired=<m> over <corpus>, want 0 and 0: <versions>`.

It then reads the three role documents of an issue the earlier release wrote, converted with `envoy-dispatch convert-issues --project CORE`. Their blocks hang under the issue, and each of the three reads back as a query node that states the node types it takes. In the answers of `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/artifacts` and `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/artifacts/{slug}`, each non-spec query node (`verification`, `plan`, `decisions`) answers its query's name as `role`, while the spec query node answers no `role` (its part is `is_primary: true`). No column of the converted issue's `artifacts` rows holds a role. It reads `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}` and finds `verification_artifact_id` and `plan_artifact_id` still answered, each with the artifact id of its query node, as R8 keeps them for one release. It runs the role census R16 states, which counts the `artifacts` rows that carry a role on issues whose documents have `document_rooms` rows, and reads 0. A role planted on one row of the converted issue is counted by the same census. No migration of this branch drops `artifacts.role`. The driver then boots the release before beside this head, as this document's preamble states, and has it write a new version of a document whose mark this head's pass has already cleared. That release is a build of marking rule 1, which indexes the version itself and writes `store_version` at it. The driver reads that build's row of `block_index_event_cursors` with `marking_rule` 1, and fails where it reads none, because such a run proves nothing of the widened rule. Before this head's tick, it reads the document's `document_block_versions` row with `store_version` equal to its version and `stated_version` behind it. After this head's next reconciliation tick, the version has its `document version` node, and each block of it holds its rank, its text and the supertag of its type. The row's `stated_version` equals its version, its `stated_rule` is 2, and the census reads zero, with no second backfill and no restart. The driver reads this head's cursor row with `marking_rule` 2, inserted at the horizon the newest backfill of rule 2 recorded and not at the cursor of the build of rule 1. A version that this head then writes to the same document holds no mark after the next tick.

It then proves that a build of rule 1 uses up no mark of rule 2. This case runs at this head's first boot over the database of the second paragraph, between that boot and the wait for the backfill. Every boot of this head in this case keeps `DISPATCH_TEST_HOOKS=1` and `DISPATCH_TEST_HOLD_ISSUE_ROOM_STEP=1` in `BASELINE_EXTRA_ENV`, as this document's preamble sets them. The driver boots the release before again beside this head, and starts this head with `DISPATCH_TEST_HOLD_BLOCK_INDEX=1` as well, so this head's backfill runs and its block-index reconciliation waits. It waits until this head's log holds the line that ends the boot backfill, `dispatch: boot backfill done` (`tree_backfill_end` in `e2e/acceptance/lib-tree.sh`), which the wait for the backfill in this document's preamble also reads. It reads the `document_block_versions` row of the spec document of the issue of the second paragraph, with `store_owed_at` set and `store_owed_rule` 2. Through the release before, it then writes a new version of that spec, which that build indexes itself in the request. It waits until the row's `store_version` equals the new version, polling every 2 s and failing after 300 s. The row still holds `store_owed_at` with `store_owed_rule` 2. The driver stops the release before, restarts this head without `DISPATCH_TEST_HOLD_BLOCK_INDEX`, whose boot runs the backfill again, as every boot does (R16), and waits for the backfill as this document's preamble states. The new version then has its `document version` node, each block of it holds its rank and the supertag of its type, the row's `stated_version` equals that version, and the row holds no mark. Else the driver exits non-zero naming the document and the column that differs.

It then proves that the backfill of rule 2 marks a document that a build of rule 1 creates after a run of that backfill. In the same window, while this head is held, the driver creates a second issue through the release before. Its spec holds a requirement block, a check block and a paragraph, and that build creates the spec and indexes it in the request. The driver waits until that spec's `document_block_versions` row has `store_version` equal to its version, polling every 2 s and failing after 300 s, and reads that the row holds no mark. The issue did not exist when this head's first backfill ran, because the driver read that backfill's end before it created the issue. After the restart, the driver reads the horizon that the row of rule 2 in `graph_backfill_horizon` records at or above the id of that issue's `issue.created` event, so no tick of this head reads that event. Else the case proves nothing, and the driver exits non-zero naming both ids. Once the wait for the backfill ends, each block of that spec holds its rank, the requirement's node carries the supertag `requirement`, the check's node carries `check`, and the paragraph's node carries `block`. The row's `stated_version` equals its version, its `stated_rule` is 2, and it holds no mark. Else the driver exits non-zero naming the document and the column or the block that differs.

Last, it proves that a later run of the backfill marks no document that rule 2 has stated. This case runs after every case above, on an issue of its own, so no other case loses a document. The driver creates a fresh issue at this head. Every live process lists `issue_room`, so the issue is born converted (R5). It uploads the issue's plan as `plan.md` through `POST /api/v1/issues/{key}/artifacts`, holding one plan node. The plan joins the issue's room: `documentJoinsIssueRoom` in `api/issue_create.go` admits the plan's slug, and the upload queues the plan's `document_rooms` row (`queueIssueRoomJoin`). It then uploads `plan.md` a second time, holding the pre-mortem of `e2e/fixtures/acme-1098-premortem.json` as `e2e/acceptance/premortem-conversion.sh` takes it, so the pre-mortem is the plan's newest version. That upload names, as its `precondition`'s `document`, the token that `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/artifacts/plan-md/text` answers for the plan's first version, because an upload over a document that already exists replaces every word of it and is refused where it names no token (the upload's `ReplaceText` in `api/artifacts.go`). The driver converts the plan through `POST /api/v1/issues/{key}/artifacts/plan-md/premortem-convert`, with a map that gives each risk of the pre-mortem one entry with a reason and no check. The conversion reads the newest version of a markdown document of the issue by its slug (`readPremortemSource` in `api/premortem_convert.go`), and it retires the document it converts (`docs.RetireDocument`). The driver reads the plan's `retired_at` set and its `document_rooms` row still naming the room, which a retirement keeps. It reads that the database also holds documents that no `document_rooms` row names. Else the case proves nothing, and the driver exits non-zero naming what it did not find. By SQL, the driver then puts on the `document_block_versions` row of the retired document, and of the room's tree artifact where that artifact holds no `artifact_versions` row, inserting the tree artifact's row where none stands, the state in which the backfill of rule 2 leaves a document that no pass of rule 2 has stated: `store_owed_at` set, `store_owed_rule` 2, and `stated_version` and `stated_rule` null. The room's pass indexes no retired document and no document that holds no version as a fragment, so only the room clear of `indexOwedRoom` clears those marks. The driver waits until `select count(*) from document_block_versions where version is null or store_owed_at is not null` reads 0, polling every 2 s and failing after 300 s. It then restarts this head with `DISPATCH_TEST_HOLD_BLOCK_INDEX=1` beside the preamble's settings, so the boot runs the backfill a second time over the documents of unconverted issues and the converted room alike, and no pass clears what that run marks. It waits until the log holds the line that ends the boot backfill. The owed count still reads 0, and each row the driver marked holds `stated_rule` 2. Else the driver exits non-zero naming each document that holds a mark, with its `version`, its `stated_version` and its `stated_rule`.

`TestAVersionWrittenAfterTheTickListedItsDocumentStaysOwed`, in `internal/dispatch/docs`, proves that the fourth statement of R16 that writes the stated columns decides against the store as it stands. The run reads its `--- PASS:` line and fails on any `--- SKIP` line. The implementer adds the test and two hooks of `docs.Service` beside `afterBlockIndexWrite` in `docs/service.go`: `afterOwedDocumentsListed`, which runs once a tick's `owedDocuments` has answered, and `beforeNoVersionClear`, which runs inside the tick's transaction just before that statement. Each wait of the test for a tick to reach a hook has a bound of 30 s. Past it the test fails, printing `the tick never reached <hook> within 30 s`, and releases every tick it holds. The test writes, by SQL, a document D with no version, and D's `document_block_versions` row as the backfill of rule 2 leaves it: `store_owed_at` set, `store_owed_rule` 2, and `stated_version` and `stated_rule` null. It holds a tick at `afterOwedDocumentsListed`, once that tick has listed D at version 0. While the tick is held, it writes D's first version through the real version write, with more blocks than `deferBlockIndexBlocks`, so the write leaves D's index to the reconciliation and marks D owed. It then releases the tick. D's row still holds its mark. The next tick indexes that version: D's row stands at it, with `stated_version` at it and `stated_rule` 2, and each block of the version holds its node. Else the test prints `the tick that listed <document> at version 0 cleared the mark of version <n>, written while it was held`, or `the next tick left version <n> of <document> unindexed`.

In its second case the test writes a document E in the same state, and holds a tick at `beforeNoVersionClear`, after that tick's re-read under the owner lock found no markdown version of E. While the tick is held, the test inserts E's first markdown version by SQL, on a connection of its own that takes no owner lock. The insert commits, and the trigger that every version insert fires (`document_block_versions_owe`) sets E's `version` null. The test then releases the tick. E's row keeps its null `version` and its mark, and the next tick indexes that version. Else the test prints `the statement that clears a document with no version cleared <document>, which holds version <n>`.

In its third case the test writes a document F in the same state, and holds no tick. F stays without a markdown version through the tick that lists it. After that tick, F's row holds no mark, its `version` reads 0, its `stated_version` reads 0 and its `stated_rule` reads 2. Once the next tick has indexed the versions of D and E, `select count(*) from document_block_versions where version is null or store_owed_at is not null` reads 0. Else the test prints `the tick left <document>, which holds no markdown version, marked: version <v>, stated_version <s>, stated_rule <r>`, or `<n> documents still owe their block index after every tick, want 0`.
:::

:::check{#c-boot-backfill serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-artifacts-in-tree dispatch://TREE-1/spec#b-r-no-regression" surface="cli" run="cd packages/envoy &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; go test ./... -run '^(TestTheBootBackfillRunLogsItsOutcome|TestTheBootBackfillHoldsNoPodsReadiness)$' -count=1 -v 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/boot-backfill.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestTheBootBackfillRunLogsItsOutcome ' $TMPDIR/boot-backfill.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestTheBootBackfillHoldsNoPodsReadiness ' $TMPDIR/boot-backfill.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q -- '--- SKIP' $TMPDIR/boot-backfill.log" when="before_merge" negative_control="Five controls, run one at a time, each on a copy as this document's preamble states. First, let the boot-run function return the run's error to its caller. TestTheBootBackfillRunLogsItsOutcome fails printing `the boot backfill returned &lt;error&gt; to its caller, which would stop the process`. Second, let the boot-run function write the done line only where the run returned no error. The same test fails printing `the boot backfill logged no done line after a run that left 2 project-moved rows`. Third, run the boot backfill's passes in the boot's own path before the server serves, ahead of the listener (listenfd.Adopt or net.Listen in cmd/dispatch/main.go). The held passes never end, the process never logs its listening line, and TestTheBootBackfillHoldsNoPodsReadiness fails at waitHealthy, which prints `Dispatch never became healthy:` and the process's output. Fourth, let the boot-run function decide its outcome by errors.Is(err, graphstore.ErrProjectMoved) in place of the test onlyProjectMoved makes. The fourth case's run, whose error joins two project-moved errors with another error, then logs the done line, and TestTheBootBackfillRunLogsItsOutcome fails printing `the boot backfill logged a done line after a run that failed beside 2 project-moved rows`. Fifth, let the boot's record of the horizon wait with no bound, as recordBackfillHorizon waits at this head. With the test's writer of the event log held open, the third process never logs its listening line, and TestTheBootBackfillHoldsNoPodsReadiness fails at waitHealthy, which prints `Dispatch never became healthy:` and the process's output."}
The run proves both tests executed. It greps the run's own log for the `--- PASS:` line of each test by itself. It fails on any `--- SKIP` line, which `storetest.Open` writes when `DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL` is unset. Both tests are new here, and the implementer adds them in `packages/envoy/cmd/dispatch`.

`TestTheBootBackfillRunLogsItsOutcome` proves what the boot run does with each outcome of the backfill, as R16 states it. It calls the boot-run function with a record of the horizon and a run that the test gives it in place of `recordBackfillHorizon` and `graphcensus.Backfill`, and reads the lines the function logs. The record succeeds in the first four calls. The first run returns no error. The function logs `dispatch: boot backfill done`. Else the test prints `the boot backfill logged no done line after a run that succeeded`. The second run returns two errors joined, each wrapping `graphstore.ErrProjectMoved`, as `Backfill` answers rows whose node the store holds in another project. The function logs the done line and, beside it, the count 2 of those rows as a finding. Else the test prints `the boot backfill logged no done line after a run that left 2 project-moved rows`, or `the boot backfill logged the count <n>, want 2`. The third run returns any other error. The function logs that error and no done line. Else the test prints `the boot backfill logged a done line after a run that failed`. The fourth run returns `errors.Join(errors.Join(moved1, moved2), other)`: two errors wrapping `graphstore.ErrProjectMoved`, joined again with any other error. That is the shape `Backfill` answers where a later pass fails after project-moved rows (`errors.Join(moved, err)` in `graphcensus/backfill.go`). The function logs that error and no done line. Else the test prints `the boot backfill logged a done line after a run that failed beside 2 project-moved rows`. In the fifth call the record fails. The function logs the record's error, calls no run, and logs no done line. Else the test prints `the boot backfill ran its passes after its record of the horizon failed`, or `the boot backfill logged a done line after its record of the horizon failed`. In the sixth call the record returns an error that wraps `context.DeadlineExceeded`, as the bound of R16 ends a record, and names the oldest writer of the event log, backend pid 4242, open for 31 s. The function logs `dispatch: boot backfill skipped` with that pid and that age, calls no run, and logs no done line. Else the test prints `the boot backfill logged no skip after its record of the horizon reached its bound`, `the boot backfill ran its passes after its record of the horizon reached its bound`, or `the boot backfill logged a done line after its record of the horizon reached its bound`. In each of the six calls the function returns to its caller with no error, so the process serves on. Else the test prints `the boot backfill returned <error> to its caller, which would stop the process`.

`TestTheBootBackfillHoldsNoPodsReadiness` proves that no pod's readiness waits for the passes. It starts a process of this build with `startDispatchProcessWith`, with `DISPATCH_TEST_HOOKS=1` and `DISPATCH_TEST_HOLD_BOOT_BACKFILL=1` in its `Env`, and waits for it with `waitHealthy`, which needs the process's listening line and `/healthz` 200 within 30 s. While the passes are held, it reads `/healthz` 200. It writes a project and an issue through `createIssue` and reads 201 for each. It reads the row of rule 2 in `graph_backfill_horizon`, so the boot recorded the horizon before it held the passes. It reads no `dispatch: boot backfill done` line in the process's output. Else it prints `the boot backfill ended while its passes were held: <line>`, or `the boot recorded no backfill horizon of rule 2 before its passes`. It then stops the process and starts one without the hold over the same database. That process logs the done line within 300 s, polling every 2 s. Else the test prints `the boot backfill logged no done line within 300 s` and the process's output.

It then proves the bound of the record. It stops that process. On a connection of its own it opens a transaction, reads its own `pg_backend_pid()`, and inserts one event of the issue it created by SQL, as `decided_wording_test.go` inserts one, and it holds that transaction open. It starts a third process over the same database with `DISPATCH_TEST_HOOKS=1` and `DISPATCH_TEST_BOOT_BACKFILL_HORIZON_WAIT=2s` in its `Env`, and waits for it with `waitHealthy`. The process logs `dispatch: boot backfill skipped` naming the pid the test read, before its listening line. It becomes healthy, and it logs no done line. Else the test prints `the boot logged no skip of the backfill while a writer of the event log stayed open past the bound`, or `the boot's skip names pid <pid>, want <pid>`, or `the boot backfill ended while a writer of the event log stayed open: <line>`. The test rolls its transaction back only once `waitHealthy` has returned.
:::

:::check{#c-search-key serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-search-key" surface="cli" run="cd packages/envoy &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; go test ./... -run '^(TestSearchFollowsABlockThatChangesOwner|TestThisBuildBootsAndRemovesWithTheRootsSearchTablesDropped)$' -count=1 -v 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/search-key.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestSearchFollowsABlockThatChangesOwner ' $TMPDIR/search-key.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestThisBuildBootsAndRemovesWithTheRootsSearchTablesDropped ' $TMPDIR/search-key.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q -- '--- SKIP' $TMPDIR/search-key.log" when="before_merge" negative_control="Three controls, run one at a time. First, let this build's search read the windows of every owner. The test searches by meaning for the moved block's words and fails, because the block answers twice, once under each owner key. Second, add a migration that drops the artifact_versions_document_search trigger. The test reads the catalog, finds no such trigger, and fails naming it. Third, run the removal's `document_search` statement whatever `to_regclass('public.document_search')` finds. The removal over the database with no `document_search` then fails, and the second test fails naming the statement."}
The run proves this test executed. It greps the run's own log for this test's `--- PASS:` line and fails on any `--- SKIP` line, which `storetest.Open` writes when `DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL` is unset.

A block that changes owner changes the key search uses. The test indexes a document's blocks, reads the window rows under the artifact uuid as owner key, then moves the blocks into the issue's tree. It reads the windows again under the issue's tree node as owner key and finds every block covered once. It finds the old owner's rows still stored, and the census counts them as the class the root deletes. It searches by meaning for the moved block's words through this build and reads the block once.

It rolls back the transaction that writes the block rows and finds the old owner's windows still present and none under the issue's tree node. It commits it and finds the windows under the issue's tree node, with the old owner's windows still stored. It reads `embeddings_kind_check` out of the catalog and finds it unchanged, and asserts the migration set runs no statement against `embeddings`.

It then holds the lexical search. It writes a word into one block, and reads `node_search` holding that word for that node. It reads the search route answering the node that matched rather than a document. It reads the catalog and finds the `artifact_versions_document_search` trigger, its function and the `document_search` table still in place, because a process of the release before reads that table and only that trigger fills it. It writes a version and reads the `document_search` row that trigger filled. It then empties `document_search` and reads the same answer from the search route, so this build's search reads `node_search` alone. It reads `node_search` holding one document row for the document, beside its node rows, and the census kind of document rows reading zero differences. With `document_search` still empty, it creates an issue whose title holds the document's words, and reads the related check and the duplicate check answer that document. It reads the related check's statement take its document arm from document rows alone, and fails, naming the statement, where that arm reads rows of nodes. A control: let the related check rank documents from the rows of their nodes again; the test fails at that read. It reads the migration set with `pgmigrate.TouchedTables` and finds no statement against `artifact_versions` or `document_search`. A second test, `TestThisBuildBootsAndRemovesWithTheRootsSearchTablesDropped` in `packages/envoy/cmd/dispatch`, builds this head with `cmdtest.Build`, migrates a database of its own, and drops there what the root's pull request drops: `document_search` with the `artifact_versions_document_search` trigger and its function, `document_search_term_queue()` with its trigger, and `document_search_backfill`. It boots this head over that database and reads `/healthz` answer 200. It then removes one document through `DELETE /api/v1/artifacts/{id}`, as a person signed in through `GET /auth/_dev/signin`, and reads 204. It then uploads a new version of another document and reads it stored, because the trigger that fired on that write is dropped, and nothing of this build replaces it. It reads `GET /api/v1/search` answer 200, because this build's search reads `node_search` and never `document_search` (R17). The removal succeeds because its one statement that names `document_search` (`artifactRemovalClears` in `api/artifact_removal.go`) runs only where `to_regclass('public.document_search')` finds the table. The run greps its log for the `--- PASS:` line of each test by itself.
:::

:::check{#c-one-dependency serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-one-dependency dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-plan-size dispatch://TREE-1/spec#b-r-needs dispatch://TREE-1/spec#b-r-plan-node dispatch://TREE-1/spec#b-r-issue-edges" surface="api" run="cd packages/dispatch &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; DATABASE_URL=$INFRA_1253_UPGRADE_DATABASE_URL DISPATCH_TOKEN=e2e-token PROJECT=CORE bash e2e/acceptance/one-dependency.sh 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/one-dependency.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^PASS: one-dependency.sh complete ' $TMPDIR/one-dependency.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q '^SKIP' $TMPDIR/one-dependency.log &amp;&amp; cd ../envoy &amp;&amp; go test ./... -run '^TestNeedsCrossesAProjectAndRefusesAProjectScopedCaller$' -count=1 -v 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/needs-reach.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestNeedsCrossesAProjectAndRefusesAProjectScopedCaller ' $TMPDIR/needs-reach.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q -- '--- SKIP' $TMPDIR/needs-reach.log &amp;&amp; cd ../daemon &amp;&amp; go test ./... -run '^TestTheDaemonReadsNeedsAndFallsBackToBlockedBy$' -count=1 -v 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/daemon-needs.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestTheDaemonReadsNeedsAndFallsBackToBlockedBy ' $TMPDIR/daemon-needs.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q -- '--- SKIP' $TMPDIR/daemon-needs.log" when="before_merge" negative_control="Three controls, run one at a time. Second, refuse a needs target of another project to a caller that names no project. The driver reads that refusal where it expects the wait taken, and exits non-zero naming the two issues and their projects. Third, name the issue wait needs in this child's restatement of graph_edges. The driver reads no blocked_by edge in graph_edges for the issue dependency, and exits non-zero naming the two issues and the kind it read."}
Waiting is one relation and the driver proves both halves answer as one. It seeds a parent issue whose plan holds two nodes, and a child issue whose plan holds two more. It writes an issue dependency through the issue route, from the child issue to a sibling issue of the same project. It writes a plan dependency in markdown, from one of the child's nodes to a node of the parent's plan.

It reads both back as `needs` tuples of the store, each from the node that waits to the node it waits on. It reads `issue_links` holding the issue pair as a row, and reads the `needs` attribute of the plan node holding its target in markdown. So both are projections of one relation. It reads `graph_edges` naming the issue wait `blocked_by`, as a process of the release before reads it, and the plan wait `needs`. It reads `GET /api/v1/references?from=<issue ref>` answering the issue wait as `needs`. It reads that same edge through `?kind=needs` and through `?kind=blocked_by`, because the kind filter takes both spellings. It retracts the issue dependency through the issue route and, on its next read with no pass run, finds the `issue_links` row gone. It writes one dependency through `dispatch issue-update --blocked-by`, which sends `needs` and `blocked_by` with the same targets, and reads the one `needs` tuple it appended. It also reads one `issue_links` row the earlier release wrote, captured as this document's preamble states, answering as a `needs` tuple after the upgrade, once the backfill the preamble states has run.

It reads the reach and the refusals each writer keeps. It creates a second project, `CORE2`, through `POST /api/v1/projects`, with `default_assignee` set to `alice`. It writes a `needs` from an issue of `CORE` to an issue of `CORE2` through the agent bearer, which names no project, and the write is taken. The Go test `TestNeedsCrossesAProjectAndRefusesAProjectScopedCaller` in `internal/dispatch/api` holds `main`'s cross-project rule since cybermonklabs/legion#5833: with a credential that names one project, a wait on a public issue of another project reads `200` on `PATCH` (`needs` and `blocked_by`) and `201` on create (`needs`); a wait on an issue of a private project the credential does not name is refused as a nonexistent key (`400 NEEDS_INPUT` for `needs`, `400 BLOCKED_BY_INPUT` for `blocked_by`), while a credential that names that private project reads `200`. A target set above `contracts.MaxIssueBlockers` is refused `400 NEEDS_INPUT` when the request names `needs`, and `400 BLOCKED_BY_INPUT` when it names `blocked_by`. A request that names `needs` and `blocked_by` with the same targets appends one `needs` tuple for each target, and one whose two lists differ is refused with status 400, and the error names both. An issue that would wait on itself through the relation and the parent chain is refused `409 DEPENDENCY_CYCLE`. A plan node pointing at a plan node of an issue outside its own tree is refused, which `refs.IssueAncestors` decides. The cross-issue `needs` from the child's plan node to the parent's is taken, which `pmdoc.CheckBlockPointers` refuses today for `scope: "document"`. It also writes, in a second document of the child issue, a plan task whose `needs` names a task of the child's own plan. `e2e/acceptance/verification.sh` asserts today that this cross-document `needs` within one issue is refused, because `pmdoc.CheckBlockPointers` holds `needs` to its own document. This child takes it, because both ends are plan nodes of one issue, and the driver reads its `needs` tuple. This work replaces that assertion of `verification.sh` with the refusal of a `needs` that names a plan task of an issue outside the writer's tree.

The Go test `TestTheDaemonReadsNeedsAndFallsBackToBlockedBy` in `packages/daemon/internal/dispatch` decodes an issue answer that holds `needs` and one that holds `blocked_by` alone, and finds the same targets in both. Last it reads the sizes. Three of the four plan nodes carry one, written `45m`, `2h` and `1h30m`. The driver reads them back as 45, 120 and 90 minutes through the node's attributes, and as written (`45m`, `2h` and `1h30m`) through `dispatch read --ref`, keeping each block's text as its author wrote it (R18). It reads no size at all on the fourth, absent rather than present and empty. Each of `2d`, `1.5h`, `0m`, `-1h` and `10001m` is refused `400 INVALID_MARKDOWN`, the shape `verification.sh` already asserts for a `when` the schema does not know. `10000m` is taken.
:::

:::check{#c-view-arms serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-issue-relations dispatch://TREE-1/spec#b-r-no-regression" surface="cli" run="cd packages/dispatch &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; DATABASE_URL=$INFRA_1253_UPGRADE_DATABASE_URL DISPATCH_TOKEN=e2e-token PROJECT=CORE PRE_1149_SHA=${PRE_1149_SHA:-62110c253b58ea2c852b60b85a7cd371f4951eac} bash e2e/acceptance/view-arms-rollback.sh 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/view-arms-rollback.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^PASS: view-arms-rollback.sh complete ' $TMPDIR/view-arms-rollback.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q '^SKIP' $TMPDIR/view-arms-rollback.log &amp;&amp; cd ../envoy &amp;&amp; go test ./... -run '^TestGraphEdgesKeepsEveryRelationAcrossARollback$' -count=1 -v 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/TestGraphEdgesKeepsEveryRelationAcrossARollback.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestGraphEdgesKeepsEveryRelationAcrossARollback ' $TMPDIR/TestGraphEdgesKeepsEveryRelationAcrossARollback.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q -- '--- SKIP' $TMPDIR/TestGraphEdgesKeepsEveryRelationAcrossARollback.log" when="before_merge" negative_control="Four controls, run one at a time. The four arms dispatch://TREE-3 moved are gone, and so is the tuple arm's join for their kinds. The `child_of` and `blocked_by` arms, the three component arms and the `artifact attached_to issue` arm stand, each answering only the rows no store writer wrote: a row with no `node_kind`, and a marked row whose edge column the release before has since changed in place, so that the newest tuple of its kind does not name the column's value. The tuple arm answers their kinds only while the projection row that names the edge carries its node. The arm over `refs` stands too, and it answers a row from an artifact only while that artifact carries no node. It seeds, by SQL, a database as the release before this one leaves it: a stamped issue link, a link that release wrote with no node, and a stamped link that release deleted with no retraction, and the same three for a parent, a component's parent and a component dependency. `TestGraphEdgesKeepsEveryRelationAcrossARollback` also moves a stamped parent and a stamped component's parent in place by SQL. Each SQL `update` sets the column to a new value and leaves the node column pair as it was. The release before moves a parent in place through the issue PATCH. No writer of the release before moves a component's parent in place, because the release before's importer deletes a source's components and inserts them again. So the component case stands for a later writer that updates that column in place. Each reads once, to its new value, through the old arm, and its old value nowhere, through `graph_edges`, `refs.BacklinkCounts` and the references read. After this child's backfill, which appends the tuple that names the new value, each reads once through the tuple arm and the old arm answers neither. It reads `graph_edges`, `refs.BacklinkCounts` and the outbound references read `GET /api/v1/references?from=<issue ref>`, which `Links:` of `dispatch read --issue` renders, and finds each standing relation once, and each deleted one nowhere. In `graph_edges` each stands under the name a process of the release before reads, so an issue link is `blocked_by` in the old arm and in the tuple arm. The references read answers that link as `needs`. It seeds an issue link, a parent, a component's parent, a component dependency, an artifact on an issue and a document's citation of another issue, each written before this child, with no node. Before this child's backfill each is answered once, by its old arm. After it each is answered once, by the tuple arm, dated with its row's own `created_at`, and the old arms answer none of them. It then runs this child's deletion of the four old arms over a database where a block row is deleted by SQL, as a build of the release before dispatch://TREE-3 deletes it, and its tuple stands: the four arms stay, the server starts and serves, and its log names the difference. It reads one answer holding every issue and every plan node of that tree. Each node stands once, after every node it needs, with its size beside it.

It reads `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/tree?view=plan` and finds the same lists on each task's node. Else the test fails, printing `the ordered read of <key> answers <task> with skills <skills> and docs <docs>, want <skills> and <docs>`, `the ordered read of <key> answers no empty list of <attribute> for <task>, which holds none`, `the plan view of <key> answers <task> with <attribute> <value>, want <value>`, or `the upload of the plan of <key> answered <status>: <body>`.

It proves the two halves. An issue is placed as a start and a done, as `waitNode` splits it. A parent issue holding a child is no cycle, and the parent's done sits after every child's done. A plan node's start sits after its issue's start, and its issue's done sits after that plan node. A sibling issue waiting on another sibling keeps its order.

The test then seeds cycles. Two plan nodes of one issue need each other. A longer cycle of three crosses two issues of one tree, which the widened reach now lets a writer make. A third runs from an issue to a plan node of another issue and back. The read reports each cycle with the nodes in it and returns no order that hides one. A node that needs itself is a cycle of one and is reported. Every node outside a cycle keeps its position, so one bad plan does not blank the answer. A plan with no cycle reports none, including a diamond where two nodes need a third and a fourth needs both, so the detector does not cry wolf. A parent's plan node that needs its child issue comes back after every plan node of that child and after the child's done half. A child's plan node that needs that same parent plan node makes a cycle, which the read reports with the parent plan node, the child's done half and the child's plan node in it. A plan node that needs an issue outside its own issue's tree is refused at the write. The control: let the read take the child's start half for a `needs` on an issue, and the parent's plan node comes back before the child's plan nodes, which the test names. `TestTheOrderedReadKeepsEachChainOfStepsTogether` in `internal/dispatch/refs`, a Go test the implementer adds, writes plan tasks a, b and c in that document order, where c needs a. It reads the ordered read answer b, a, c. It then writes a parent issue with two tasks and a child issue with two, where the parent's first task needs the child's second, and reads each need just before the first node that needs it, with the parent's own tasks first in their document's order and the child's after in theirs.

It holds a spec of two requirement blocks and a Verification document of two check blocks that serve them. It holds a plan of one plan node that serves one of those requirements. The driver records each block's id, text and `serves` targets, and stops that server. It boots this branch's server over the same database and waits for the backfill as this document's preamble states.

With every live process and the newest announcement at the conversion's own stamped commit, the driver runs `envoy-dispatch convert-issues --project CORE`. So the driver converts rows the earlier release stored.

The driver reads `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/tree` once. The answer reads `converted: true`. It holds each requirement, each check and the plan node as one node. Each node carries its id, its supertag, its parent and its rank. Each node's parent is the issue's node or another node of the answer. Each parent stands before its children, and siblings stand in increasing rank, compared byte for byte. The driver refuses to run, printing a FAIL line, where `select 'a' < 'B'` is false, since such a database cannot tell byte order from its own collation.

The same answer holds every `serves` tuple among those nodes. The driver walks the `serves` tuples from each requirement. It reaches each check whose `serves` names that requirement, and the plan node whose `serves` names it. The set it reaches equals the set the earlier release wrote. A second read answers the same nodes in the same order.

The driver reads `?view=spec` from the same route. That answer holds the two requirement nodes, each marked as the query's, in the order the first read gave them. Each carries its parent's id, supertag and first line. The driver reads the issue read, `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}`, and finds the spec query node. That node states the node types it takes, which are the types R14 gives the spec query. It states the subtree it takes them from, which starts at the issue's tree node.

The driver changes one word of a check and one word of the plan node in one write of the issue's room. The two nodes stood in the Verification document and in the plan before the conversion. The driver reads the tree and finds both new words.

`e2e/acceptance/issue-tree-spec-query.sh` is this check's own driver and is new here.

The run proves this test executed. It greps the run's own log for this test's `--- PASS:` line and fails on any `--- SKIP` line, which `storetest.Open` writes when `DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL` is unset.

`TestOnlyAPersonOrAnArchitectWritesASpecNode` in `internal/dispatch/api` already exists in `api/node_writer_test.go`. This child extends it to both routes in R7. It can pass only on a head that holds both this child's routes and the writer check of cybermonklabs/legion#4725. So it runs at #4180's head once #4180 has merged #4725, which merges first (R28).

The test builds its issue as `TestSpecWriteRefusesAWorkerOnEveryRoute` in `api/spec_writer_test.go` of #4725 builds one. The issue carries the label `legion`, and a role-holder publication marked its project (`project_role_holder_marks`). An architect session holds the architect role on the issue, and a worker session holds another role on it. The issue is converted. It holds a criterion a person wrote, two requirements under that criterion, a constraint, and two checks that serve the requirements.

As the worker session, the test sends five writes. First, `overtaken` on a requirement through `POST /api/v1/issues/{key}/nodes/{id}/state`. Second, `constrained_by` out of a requirement to the constraint through `POST /api/v1/issues/{key}/nodes/{id}/pointers`. Third, a new criterion through an edit of the issue's `tree` artifact, `POST /api/v1/artifacts/{id}/edits`. Fourth, a check moved under the other requirement through `PATCH /api/v1/issues/{key}/nodes/{id}`, with the `If-Match` of the check's `placement_seq`. Fifth, a `DELETE /api/v1/issues/{key}/nodes/{id}` of a check a person wrote that holds no result, with the `If-Match` of its `placement_seq` and the `expected_count` its dry run answers. R28's writer check comes before R32's on both routes, so the fourth and the fifth answer R28's code. Each write answers `403 DOCUMENT_WRITER_NOT_ARCHITECT`. Before and after each write, the test counts the `graph_tuples` rows, the `artifact_versions` rows and the events of the issue, and each count stays the same. Else it prints `<route> let worker <session> write <node>` with the counts.

The architect's session then sends the first four kinds of write, each on a node of its own, and each write is accepted. The architect moves a person-written check that contains no protected decision. A person repeats those writes with a token holding the person scope. Each write is accepted. R28 and R32 both use the credential's person scope. Else the test prints `<route> refused <writer>` with the answer.

Last, the test reads the agreed state. A person approves version 1 of the spec query and version 1 of the Verification query, each after the pass that states that version (R15). A person then moves a requirement under another criterion through `PATCH /api/v1/issues/{key}/nodes/{id}`. A person also changes the `negative_control` of a check through the edit route, which weakens that check. The test reads `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/tree?view=spec&v=1` and `?view=verification&v=1`. For each query, the nodes of that answer are the nodes of the record of R14 at the store revision version 1 read (`docs.ReadQueryRecord`), in the record's order. Else the test prints `the <query> answer at version 1 differs from its record at node <address>`. That record digests to the `content_sha256` of the approval of version 1, and the record of the current answer does not. Else the test prints `the agreed <query> state at version 1 digests to <digest>, the approval pins <pin>`.
:::

First, reject a same-spec ancestor move just because it has a protected decision below it. The test prints `agent PATCH of &lt;section&gt; answered 409, want 200`. Eighth, count only the token minted in the browser with no scopes named as a person's. The test prints the refused write of each other token that holds the person scope, and fails. Ninth, let a `retype` that changes the decision's words through. The test prints `agent retype of &lt;decision&gt; answered 200, want 409 ANSWERED_ASK_KEPT` with the words before and after. The second session's `proposed` then answers `403 STATE_NOT_PERMITTED`, and the test prints `agent state proposed of &lt;ask&gt; answered 403 STATE_NOT_PERMITTED, want 409 ANSWERED_ASK_KEPT` and fails. Twelfth, remove R32's refusal on `ask/&lt;uuid&gt;` alone. The asking session's `overtaken` is then taken, and the test prints `agent state overtaken of &lt;ask&gt; answered 200, want 409 ANSWERED_ASK_KEPT` and fails. Thirteenth, give the mint route's row `person` alone in place of `person` and `approve` (`api/routes_table.go`). The broker token's mint is then taken, and the test prints `broker token mint answered &lt;status&gt;, want 403 OAUTH_SCOPE_REQUIRED` and fails. Fourteenth, leave the Keep pass out of `backfillPasses` in `graphcensus/census.go`. E1 reads `waiting_review` true after the backfill, and the test prints `the Keep of &lt;E1&gt; reads waiting_review true after the backfill, stored &lt;sum&gt;, want &lt;sum&gt;` and fails. Fifteenth, let the pass rewrite each Keep on a decision that carries `shaped`, whatever its sum. The test prints `the pass rewrote the Keep of &lt;E2&gt;, which did not match: &lt;sum&gt; to &lt;sum&gt;` and fails. Sixteenth, leave `shaped` out in `ownWords` alone and keep it in `refs.DecisionWords`, which the pass sums through. The pass writes E1's old sum again, the decisions read answers another, and the test prints E1, both sums and `waiting_review` true, and fails.
