The implementer adds `TestOnlyAPersonChangesAPersonsDecision` in `internal/dispatch/api`. Use an issue that Legion does not run so R28 does not mask R32. Alice answers an ask and makes a decision whose `decided_by` names her. Keep a separate agent-written decision as Alice. Include person-written prose. Use a separate fixture for each destructive write. Obtain the shared token and the four kinds of token that hold the person scope (R32) through the test server's authentication paths. The first is a token Alice mints in the browser with no scopes named, which takes her own scopes (`tokenScopes` and `callerScopes` in `api/agent_tokens.go`). The second is a token minted through `POST /api/v1/me/agent-tokens` with `person` among its scopes. Test it twice: minted that way, and minted without `person` and then changed to hold it through `PATCH /api/v1/me/agent-tokens/{id}`. The third is a broker token scoped to Alice (`api/broker_token.go`). The fourth is a token that a personal token of Alice's mints with no scopes named, where that personal token holds `person` and `approve`. The new token takes those two scopes, the scopes of the credential that minted it (`tokenScopes` and `callerScopes` in `api/agent_tokens.go`). No broker token mints a token. The broker token's `POST /api/v1/me/agent-tokens` answers `403 OAUTH_SCOPE_REQUIRED` naming `approve` and mints nothing, because the mint needs `person` and `approve` (`api/routes_table.go`) and no broker token holds `approve` (`TestNoBrokerTokenGetsApprove` in `api/broker_token_approve_test.go`).

On node `PATCH`, the shared token can move a section or a child issue's node that contains a person's decision. Read the decision's document and words before and after. The decision stays in its spec, because the `PATCH` keeps every node in its own document (R7). The same token cannot move the decision's own node: that `PATCH` answers `409 ANSWERED_ASK_KEPT`. The ask itself, `ask/<uuid>`, is no move target, because R7 answers it `400 NODE_NOT_MOVABLE`. On `DELETE`, the shared token cannot take a person's `decision` node, including one inside a removed subtree. An answered ask's block is lifted out and stays in its document, as `c-node-delete` checks.

On the state route, write each value on Alice's decision with the shared token. `overtaken` answers `409 ANSWERED_ASK_KEPT`. To try `live`, Alice first marks her decision `overtaken` with her browser cookie. The shared token's `live` then answers `409 ANSWERED_ASK_KEPT`, so an agent cannot undo her `overtaken`. The other three values keep today's refusals, which come before R32's. `proposed` answers `403 STATE_NOT_PERMITTED` (`takesTheSettleRule` and `maySettle` in `api/node_state.go`). `settled` and `gone` answer `409 NODE_STATE_NOT_WRITABLE` (`stateRefusal` in the same file). Each refused write leaves the state unchanged. With each token that holds the person scope, `overtaken` and then `live` on the decision are each taken.

On the state route, name as `{id}` the own node, `ask/<uuid>`, of an ask that an agent session asked and Alice answered. This case runs on a server that `newBrokerTokenRig` in `api/broker_token_test.go` starts, on an issue of the project that its named tokens may write. The asker and a second session are each a session that the broker verified, each with a named token of its own, as `liveNamedToken` answers one. Each session is owned by a person other than Alice, and the two owners are two persons. Neither token holds the person scope, and `graphstore.SameAuthor` reads the two sessions as two authors, because each proves its owner (`provedAuthor` in `graphstore/author.go`). So the asker is the proved author of the ask's node. Alice's answer stands on that node as its `answer_state` tuple (`askNodeStateOf` in `api/ask_rows.go`), apart from the node's own `state`. The asker writes `proposed`, `overtaken` and `live` on that node, and each write answers `409 ANSWERED_ASK_KEPT`. Without R32's refusal, the settle's author rule (`takesTheSettleRule` and `maySettle` in `api/node_state.go`) would let the asker's `proposed` through, and no rule would refuse its `overtaken` or its `live`. The second session's `proposed` answers `409 ANSWERED_ASK_KEPT` and not `403 STATE_NOT_PERMITTED`, the author rule's refusal, so R32's refusal comes first. Its `overtaken` and its `live` answer `409 ANSWERED_ASK_KEPT` too. Each refused write leaves the ask's state, its answer and its events unchanged.

On the edit and upload paths, attempt a word change, retype, removal and transfer out of the document for each protected block. Include issue edits by artifact id and issue slug, project edits by artifact id and project slug, and both issue and project uploads. Inside either document, reordering around a decision and changing its parent without moving it out are allowed. So a text edit that moves Alice's decision inside its spec is taken, while the shared token's `PATCH` of that decision answers `409 ANSWERED_ASK_KEPT`. A `retype` that changes the decision's words answers `409 ANSWERED_ASK_KEPT`. Use the real write paths and keep the block's identity when the change does not remove it from the document.

For each protected write, the shared token receives `409 ANSWERED_ASK_KEPT`. The refusal names a visible node and quotes its words. For an unseen node it names no node. The room text, tuples, versions, state and events do not change. Repeat otherwise valid writes on all five paths with each person-scoped token. R32 does not refuse them. A Keep on a session's decision does not make it person-decided. The shared token can still change such a decision or replace a person's document that has no protected decision. R28 and the lens rule remain separate.

As the shared-token agent, insert a reading into Alice's decision through the edit route. Then write the decision's `shaped` attribute through the edit route's `retype` op, and keep its words. Both writes are taken. The tree shows the reading and the `shaped` tuple, and the decision's words and own placement are unchanged. The protection and scope rules follow the owner's answer in dispatch://TREE-2/comment/6fe69ea5-1afc-437a-9247-c0af3952228a, as recorded in dispatch://TREE-2/comment/dd478237-1093-48ff-80a4-432128b9a051.

Name as `{id}` the `:::ask` block node of Alice's answered ask: the node of the block, not `ask/<uuid>`. The shared token's `PATCH` and its `DELETE` of that node each answer `409 ANSWERED_ASK_KEPT`. Its writes of `overtaken`, `live`, `proposed` and `gone` on that node through the state route each answer `409 ASK_HOLDS_STATE`, which `askHoldsState` in `api/node_state.go` answers before every other rule of that route. Alice's `DELETE` of the node answers `400 NODE_NOT_DELETABLE`, which R7 answers after R32's refusal. None of these writes stores anything.

The `shaped` write keeps the decision's sum (R8, R32). Read Alice's decision in `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/decisions` before and after the `retype`: its `text_sha256` is the same. Alice keeps the session's decision through `POST /api/v1/artifacts/{id}/blocks/{block_id}/keep` with the `text_sha256` that read answers. The shared-token agent then writes that decision's `shaped` attribute through `retype`. The decision's `text_sha256` is unchanged, `kept` still names Alice, and `waiting_review` is false, so the Keep still holds. This needs the change of R8 and R32. At this branch's head `ownWords` in `decisionread/decisions.go` keeps `shaped` in the words that `refs.DecisionWords` (`refs/decision_nodes.go`) renders. This child leaves `shaped` out in `refs.DecisionWords` itself, the one function every sum goes through, so `ownWords` and the decisions step's conversion, which writes a converted Keep's `kept_text_sum` (`docs/decision_restore.go`), sum the same words.

A Keep made before this change on a decision that carries `shaped` holds a sum over the words with `shaped`. A pass of the boot's backfill recomputes that sum where it equals the sum of the words with `shaped` (R32, new). Two cases hold that pass. An agent session writes two decisions, E1 and E2, and the shared-token agent writes the `shaped` attribute of each through `retype`. Alice keeps both. Alice then changes E2's words through the edit route, so E2's Keep no longer matches.

By SQL, in the shape the release before this one stores, the test then writes each Keep's sum as that release summed it, over the words with `shaped`: over E1's current words, and over E2's words before Alice's change. It writes the sum into `decision_keeps.text_sha256` and appends it as the node's `kept_text_sum` value. It computes each sum by rendering the decision with its `shaped` attribute, without the readings it closes with, through `pmdoc.Render`, as `refs.DecisionWords` rendered it before this change. The store census, as `envoy-dispatch census --store` runs it, then counts 1 for the census kind `keep_shaped_sum`, which the implementer adds: E1's Keep, which the pass would rewrite.

The test runs `graphcensus.Backfill`. After it, E1's `decision_keeps.text_sha256` and its current `kept_text_sum` equal the `text_sha256` that `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/decisions` answers for E1, `kept` names Alice and `waiting_review` is false: a Keep that matched before still matches. E2's stored sums are the ones the test wrote, and `waiting_review` is true: a Keep that did not match keeps its sum. The census kind `keep_shaped_sum` reads 0. Else the test prints `the Keep of <E1> reads waiting_review true after the backfill, stored <sum>, want <sum>`, `the pass rewrote the Keep of <E2>, which did not match: <sum> to <sum>`, or `census kind keep_shaped_sum reads <n>, want <m>`. `c-keep-sum-pass` holds the same pass at the boot of a process.
:::

:::check{#c-keep-sum-pass serves="dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-person-node-kept dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-queries" surface="cli" run="cd packages/envoy &amp;&amp; set -o pipefail &amp;&amp; DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL=$LEGION_TEST_PG_DSN go test ./cmd/dispatch/ -run '^TestTheBootBackfillRecomputesTheKeepSumsOfShapedDecisions$' -count=1 -v 2&gt;&amp;1 | tee $TMPDIR/keep-sum-pass.log &amp;&amp; grep -q '^--- PASS: TestTheBootBackfillRecomputesTheKeepSumsOfShapedDecisions ' $TMPDIR/keep-sum-pass.log &amp;&amp; ! grep -q -- '--- SKIP' $TMPDIR/keep-sum-pass.log &amp;&amp; gh pr view legion/TREE-2 --repo cybermonklabs/legion --json body --jq .body &gt; $TMPDIR/pr-body-keep.md &amp;&amp; { grep -E '^KEEP_SHAPED_SUM: ([0-9]+ [^ ].*|owed)$' $TMPDIR/pr-body-keep.md || { echo 'c-keep-sum-pass: the pull request body holds no KEEP_SHAPED_SUM line with a count or owed'; false; }; } | tee $TMPDIR/keep-shaped-sum-line.log &amp;&amp; { [ &#x22;$(grep -c -E '^KEEP_SHAPED_SUM: ' $TMPDIR/pr-body-keep.md)&#x22; -eq 1 ] || { echo 'c-keep-sum-pass: the pull request body holds more than one KEEP_SHAPED_SUM line'; false; }; }" when="before_merge" negative_control="Six controls, run one at a time, each on a copy as this document's preamble states. First, leave the Keep pass out of `backfillPasses` in `graphcensus/census.go`. The second boot logs no line of the pass, and the test prints `the boot backfill logged no line of the Keep pass` and fails. Second, let the pass rewrite each Keep on a decision that carries `shaped`, whatever its sum. The test prints `the Keep pass rewrote the Keep of &lt;D2&gt;, which did not match: &lt;sum&gt; to &lt;sum&gt;` and fails. Third, let the pass write `decision_keeps.text_sha256` alone and append no `kept_text_sum` value. The test prints `the kept_text_sum of &lt;D1&gt; reads &lt;sum&gt; after the boot backfill, want &lt;sum&gt;` and fails. Fourth, let the census kind `keep_shaped_sum` count each Keep on a decision that carries `shaped`. Before the second boot it reads 2, and the test prints `census kind keep_shaped_sum reads 2, want 1` and fails. Fifth, let the pass compare a Keep's stored sum with the sum of the words without `shaped`. The second boot then rewrites nothing, and the test prints `the Keep pass rewrote 0 Keeps, want 1` and fails. Sixth, run the last two steps over a copy of the pull request body with its `KEEP_SHAPED_SUM:` line deleted. The run prints `c-keep-sum-pass: the pull request body holds no KEEP_SHAPED_SUM line with a count or owed` and exits non-zero."}
The run proves that the test executed. It greps the run's own log for the test's `--- PASS:` line and fails on any `--- SKIP` line, which `storetest.Open` writes when `DISPATCH_TEST_DATABASE_URL` is unset. `TestTheBootBackfillRecomputesTheKeepSumsOfShapedDecisions` is new, and the implementer adds it in `packages/envoy/cmd/dispatch`. It proves that the pass of R32 that recomputes a Keep's stored sum runs in the boot's backfill (`graphcensus.Backfill`, in the order that `backfillPasses` in `graphcensus/census.go` gives), logs its outcome, and leaves its census kind at 0. The pass is Go and no SQL migration, because only Go renders a decision's words.

The test starts a process of this build with `startDispatchProcessWith` and waits for it with `waitHealthy`, as `c-boot-backfill` does. Through that process's routes, as alice, it creates an issue whose spec holds two `decision` blocks, D1 and D2, and writes the `shaped` attribute of each through the edit route's `retype`. Alice keeps both through `POST /api/v1/artifacts/{id}/blocks/{block_id}/keep`. She then changes D2's words through the edit route, so D2's Keep no longer matches. The test stops the process.

By SQL, in the shape the release before this one stores, the test then writes each Keep's sum as that release summed it, over the words with `shaped`: over D1's current words, and over D2's words before alice's change. It writes the sum into `decision_keeps.text_sha256` and appends it as the node's `kept_text_sum` value. It computes each sum by rendering the decision with its `shaped` attribute, without the readings it closes with, through `pmdoc.Render`, as `refs.DecisionWords` rendered it before this change. The store census of this build (`envoy-dispatch census --store`) then counts 1 for the census kind `keep_shaped_sum`, which the implementer adds: D1's Keep, which the pass would rewrite.

The test starts a second process of this build over the same database. It waits for the `dispatch: boot backfill done` line for at most 300 s, polling every 2 s. The process output holds the Keep pass's line, which names the count 1 of Keeps it rewrote. The implementer adds that line: at this branch's head the boot runs the passes with their output sent to `io.Discard` (`startBootBackfill` in `cmd/dispatch/main.go`), and it logs only its done line and its skipped line. Then D1's `decision_keeps.text_sha256` and its current `kept_text_sum` equal the `text_sha256` that `GET /api/v1/issues/{key}/decisions` answers for D1, `kept` names alice and `waiting_review` is false. D2's stored sums are the ones the test wrote, and `waiting_review` is true. The census kind `keep_shaped_sum` reads 0.

The test then starts a third process over the same database and waits for its done line in the same way. Its Keep pass line names the count 0, and neither Keep's stored sums change. Else the test prints `the boot backfill logged no line of the Keep pass`, `the Keep pass rewrote <n> Keeps, want <m>`, `the Keep of <D1> reads waiting_review true after the boot backfill, stored <sum>, want <sum>`, `the kept_text_sum of <D1> reads <sum> after the boot backfill, want <sum>`, `the Keep pass rewrote the Keep of <D2>, which did not match: <sum> to <sum>`, or `census kind keep_shaped_sum reads <n>, want <m>`.

One reading of this pass stays owed: the count that the census kind `keep_shaped_sum` reads on a copy of production's `decision_keeps`. No pod of this tree reads production's database (R32, dispatch://TREE-2/spec#b-r-person-node-kept), so no role runs that reading in CI or in the pod. The pull request body carries it as one line, `KEEP_SHAPED_SUM: <count> <source>`, where the source names the copy and the time of the reading, or as `KEEP_SHAPED_SUM: owed` until the reading is made. The run's last steps read the body once with `gh pr view`, as `c-migration-size` reads it, and require exactly one such line, which they print. So the check passes while the reading stays owed, and fails where the body holds neither form of the line.
:::
